Scenario policy-driven comms state machine (`Nominal` / `Degraded` / `Denied`), tactical datalink track-sharing lag/merger state (cross-ref doc 15), and link degradation metadata (`delayMs`, `dropRate`, `trackAgeMaxSec`, `Jamming` cause). `CommsTimelineSimulator`, `CommsState`, and replay tests step scenario-wide transitions, while datalink track merger, per-link `dropRate`/`delayMs`/`trackAgeMaxSec`, and jamming cause remain open in Backlog/Not started.

- [ ] [COM-01] Tactical datalink track-sharing lag and merger state (doc 15) propagate and merge contacts deterministically under degraded comms.
- [ ] [COM-01] Link-level degradation parameters (`dropRate: 0.05`, `delayMs: 800`, `trackAgeMaxSec: 120`) and jamming-cause attribution (`cause: { type: Jamming, sourceUnitId }`) are modeled and logged deterministically.

Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/19-Cyber-And-Comms.md` (lines 55-56). Track staleness acceleration and tactical datalink lag/partial-picture gating under comms degradation. Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/19-Cyber-And-Comms.md` (lines 108-112). C2 comms display projection (`CommsStateProjection`, `commsDisplay` ghost offsets, top-bar status, message log `COMMS` entries, and contact list stale/datalink vs organic indicator). Open in Backlog/Not started.

pages.content:
**Linear:** [DRG-880](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-880/loop-01-loop-02-loop-03-loop-05-phase-1-scenario-selection-and-phase-2) (Backlog)

**Req IDs:** LOOP-01, LOOP-02, LOOP-03, LOOP-05
**Lifecycle:** Active

### LOOP-01 — Phase 1: Scenario Selection and Force Composition
Allow the player or agent to select theater, time period, and force packages (manned platforms, loyal wingmen, drone swarms, submarines, support assets) and assign initial agent personalities and autonomy levels (Phase 1 full C2 surface remains partial).
- [ ] Player can select a scenario and inspect/configure force packages before entering Phase 2.
- [ ] Initial agent personalities and autonomy tiers can be bound to units or task forces at setup.

### LOOP-02 — Phase 2: RTwP Pre-Mission Planning with Explicit Begin Execution
Enter Phase 2 with the simulation clock paused by default (CMO-style RTwP) for route, sensor, EW, ROE, and agent assignment planning, transitioning to Phase 3 only via an explicit Begin Execution action (headless gate shipped; C2 UX polish ongoing).
- [ ] DelegationOrchestrator and SimulationSession remain in Planning phase (ticks and orders blocked) until BeginExecution() is explicitly invoked.
- [ ] Player can plan routes, ROE, EMCON, and agent assignments without time pressure, or optionally unpause if scenario timing requires.
- [ ] C2 TopBar Begin Execution UX polish completes per implementation-tracker row 02.

### LOOP-03 — Phase 3: Variable Time Compression During Execution
Support variable time compression during Phase 3 execution across interactive tiers (1x-10x), accelerated oversight (30x-300x), and headless batch speeds (900x+) while dynamic combat events drive the simulation (also indexed in Functional Requirements summary table lines 53-59).
- [ ] Interactive execution supports step-free or tiered time compression from 1x up to 300x+ with safe stop/pause controls.
- [ ] Headless execution supports high-speed AvA progression without losing determinism.

### LOOP-05 — Scenario playerInfoModel and personalityEditPolicy Gates
Configure scenario playerInfoModel (fullTransparency/delegationFog/tieredByAutonomy) and personalityEditPolicy (anytime/planningOnly/tieredRebrief). LoopPolicyGate, ScenarioPolicyProfile, and PlayerInfoFilter are shipped, while TieredByAutonomy aliases DelegationFog (no delayed contacts), tieredRebrief sim-time cost is deferred, and CanEditPersonal
- [ ] ScenarioPolicyProfile and JSON loader parse playerInfoModel and personalityEditPolicy with defaults fullTransparency and anytime, and GetLiveOrderLogView filters live HUD visibility without altering DecisionLog.
- [ ] PlayerInfoFilter differentiates TieredByAutonomy (SemiAutonomous detail and delayed contact updates) from DelegationFog.
- [ ] LoopPolicyGate enforces sim-pause checks in CanEditPersonality and tieredRebrief sim-time cost policy fields in CanRebriefAgent.

### AGD-04 — Four Autonomy Levels with ROE/Policy Gate and Lethal Opt-In
Implement four autonomy levels (Manual, Assisted, SemiAutonomous, FullAutonomous) integrated with ROE/policy evaluation (AutonomyGate + RoePolicyAdapter), requiring explicit player opt-in per mission phase for full-autonomous lethal engagement.
- [ ] AutonomyLevel defines Manual, Assisted, SemiAutonomous, and FullAutonomous tiers gated by AutonomyGate and IRoeFilter.
- [ ] Full autonomous lethal engagement enforces explicit player opt-in per mission phase (aligned with PendingApprovalQueue / HOL).

### AGD-07 — Realistic Variability via Deterministic Trait-Weighted Softmax DecisionPipeline
Exhibit human-like decision variability (mistakes, hesitation, personality styles). DecisionPipeline softmax (Decisiveness), SeededRng, SlowerReactions (ReactionDelay*5), and NarrowedFocus (Take(2)) are shipped, while ErrorRate, Aggression, and RiskTolerance candidate scoring remain unwired across DecisionPipeline and IPolicy implementations.
- [ ] DecisionPipeline selects among candidate actions deterministically using SeededRng given identical seed, traits, candidates, and attention state.
- [ ] ErrorRate (occasional mistakes), Aggression, and RiskTolerance drive candidate scoring and personality-specific decision styles in IPolicy/DecisionPipeline rather than remaining unwired.

### AGD-09 — Agent Delegation Responsiveness, Logging, and ROE Compliance NFRs
Ensure delegation remains responsive at thousands of entities without performance degradation, logs 100% of agent decisions for replay, and strictly respects ROE and player-defined constraints.
- [ ] All agent intents pass through AutonomyGate and IRoeFilter before execution.
- [ ] Delegation tick overhead remains bounded as entity count scales.

### AGD-11 — Agent Attention and Bandwidth Model with Graceful Degradation
Enforce per-agent attention budget (default 20, personality-modulated) scaling load by contacts/engagements/groups and degrading overloaded decisions. AttentionCalculator, SlowerReactions, and NarrowedFocus + IsOverloaded temperature scaling are shipped, while SimplerDecisions (>1.5x budget) is UI-only and overload integration tests are missing.
- [ ] AttentionCalculator computes load from contacts, engagements, and group members against personality-modulated budget (default 20), with SlowerReactions and NarrowedFocus active.
- [ ] SimplerDecisions drives simpler decision behavior in AgentController/DecisionPipeline (beyond UI projection) and overload degradation is covered by integration tests beyond AttentionCalculator.Evaluate.

### AGD-14 — Delegation Comms Degradation and Attention Coupling
Integrate CommsTimelineSimulator order delays and stale/datalink flags into agent observations and reduce effective attention budget under degraded comms (Phase 2), with EW Specialist preset balancing comms/EMCON tradeoffs.
- [ ] Agents observe stale/datalink status flags from comms timelines without breaking determinism.
- [ ] Degraded comms modulates effective attention budget per doc 19 integration.

Source: `Game-Requirements/drafts/24-Human-On-The-Loop-Authority.md` (lines 118-123). Ensure headless `ThreatAssessmentProjection` evaluates DLZ range, magazine state, mount status, and doctrine purely as an advisory recommendation without issuing fire orders. Headless subset exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] [HOL-06] Draft (pending owner): `WeaponRecommendation` MUST explicitly assert `IsWeaponsReleaseAuthorization=false`, `IsFireOrder=false`, and `IsAutomaticEngagement=false`.

- [ ] [HOL-06] Draft (pending owner): `ComputeFingerprint` MUST produce deterministic, replay-stable fingerprints across runs given identical inputs.

### HOL-07 — Resource Scarcity Ranking & Weapon Pairing

Source: `Game-Requirements/drafts/24-Human-On-The-Loop-Authority.md` (lines 125-130). Evaluate and rank candidate shooter/weapon pairings under scarcity constraints via `ResourceRankProjection` using five deterministic weights without authorizing weapons release. Headless subset exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] [HOL-07] Draft (pending owner): `ResourceRankSnapshot` MUST assert `IsWeaponsReleaseAuthorization=false`, `IsFireOrder=false`, and `IsAutomaticEngagement=false`.
- [ ] [HOL-07] Draft (pending owner): Candidates MUST be scored using weights: Expected Effect (0.35), Time-to-Effect (0.20), Round Availability (0.20), Commitment (0.15), Magazine Conservation (0.10).
- [ ] [HOL-07] Draft (pending owner): Candidates MUST categorize into `Preferred` (rank 1), `Alternative` (rank 2+), or `Excluded` with explicit reason codes.
- [ ] [HOL-07] Draft (pending owner): `ComputeFingerprint` MUST produce a deterministic fingerprint string.

### HOL-08 — Collateral Damage Estimation (CDE) & Advisory Withhold

Source: `Game-Requirements/drafts/24-Human-On-The-Loop-Authority.md` (lines 132-136). Project advisory collateral risk levels (`Low`, `Elevated`, `Withheld`), range classes, and policy denials via `CdeAssessProjection` without issuing fire authorizations. Headless subset exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] [HOL-08] Draft (pending owner): `CdeAssessSnapshot` MUST be strictly advisory and MUST NOT emit weapons release or fire authorizations.
- [ ] [HOL-08] Draft (pending owner): Risk MUST categorize as `Low`, `Elevated`, or `Withheld` (explicit collateral withhold or shooter-scoped policy denials).
- [ ] [HOL-08] Draft (pending owner): Projections MUST record explicit assumptions regarding engage preview, policy denial records, and CDE withhold status.

### LOG-10 — Scenario-level scalar sea-state gate for boat launch and stricter recovery

Linear: [DRG-840](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-840) | Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/16-Logistics-And-Magazines.md` (lines 104-113). Gate boat launch/recovery using scenario-level Douglas sea-state scalar (0-9) and per-craft `maxLaunchSeaState`/`maxRecoverySeaState`. `ScenarioSeaState`, `BoatOpsFsm`, `BoatOpsStateMap`, `BoatOpsProjection`, and `BoatOpsPanelHost` exist, while `ScenarioMetadataDto` and `ProjectAegis.Data/Catalog` lack `seaState`/`maxLaunchSeaState`/`maxRecoverySeaState` wiring (open in Backlog/Not started).

- [ ] [LOG-10] Launch is refused with `BOAT_NOT_READY:maxLaunchSeaState=` when sea state exceeds launch limit.
- [ ] [LOG-10] Recovery is refused with `BOAT_NOT_READY:maxRecoverySeaState=` when sea state exceeds stricter recovery limit, allowing craft launched in rising seas to be blocked from recovery.
- [ ] [LOG-10] `ScenarioMetadataDto` and `ProjectAegis.Data/Catalog` (`CatalogPlatformEntry`/`SqliteCatalogReader`) deserialize and wire `seaStateDouglas`, `maxLaunchSeaState`, and `maxRecoverySeaState` into `SimulationSession.BoatOps`.

### LOG-11 — Embarked load capacity, stranded craft persistence, VBSS, and SWARM-13 regen

Linear: [DRG-840](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-840) | Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/16-Logistics-And-Magazines.md` (lines 116-132). Enforce craft embarked capacity limits, transition abandoned waterborne craft to `Stranded` with order-log entry, track independent fuel (P2), VBSS boarding (P2), and `SWARM-13` host regeneration. Embarked overload refusal and `BoatOpsFsm.HostDepartWhileWaterborne->Stranded` are shipped, while stranded log rows, craft fuel, VBSS, and `SWARM-13` coupling remain open in Backlog/Not started.

- [ ] [LOG-11] Overloaded craft refuse launch with `EMBARKED_OVERLOAD` and waterborne craft whose host departs enter `Stranded` with a logged order-log row rather than silent destruction.
- [ ] [LOG-11] Stranded craft track independent endurance/fuel and support VBSS boarding outcomes and `SWARM-13` host-magazine regeneration.

### LOG-MCP — Logistics and magazine MCP tools

Linear: [DRG-840](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-840) | Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/16-Logistics-And-Magazines.md` (lines 207-216). Expose MCP/CLI verbs `logistics_get_readiness`, `logistics_project_sorties`, and `magazine_get` for inspecting unit readiness breakdowns, sorties-until-bingo projections, and magazine stores/counts. None of these verbs exist yet in `ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli` (open in Backlog/Not started).

- [ ] [LOG-MCP] `logistics_get_readiness`, `logistics_project_sorties`, and `magazine_get` are exposed via MissionEditor CLI/MCP with structured JSON output.

### LOG-AGENT-01 — Agent logistics compliance, Swarm Coordinator expendable inventory, LogisticsAbortReason takeoff block, and Cautious boat launch-margin refusal

Linear: [DRG-840](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-840) | Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/16-Logistics-And-Magazines.md` (lines 176-182). Enforce agent-logistics rules: agents respect bingo/WRA with Cautious early RTB; Swarm Coordinator tracks sub-swarm expendable inventory; P0 blocked takeoff emits `LogisticsAbortReason` enum; P1 boat launch refuses on sea-state recovery limit (`BOAT_NOT_READY`), with Cautious refusing at launch margin. Open in Backlog/Not started.

- [ ] [LOG-AGENT-01] Agents respect bingo and WRA limits, and Cautious agent personalities return strike assets earlier than Normal/Aggressive under identical fuel/ordnance constraints.
- [ ] [LOG-AGENT-01] Swarm Coordinator tracks expendable inventory across sub-swarms deterministically.
- [ ] [LOG-AGENT-01] Agent takeoff orders blocked by readiness emit canonical `LogisticsAbortReason` enum values (P0), and Cautious boat-launch agents refuse at the launch margin with `BOAT_NOT_READY` rather than waiting for the recovery margin.

### ROE-AGENT-01 — Agent policy compliance, Assisted blocked proposals, Swarm Coordinator WRA proposals, and EW Specialist

Enforce policy rules on agents (doc 04): block Policy Snapshot violations, prompt Assisted illegal actions with reasons, let Swarm Coordinator propose WRA bumps via PolicyUpdate, and let EwSpecialist prioritize legal jamming/deception. SwarmCoordinator and EwSpecialist presets exist in PersonalityCatalog, while PolicyUpdate proposal loop and EW prioritization remain open in Backlog/Not started.

- [ ] Agent controllers never issue orders that violate the active Policy Snapshot, and Assisted mode surfaces blocked agent proposals with abort reasons before confirmation.
- [ ] Swarm Coordinator can propose WRA adjustments via PolicyUpdate subject to player or event approval in Assisted+ autonomy.
- [ ] Electronic Warfare Specialist prioritizes legal jamming and deception actions strictly within active EMCON and ROE constraints.

### ROE-08 — Editor effective-policy resolution, contradiction validation, and What-If preview

Provide Mission Board doctrine/ROE/EMCON editing tabs with inheritance visualization, contradictory-policy validation (e.g., Strike mission with HoldFire), and P1 editor-only What-If rule relaxation preview. Validation tests and DoctrineInheritanceProjection exist, while Mission Board tabs, contradiction checks, and What-If preview remain open.

- [ ] Scenario validation emits deterministic findings for contradictory policies (such as Strike mission paired with HoldFire ROE) alongside DOCTRINE\_RESOLVED provenance.
- [ ] Mission Board exposes doctrine/ROE/EMCON inheritance tabs and an editor-test-only What-If preview disabled in ranked play.

### ROE-MCP — Policy MCP and agentic inspection/override tools

Expose MCP/CLI verbs policy\_get\_effective, policy\_set\_override, policy\_explain\_fire, and policy\_snapshot\_list for editor and authorized agent workflows. None of these verbs exist in ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli.

- [ ] policy\_get\_effective, policy\_set\_override, policy\_explain\_fire, and policy\_snapshot\_list are exposed via MissionEditor CLI/MCP with structured JSON output.
- [ ] policy\_set\_override respects policy legality and logs provenance without bypassing PolicySnapshot immutability.

### ROE-NFR — Doctrine/ROE determinism, O(1) evaluation cache, 5k-unit scale, and localization

Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/13-Doctrine-ROE-EMCON-WRA.md` (lines 128-136). Guarantee deterministic policy evaluation order, O(1) per-mount policy checks with per-tick caching, 5,000+ units with inherited policies without UI stall, and localized string tables for all FireAbortReason descriptions.

- [ ] [ROE-NFR] Headless runs with identical PolicySnapshot, world state, and seed produce identical policy denial sequences.
- [ ] [ROE-NFR] All FireAbortReason user-facing strings resolve via localization string tables and 5,000+ inherited units render without UI stall.

- [ ] ScenarioValidationEngine emits AIR_NOT_READY, FERRY_UNREACHABLE_FUEL, STRIKE_UNREACHABLE_FUEL, and configurable missing-tanker strike advisories.

BoatOpsFsm, BoatOpsStateMap, BoatOpsProjection, and SimulationSession.BoatOps ARE shipped, while host coupling, simultaneity limits, and LogisticsAbortReason enum rema

pages.content:

**Req IDs:** RPL-29, RPL-30, RPL-31, REC-RPL-29..31

### RPL-29 — H6 Deterministic save/resume preserving authoritative state and future fingerprints
Proposed H6 contract (pending feasibility/scope/ADR under DRG-328/329/330/348/349): uninterrupted and saved/resumed runs with identical build, scenario, catalog, policy, and inputs yield identical state and order-log fingerprints at future ticks, covering RNG, tick/sequence, pending commands, mission/delegation, engagements, and resources.
- [ ] Draft — pending H6 feasibility/ADR: differential uninterrupted vs saved/resumed runs across multiple interruption points (with queued orders/events and in-flight engagements) yield identical state and order-log hashes at

### RPL-30 — H6 Explicit save compatibility validation before session replacement
Proposed H6 contract: record schema/version, build identity, scenario identity/hash, catalog identity/hash, and policy identities/hashes in every save, and validate compatibility before replacing the active session (cross-build migration and multiplayer excluded).
- [ ] Draft — pending H6 feasibility/ADR: save files embed schema/build/scenario/catalog/policy identities/hashes, and loader rejects mismatched builds, scenarios, catalogs, or policies prior to replacing active session.

### RPL-31 — H6 Non-mutating load failure leaving active session unchanged
Proposed H6 contract: corrupt, incomplete, unsupported-version, or identity-mismatched saves return a stable diagnostic and leave the active session state, command queue, RNG, and order log completely unchanged, committing only after isolated validation.
- [ ] Draft — pending H6 feasibility/ADR: corrupt, truncated, unsupported-version, and mismatched load attempts against a live session return a stable diagnostic and verify exact before/after equality of session state, RNG, co

### REC-RPL-29..31 — Same-build deterministic save/resume reconciliation (H6)
Same-build/scenario/catalog/policy save/resume preserves authoritative state & future deterministic execution; corrupt/incompatible input fails without mutating active session (DRG-348 -> DRG-349); multiplayer separate later decision. Proposed draft.
- [ ] Draft (pending owner): Uninterrupted vs resumed differential runs with identical inputs & matching state/order-log fingerprints; negative loads leave active state/log unchanged.

### RPL-16 — Message log click-through to select unit and open explain panel

Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/17-Replay-AAR-And-Order-Log.md` (line 107). Clicking a message log row selects the associated unit and opens the policy/engage explain panel. `DecisionLogDeepLinkProjection`, `DecisionLogDeepLinkBinder`, and `MessageLogPanelHost` deep-link drawer exist in repo, while cross-panel unit selection and `EngageExplainPanelHost` integration remain held in Backlog pending owner-go under DRG-268/DRG-269 (`Status=Not started`, active Backlog rather than Blocked).

Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/20-Command-And-Control-UI.md` (line 78). Headless projection and host exist; full interactive sequence explain UX and Editor sign-off remain open.

### AGD-08 — Agent Communication, Rationale Explanation, and Order-Log Feedback

Linear: [DRG-195](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-195) | Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/04-Agent-Delegation.md` (lines 64-68). Report key agent decisions, status changes, and clear decision rationale to the player via order logs and optional agent voice/text log UI. Open in Backlog/Not started.

- [ ] [AGD-08] DecisionLog records AgentIntent, PolicyDenial, and rationale payloads for every agent decision.
- [ ] [AGD-08] Player-facing C2 message/voice log surfaces readable explanations for why an agent took or aborted an action.

### RPL-04 — Agent provenance recorded on AgentDecision order-log entries

Linear: [DRG-195](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-195) | Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/17-Replay-AAR-And-Order-Log.md` (lines 81-81). Attach `agentId`, `personality`/traits, `policySnapshotId`, and `autonomyLevel` onto `AgentDecision` / `DecisionRecord` order-log payloads. `AgentId`, `AutonomyLevel`, `ScoredIntents`, and `Rationale` are shipped on `AgentDecisionPayload`/`DecisionRecord`, while `PolicySnapshotId` and `Personality` remain open in Backlog/Not started (`DecisionLogDeepLinkProjection` currently sets `PolicySnapshotId=null` for `AgentDecision`).

- [ ] [RPL-04] Every AgentDecision entry in DecisionLog records AgentId, AutonomyLevel, ScoredIntents, and Rationale (shipped spine) plus Personality/traits context and PolicySnapshotId (currently omitted on AgentDecisionPayload/DecisionRecord and projected as null in DecisionLogDeepLinkProjection).
- [ ] [RPL-04] DecisionLogDeepLinkProjection surfaces non-null PolicySnapshotId and Personality provenance for AgentDecision entries matching the active PolicySnapshot at decision tick.

### INF-7.3 — Copilot Compliance With PolicyEvaluator and FireAbortReason Gates

Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/07-Agentic-Infrastructure.md` (lines 172-172). Remaining Copilot safety-gate integration open in Backlog/Not started.

Provide a selectable Military Tactical symbology profile (DRG-231) using documented NTDS naval display conventions and versioned mapping to NATO APP-6 / MIL-STD-2525 over observer-side projections without altering simulation truth. Headless scaffold exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

### RPL-MCP — Replay and AAR MCP tools (replay_list, replay_export, aar_generate)
Expose MCP/CLI tools replay_list, replay_export, replay_verify, aar_generate, and metrics_batch. metrics_batch (BalticBatchRunner) and replay_verify (ReplayGolden/skill) are met, while replay_list, replay_export, and product aar_generate remain open.

Repo: drgaciw/cmano-clone. Lane: CI config. Jev router ruled (a), confidence 0.75: port to GHA self-hosted as a draft, to stop paying for Buildkite.

Scope:

## Goal

Establish one repeatable delivery loop across requirements, planning, code, review, CI, and merge.

## Acceptance criteria

* A contributor can start from a Linear story linked to its Notion requirement.
* Each GitHub pull request carries the Linear story reference, Notion requirement reference, acceptance criteria, and test evidence.
* Graphite stack layers are atomic and map to implementation tasks or reviewable delivery increments.
* GitHub required checks govern mergeability; Graphite is configured to work with the repository’s CI and stacked branches.
* Completion updates Linear delivery status and preserves links to the merged GitHub pull request.

## Boundary

Notion is requirements/design source; Linear is delivery source; GitHub is code, review, and CI source; Graphite manages stacked branches and pull requests.

That SHA is not on origin (missing from the fetched clone and from GitHub). Uncommitted changes cannot be pinned. Candidate main SHAs were linked, not chosen: historical tip [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd) (2026-09-27, last main at the 2026-09-30 refresh) and current main [99a4d6e4](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/99a4d6e4be82dcf1bbce372caa47abef150f2b9b). Which SHA should replace the broken `4190fb1b` blob links is a Decision item; those file links were not retargeted.

The S10 retro’s audited SHA `7eed6791` is on main and was pinned to [the commit](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/7eed67910f340f870a8c00ed4b7b4fccd7655846).

The figures match; the exact median is recorded rather than overwritten to 0.9. Other windows diverge (UTC `merged:2026-11-02..2026-11-16` = 54; UTC through Nov 15 = 40; cutoff at `7eed6791` = 41 because #863’s `merged_at` is one second later) and were not used.

## Problem

With the SDK already on 11.0.100, this PR changes only the runtime and base libraries. Its exit is gate **G0** for the AI integration epic.

## Scope

* `net10.0` to `net11.0` in all 16 project files. Data, Sim, Delegation, and Delegation.UnityAdapter keep `netstandard2.1`.
* `LangVersion` stays 12.0 everywhere.
* `tools/cmano-db-crawler/import-qa-slice/ImportQaSlice.csproj` is **not** in `ProjectAegis.sln`. Build and run it explicitly.
* Package versions unchanged. `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite`, `System.Text.Json`, and `System.Net.Http.Json` stay at 10.0.14.
* Update the comment in `Directory.Build.props` that describes what `latest` means on the current SDK.
* Runtime Async stays off. It is opt-in through `runtime-async=on`.

No conditional-compilation edits are expected: the source uses only `NET10_0_OR_GREATER`, `NET8_0_OR_GREATER`, and `NETSTANDARD2_1`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Full gate script green. 0 failures, at least 1,638 passes, test count not below baseline.

## Problem

GitNexus builds process flows for only part of the codebase. Impact checks report `processes_affected` from those flows, so a count of 0 does not mean no runtime flow exists. Blast-radius reads can therefore under-report risk.

## Evidence

* Related but separate: [DRG-324] (missed overloaded static `Project(...)` calls) and [DRG-323] (MCP corruption).

After the `cmano-clone` GitNexus index was rebuilt at 2026-09-27 14:23 CT (main `7a097f93`), the running `user-gitnexus` MCP servers started returning corrupted results: empty or garbled symbol ids, NUL bytes in strings, UIDs that are not found, and unrelated symbols merged together.

---

## Overview

This draft describes the implemented headless engagement path and its presentation boundary; owner design review and product acceptance are pending. Scope covers launch permission, magazine consumption and deterministic Hit/Miss → Intercept → Kill assessment. It does not claim physical missile flight, a universal damage equation or completion of every combat-domain requirement.

Evidence identity: The 2026-09-30 review cited local checkout `4190fb1b49cd15775b6b995b7c245d73828cd7a2` with uncommitted changes. As of 2026-11-20 that SHA is not on origin (absent from a fetched clone and from GitHub), and uncommitted working-tree changes cannot be pinned. Published main SHAs: last main tip at the time of the review, [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd) (2026-09-27, 2:40 PM CDT, #681), already named here as a distinct remote reference; current main [99a4d6e4](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/99a4d6e4be82dcf1bbce372caa47abef150f2b9b) (2026-11-17, 7:16 PM CT). The source map below was not GitHub blob or commit links, so those paths were left as-is after confirming they exist at [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd). Refreshed against main 1902dc12 because 4190fb1b was never pushed (ruling: Decision, 2026-11-20). Source observations below are not an owner acceptance of either revision.

Source map: `src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Engage/MvpEngagementResolver.cs`, `CombatOutcomeResolver.cs`, `MagazineLedger.cs`, `SwarmOffensiveEffect.cs`, `WeaponEnvelope.cs`, `DlzEngageGate.cs` and `DlzEvaluator.cs` in the same Engage directory. Presentation sources are `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/CombatEvents/CombatEventLogProjection.cs`, `CombatEventProjection.cs` and `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Presentation/CombatMapPresentation.cs`.

## Player Fantasy

The commander decides whether to commit scarce weapons under ROE, fire-control, readiness and range constraints. A denied shot provides its actual refusal reason; an accepted shot consumes the real magazine ledger and yields a deterministic outcome suitable for replay and after-action review. Map effects communicate logged events without becoming combat authority.

## Detailed Rules

1. `MvpEngagementResolver.Resolve` checks killed shooter, killed target and context availability first. Zero unit identifiers skip their respective killed-registry check. The first failing gate returns its explicit abort result; later gates do not replace that reason.
2. Remaining prelaunch checks follow source order: speculative settings; optional policy evaluator; optional domain validator registry; air readiness; damage withdrawal; Bingo; Shotgun; spoofed track; radar EMCON; remote CEC/fire-control eligibility; usable fire-control; Winchester/magazine; combat-domain validation; hypersonic gate; inclusive weapon envelope; DLZ. Some validators are optional/configured, so do not describe every domain registry as active in every run.
3. Live rounds use tracked ledger state when present, including tracked zero; an unseeded mount falls back to context rounds for gate assessment. Launch still requires an actual seeded ledger entry with enough rounds in `TryConsumeSalvo`.
4. All abort paths in this resolver precede successful consumption. Failed `TryConsumeSalvo` leaves rounds unchanged. On success it consumes the complete normalized salvo, allocates the next engagement ID and resolves outcomes in the same invocation using the request's simulation tick.
5. Outcome order is `CombatOutcomeResolver.Apply` (Hit/Miss), then `ApplyInterceptOnHit`, then `ApplyKillOnHit`. Miss bypasses both later stages. Successful intercept replaces Hit with Intercept and therefore bypasses kill. Remaining Hit can become Kill. This path does not schedule a later physical flight/impact time.
6. For swarm shooters the resolver scales offensive base probability by living integrity. For a swarm target, final Hit/Kill can apply integrity damage through the injected authorized sink when target swarm metadata is present.
7. `CombatEventLogProjection` derives presentation phases from authoritative log rows, with sequence IDs as correlation IDs. It shows InFlight for a missile launch with no matching outcome yet; matching outcome produces TerminalOutcome. `CombatEventProjection` also projects InFlight when an assessed launched leg has no outcome row. These labels are visual lifecycle state, not evidence of simulated weapon kinematics. The current checkout did not contain a `BattleGraphicsPresentationBridge` declaration; no behavior is attributed to that unavailable source.

## Formulas

Implemented formulas, verified directly in source:

- Normalized salvo: `n = max(1, SalvoSize)`. Successful ledger consumption: `remaining' = remaining - n` only when the mount is tracked and `remaining >= n`; otherwise return false without mutation.
- Hit: `pHit = clamp(pkBase, 0, 1)`; `u0 = SeededRng.UnitFloat(seed, Combat, engagementId, simTick, 0)`; Hit iff `u0 < pHit`, otherwise Miss. Hit draw occurs only for a launched result.
- Intercept: only when incoming outcome is Hit and `clamp(pkIntercept,0,1) > 0`, draw salt 1 and replace Hit with Intercept iff `u1 < clamp(pkIntercept,0,1)`. Zero intercept probability skips the draw.
- Kill: only when the remaining outcome is Hit, draw salt 2 and replace Hit with Kill iff `u2 < clamp(pkKill,0,1)`. The kill draw is still evaluated for zero kill probability on a remaining Hit.
- Swarm scale: for positive base effect, living count and maximum, `effectivePkBase = pkBase * clamp(living/max,0,1)`; otherwise `SwarmOffensiveEffect.Scale` returns zero. This scaling is used only when the resolver has positive shooter maximum metadata.
- Envelope: `minRange <= range <= maxRange`. DLZ evaluates OutOfZone below `0.9*minRange` or above `maxRange`; Approaching above `0.85*maxRange`; otherwise InZone. Early accepts InZone/Approaching, Normal accepts InZone, Late additionally requires `range <= 0.7*maxRange`. Resolver envelope approval precedes DLZ, so DLZ's lower tolerance does not permit a launch below the weapon minimum.

These are per-engagement implementation rules, not a multiplied salvo probability, a continuous trajectory model or a general damage formula. Numerical validity and tuning changes require their own validated input contract.

## Edge Cases

- Dead shooter/target and denied policy consume no rounds; competing failures expose the first source-ordered gate.
- A tracked-empty mount must not be mistaken for an unseeded mount. Context ammunition alone cannot make an unseeded ledger consume successfully.
- Nonpositive salvo sizes normalize to one; insufficient rounds reject the whole salvo rather than partially consume it.
- Probabilities zero/one and repeated identical inputs are boundary cases. Draws are conditional, so code must not add extra random calls or use wall-clock/shared RNG.
- Intercept is a terminal nonlethal outcome on this path; it must not subsequently become Kill.
- Missing victim/weapon enrichment appears as explicit unknown facts in presentation. Missing outcome data may produce an InFlight label; do not invent travel time, physical position or a delayed authoritative kill from it.
- Different optional gate configuration, catalog/policy inputs or local deltas require separate evidence identity.

## Dependencies

Requirements: `Game-Requirements/requirements/14-Engagement-And-Fire-Control.md`, `18-Combat-Domains.md`, and `17-Replay-AAR-And-Order-Log.md`. Simulation contracts: `IEngageWorldQuery`, `EngageContext`, `MagazineLedger`, `KilledTargetRegistry`, `IPolicyEvaluator`, configured domain/speculative gates, `SimSeed` and `SeededRng`.

Presentation follows ADR-010 §2–3, ADR-007 and ADR-001: read snapshots/projections and submit intent through approved commands. No UI/content asset becomes simulation authority. DelegationBridge remains zero-touch; existing CatalogWriteGate paths remain extend-only; Baltic v2 replay hash `17144800277401907079` remains pinned.

Documentation delivery/review is [DRG-344](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-344), with native reconciliation context Requirements, backlog and roadmap reconciliation — 2026-09-30. GitNexus evidence is qualified by exact path and source inspection because DRG-323/324 track overload/index defects and DRG-197 graph recovery. No new graph-count certainty or code-edit authorization follows from this page.

## Tuning Knobs

Scenario/catalog/context inputs include weapon envelope, salvo size, effective ROE/WRA, DLZ personality, `PkBase`, `PkIntercept`, `PkKill`, readiness/track/EMCON state, configured speculative/domain gates and swarm integrity metadata. Gameplay configuration stays data-driven and revisioned with replay inputs.

The current source contains DLZ thresholds 0.9/0.85/0.7 and a linear living-integrity scale; these are observed implementation constants, not newly approved balancing targets. A proposed nonlinear curve, new flight model, per-round salvo resolution or revised damage model needs an explicit design decision, backlog scope and deterministic regression evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Named owner reviews this complete eight-section draft and records approved/rejected design scope; document completion alone does not satisfy product acceptance.
- [ ] Headless gate fixtures prove first-refusal reason, dead shooter/target, ROE/WRA, readiness/EMCON/fire-control, envelope/DLZ and insufficient-ammo behavior; every abort preserves rounds.
- [ ] Successful normalized salvo consumes exactly its size; repeated identical seed/request/configuration produces equal outcome and recorded hit draw.
- [ ] Probability boundaries and Hit → Intercept → Kill precedence are tested, including conditional intercept draw and remaining-Hit kill behavior.
- [ ] Swarm scaling and authorized integrity updates are verified against the source-defined positive/zero bounds.
- [ ] Presentation fixtures prove refusal visibility, explicit unknown enrichment, correlation and InFlight/TerminalOutcome projection without world/order/RNG mutation or a physical-kinematics claim.

Candidate tests: `src/ProjectAegis.Sim.Tests/Engage/MvpEngagementResolverTests.cs`, `CombatOutcomeResolverTests.cs`, `SwarmOffensiveEffectTests.cs`; `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/CombatEvents/CombatEventLogProjectionTests.cs`, `CombatEventProjectionTests.cs`; `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Presentation/CombatMapPresenterTests.cs`.

Fresh coordinating local regression results on 2026-09-30 were 3,352 solution tests, 26 proxy smoke and six canonical replay tests, with zero failures; build zero warnings/errors using SDK 8.0.425. These broad results do not independently prove each criterion above, exact SDK 8.0.400, live Editor visuals, owner design approval or DRG-208 acceptance at `1902dc12`. Record per-criterion revision/input identity and named owner decision before checking these boxes.

pages.title: Scenario Editor Spec
pages.content:
Status: DRAFT — generated from implementation, needs owner review

Owner: (unassigned)

Related Linear Milestone: M6 — Scenario Editor

Last updated: 2026-07-26

Provenance: Reverse-engineered from repo HEAD by automated audit; NOT an authored design doc. Verify before treating as authoritative.

## Overview

The Project Aegis Scenario Editor is a headless-first authoring system over a canonical `*.scenario.json` document, with interchangeable front-ends. The engine-free core (`src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Authoring/`) owns the document DTO, loader/writer, mutation editor, disk-backed undo stack, and the deterministic Validation Engine; the one-shot verb surface is `src/ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli/`; the long-lived in-process host is `ScenarioAuthoringSession` + `ScenarioEditCommandBus`, bound by engine-free presenters in `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/` and rendered by a Unity `EditorWindow` at `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Editor/ScenarioMapAuthoringWindow.cs`. Per ADR-017 the core is the system of record and every UI is a thin front-end; per ADR-008 validation is pure, deterministic, LLM-free, and gates export/play/sample but never save.

## Player Fantasy

Per `design/gdd/agentic-mission-editor.md` §2, the v1 fantasy is theater designer: you place the ORBAT, draw patrol zones, and lay missions and triggers on a map-first surface. The differentiator stated in the GDD is that the tool never lets you ship something broken silently — the moment a strike cannot reach its target on fuel, a patrol zone is empty, or a ferry has no destination, the editor names what, where, and how to fix it before play. The scenario is a plain, diffable artifact that replays identically. The GDD explicitly scopes the "AI staff drafts your scenario" experience to Phase 2/3 as a north star, not a v1 promise.

## Detailed Rules

Authoring surfaces that exist. Three, over one contract:

1. CLI/MCP one-shot verbs (`src/ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli/Program.cs`): `scenario_create`, `scenario_validate`, `scenario_export`, `scenario_export_brief`, `scenario_publish`, `scenario_simulate_sample`, `scenario_undo`, `scenario_ai_scaffold`, `scenario_diff_summary`, `scenario_event_trace`, plus `mission_*`, `orbat_*`, `event_*`, `side_*`, `timeline_*`, `reference_point_upsert`.
2. In-process host — `ScenarioAuthoringSession.Open(path)` → `session.Bus` verbs (`PlaceUnit`, `MoveUnit`, `CloneUnit`, `UpsertReferencePoint`, `Attach{Patrol,Strike,Ferry,Support}FromSelection`, `CloneMission`, `AddFromTemplate`, `DeleteMission`, `UpsertEvent`, `UpsertSide`, `UpsertTimelineEntry`, `RefreshFindings`), documented in `docs/engineering/scenario-authoring-host.md`.
3. Unity Editor window — menu `Project Aegis/Scenario Map Authoring`, UI in `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/UI/ScenarioEditor/ScenarioMapAuthoringPanel.uxml`/`.uss`: sticky path/Open/Save/Rebuild/Refresh-Findings bar, ORBAT/RP/findings-code lists, a PLACE UNIT form, and a 3-vertex RP polygon upsert.

Lifecycle. Place/edit → mutate → validate → export/publish. Every mutation goes through one pipeline: `RequireEditVersion` → `CaptureUndoSnapshot` → action → persist snapshot → `CommitMutation` (bumps `editVersion` by 1) → optional save → live validate. Undo is disk-backed at `.undo-stack.json` and cross-process. Reading is tolerant (case-insensitive, comments, trailing commas); writing is canonical camelCase with `DefaultIgnoreCondition = Never`. Gestures are two-phase: `Begin*` stages a tentative DTO, `Commit*` pushes through the bus, `CancelGesture()` discards.

Save is never gated; export/publish/sample are. `ScenarioPublishCommand` refuses with `VALIDATION_BLOCKED` when `ScenarioExportCommand.Prepare(...).Allowed` is false, and emits a manifest with provenance tags and the embedded `ReportHash`.

Host policy (`ScenarioMapAuthoringHostPolicy.cs`): catalog/domain/form chrome is always enabled; session write actions require an open session; the no-session message is `"Open a scenario.json first (Browse… then Open)."`. Chrome rebuilds and any domain/form change call `CancelGesture()` so Commit can never write a stale invisible payload. Default UI-dev seed candidates, first-existing-wins: `assets/data/scenarios/authoring/russia-vs-nato-baltic-ui-dev.json`, then `assets/data/scenarios/validation/golden_clean.json`.

Domain catalog constraints (`ScenarioPlatformDomainCatalog.cs`): four stable domains — `aircraft`, `ships`, `subs`, `ground` — with a hard-coded preset list per domain, each carrying a `DefaultSideId` of `blue`/`red`. `GetPresets` accepts aliases (`air`, `naval`, `land`); unknown domains return empty. `SuggestUnitId` emits `u-{platform-slug≤24}-{n}`. This is a UI preset list, not the authoritative catalog — ids resolve at validation time against the bound `dbRef` catalog.

Agent-authored transparency. Per `docs/engineering/scenario-ai-authoring-and-adjudication.md`, the v1 "no-LLM contract" holds: `AiAuthoringServices` are deterministic heuristic stubs, enforced by `NoDynamicExecutionGateTests` which bans Lua packages and `Reflection.Emit`/Roslyn/`CSharpScript`/`Process.Start` from the authoring path. Every output carries `ManifestBuilder.ProvenanceTag(Tag, Source, AgentId?, Evidence?, Hash?)` with `Source ∈ {user, ai, import}`, surviving into the published manifest. ADR-015 (Proposed, decision due 2026-09-01) would derive an "agent-assisted / agent-authored" label from provenance — not implemented.

## Formulas

Strike/ferry reachability (GDD §4.1, ADR-008), haversine in nm. `combat_radius_nm` is a round-trip budget and must not be doubled:

```javascript
range_to_target_nm  = haversine(launch_base, target) + ingress_egress_pad_nm
available_radius_nm = combat_radius_nm * fuel_fraction
reachable           = available_radius_nm >= range_to_target_nm
```

Event-graph complexity (ADR-016):

```javascript
complexity        = E + sum(conditions_per_event) + C * cross_refs   warn if > WARN_THRESHOLD
peak_tick_density = max over ticks of (events with trigger_time_resolved == tick)   warn if > DENSITY_THRESHOLD
```

Both are soft warnings and never block export. The single hard cap is 32 conditions per event → `EVENT_CONDITION_CAP_EXCEEDED` (Error). Live defaults in `assets/data/editor/validation-config.json`: pad `50` nm, fuel fraction `0.85`, floor `error`, complexity `400`, density `20`, cross-ref weight `2`, max conditions `32`.

Determinism: findings sort `(Severity DESC, Code ASC, MissionId, UnitId, TargetId, Message)` with a SHA-256 `ReportHash` (ADR-008). Seed default `42` (`metadata.seed`); `scenario_simulate_sample` defaults to 32 ticks and emits `SEED=… HASH=…` plus a world-state SHA-256 excluding `editorState`. Authoring-time fire order (`EventFireOrderCalculator.cs`): `Time` triggers rank `0`, all others `int.MaxValue`, ties broken by event id ordinal.

> OPEN QUESTION: GDD §4.2 specifies `sort_key = (trigger_time_resolved, event.priority, event.id)` with a designer `priority` field (0–1000, default 100). `ScenarioEventDto` has no `priority` field and `EventFireOrderCalculator` ignores it. Is the GDD formula aspirational, or is the implementation under-built?

## Edge Cases

- Invalid placement / geometry. Invalid reference-point geometry still commits by design — `MapAuthoringSurface` + `ScenarioGeometryValidity` mark it `IsGeometryValid=false` with an `InvalidReason` map hint, not a Validation Engine finding. A Patrol with fewer than 3 waypoints is `PATROL_ZONE_DEGENERATE` (Error).
- ID resolution failures. `DB_MISMATCH` when `dbRef`/`dbSnapshotId` resolves to no snapshot; `BROKEN_REF` for a `ref:`-prefixed id resolving to nothing; unresolved ids are skipped by reachability rather than falsely flagged. `ScenarioValidateCommand.ResolveCatalog` falls back to `InMemoryCatalogReader.BalticPatrolFixture()` when SQLite or the binding fails.
- Policy / gate violations. Export, brief, publish, and sample are refused while any `Error` finding stands; save always succeeds. TL branch errors: `TL_BRANCH_MISSING/INVALID/SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH`, `TL_RELEASE_TRAIN_NOT_FOUND/MISMATCH`. Strike readiness: `AIR_NOT_READY`, `STRIKE_INVALID_PLATFORM` (`combat_radius_nm ≤ 0`).
- Round-trip failures. A stale `--edit-version` raises `ScenarioEditConflictException`, `code: "CONFLICT"`, exit `3`, carrying `currentEditVersion` + `fileHash`; the guard throws before any write, so no partial state. Bus verbs return `ScenarioMutationResult` with `CONFLICT` or `INVALID_OPERATION` instead of throwing. `save: false` batches in memory — un-flushed edits are lost without `session.Save()`. `DeleteSide` does not cascade ORBAT units.
- Event graph. `EVENT_DEAD_TRIGGER`, `EVENT_UNREACHABLE_ACTION`, `EVENT_CONTRADICTORY`, and `EVENT_CIRCULAR` (Tarjan SCC over `ActivateMission → MissionComplete`) are all Warnings. `scenario_event_trace` reports `fired: false` for nearly everything because there is no live sim state.
- Agent-authored content. Reproducible stub output only; `scenario_ai_scaffold` refuses a blank brief (`MISSING_BRIEF`) and an existing `--out` (`FILE_EXISTS`).

> OPEN QUESTION: GDD §5 specifies edge behaviors not found in the implemented finding catalog — the TeleportUnit export transform, the "time trigger before scenario start" warning, and the zero-distance-strike `STRIKE_COLOCATED_WARNING` (explicitly listed non-v1 in ADR-008). Current status was not determinable from the code read.

## Dependencies

| Kind | Path |
| --- | --- |
| Core assembly | `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Authoring/`, `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Validation/` |
| Presenters | `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/` (8 files) |
| CLI | `src/ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli/` (`Program.cs`, `Scenario*Command.cs`, `Mission*Command.cs`, `EventCommands.cs`) |
| Sim policy | `src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Scenario/` (`ScenarioPolicyRepository`, `ScenarioPolicyJsonLoader`, `ScenarioPolicyCatalog`) |
| Unity host | `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Editor/ScenarioMapAuthoringWindow.cs`, `Assets/UI/ScenarioEditor/ScenarioMapAuthoringPanel.uxml`/`.uss` |
| Data files | `data/scenarios/scenario-document.schema.json`, `data/scenarios/examples/*.scenario.json`, `assets/data/editor/validation-config.json`, `assets/data/scenarios/authoring/russia-vs-nato-baltic-ui-dev.json` |
| ADRs | 008 (Accepted), 014 (Accepted), 016 (Accepted), 015 (Proposed), 017 (Proposed); ADR-008 depends on ADR-001/004/006 |
| Docs | `docs/engineering/scenario-{document-authoring,authoring-host,event-system,policy-authoring,ai-authoring-and-adjudication,mission-editor-cli}.md` |

## Tuning Knobs

`assets/data/editor/validation-config.json` — `ingressEgressPadNm` (20–150, default 50), `fuelFraction` (0.70–0.95, default 0.85), `exportBlockSeverityFloor` (`error`/`warning`, default `error`), `complexityWarnThreshold` (200–1000, default 400), `densityWarnThreshold` (10–50, default 20), `crossRefWeight` (1–4, default 2), `maxConditionsPerEvent` (fixed 32).

CLI — `--edit-version` (required on every mutating verb); `--seed` / `--db-ref` / `--policy-id` on `scenario_create` (defaults `42` / `baltic_patrol` / `baltic-patrol-catalog`); `--ticks` (default 32) and `--policy-dir` on `scenario_simulate_sample`; `--policy` / `--policy-dir` / `--profile ladder|ci` on `gauntlet_oracle_eval`; `--event` on `scenario_event_trace`.

Document-level — `metadata.seed`, `metadata.tlBranch` (`TL-0`…`TL-5`), `metadata.maxTechnologyLevel` (default 2), `features.maxTimeCompression` (default 256), `LiveFindingsPresenter(debounceMs)` (default 300, reserved/inert).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `scenario_validate --path ` emits `passed`, `canExport`, `reportHash`, `findings[]`; exit `1` on any blocking finding, `0` otherwise.
2. Save succeeds on a document with blocking errors; `scenario_export`, `scenario_export_brief`, `scenario_publish`, and `scenario_simulate_sample` on the same file are rejected with the same finding list.
3. Two `scenario_simulate_sample` runs at fixed seed and knobs produce byte-identical `fire_order` and identical world-state SHA-256, both emitting `SEED=… HASH=…`.
4. A stale `--edit-version` returns `CONFLICT` with `currentEditVersion` + `fileHash`, exit `3`, with no partial write.
5. Each of the six ADR-008 v1 rules has a dedicated test asserting its code; `STRIKE_UNREACHABLE` carries `Data["excess_nm"]`. Baltic-scale validation completes in under 100 ms.
6. An event with more than 32 conditions blocks export; complexity and density breaches warn and still export; warnings are byte-identical run-to-run.
7. Committed examples in `data/scenarios/examples/` and live `ScenarioDocumentEditor` output both conform to `scenario-document.schema.json`.
8. Host/presenter contracts are green headless: `ScenarioEditCommandBusTests`, `MissionBoardPresenterTests`, `MapAuthoringSurfaceTests`, `EditModeControllerTests`, `LiveFindingsPresenterTests`, `EventGraphPresenterTests`.
9. Unity panel contract: `ScenarioMapAuthoringPanelUiTests` pins stable UXML element names, USS token imports, and that `CreateGUI` loads the shipped UXML path.
10. `NoDynamicExecutionGateTests` fails the build on any Lua/eval/reflection-emit reference in the authoring path (ADR-014).
11. Repo gates: `dotnet test ProjectAegis.sln --filter "PlayModeSmokeHarnessTests|ReplayGolden"` and the `/scenario-audit` skill's per-scenario PASS/FAIL.

> OPEN QUESTION: ADR-008 declares "exactly six v1 rules", but the shipped catalog in `docs/engineering/scenario-document-authoring.md` has roughly 20 codes (TL branch, fuel variants, `BROKEN_REF`, `INCOMPATIBLE_HOST`, `DOCTRINE_RESOLVED`, event codes). The ADR has not been amended to reflect the delivered rule set.

> OPEN QUESTION: `event_validate` exists as `EventValidateCommand` but is not wired into CLI dispatch. Dead code, or an unfinished verb?

## Overview

The tactical map is a presentation client over the headless simulation. It renders registered friendly units, log-derived contacts, alive/dead state, optional kinematic poses, and plotted courses through MapPictureBridge and immutable projection rows. Presentation boundaries are ADR-010 §2–3, ADR-007, and ADR-001.

Evidence scope: The 2026-09-30 source inspection cited a local checkout at HEAD 4190fb1b49cd15775b6b995b7c245d73828cd7a2, with existing working-tree changes. As of 2026-11-20 that SHA is not on origin (absent from a fetched clone and from GitHub), and uncommitted working-tree changes cannot be pinned. Published main SHAs: last main tip at the time of the inspection, [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd) (2026-09-27, 2:40 PM CDT, #681); current main [99a4d6e4](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/99a4d6e4be82dcf1bbce372caa47abef150f2b9b) (2026-11-17, 7:16 PM CT). The source contracts below were not GitHub blob or commit links, so those paths were left as-is after confirming they exist at [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd). Refreshed against main 1902dc12 because 4190fb1b was never pushed (ruling: Decision, 2026-11-20). This is not a claim about current main or owner Play Mode acceptance. GitNexus was queried with the absolute repository path and corroborated against source because DRG-323/324 record index/overload limitations.

Existing delivery includes the placeholder map host, map bridge/binder, selection controller, course projection, glyph/atlas fallback seams, and globe status host code. Full globe interaction, complete tactical symbology, and H5 content loading remain separately scoped delivery or design work; host presence does not establish product completeness.

## Player Fantasy

The player reads a theater picture, selects a friendly force or contact, inspects why events occurred, and issues deliberate commands. The map must make unavailable positional evidence distinguishable from a real tracked position. Selecting or inspecting an item changes presentation context without changing authoritative simulation state.

## Detailed Rules

1. MapPictureBridge collects OOB membership from the target registry, alive state and optional kinematic poses from ISimWorldSnapshot, and contact rows from the decision-log contact projection. Rendering does not write the world or decision log.
2. Placement precedence is exact: a complete normalized X/Y pair wins; otherwise a complete latitude/longitude pair projects onto the Baltic canvas; otherwise use deterministic hash placement and set HasAuthoritativePose to false. With normalized coordinates, supplied geographic coordinates are retained when both exist; otherwise derive Baltic geographic coordinates. Normalized coordinates are not clamped by this projection.
3. Friendly and contact rows are sorted by affiliation and then symbol ID using ordinal comparison. The current basic contact path renders contacts as Hostile; it does not implement the full future affiliation/classification symbology matrix.
4. MapPanelBinder marks non-authoritative placements as unknown-pose, applies selection styling, adds stale/ghost presentation for degraded hostile contacts, and frozen styling for denied comms. These styles are presentation effects, not additional sensor truth.
5. Selecting a friendly unit clears contact selection. Selecting a hostile contact clears the friendly selection and graph highlights from the previous unit. CombatInspection is separate from the unit selection used for player commands.
6. Plotted courses omit destroyed units, absent waypoint lists, and paths with fewer than two vertices. The current pose or hash fallback is prepended unless it already matches the first waypoint.
7. Interpolation only blends matching, non-destroyed symbols with authoritative previous and current poses. New, unknown-pose, or destroyed symbols use the current row. Frame interpolation never enters authoritative clocks or order logs.
8. MapPlaceholderPanelHost binds the projected picture and routes symbol clicks through its presentation feed. Its existing atlas choice is: unavailable catalog when frames are disabled; successfully loaded local manifest catalog when preferred; otherwise the default atlas catalog. This bounded fallback does not prove the broader H5 loader or LIB-05 failure-isolation requirement is implemented.
9. Authority-changing map actions use the approved command façade under ADR-010. Camera, layout, selection, and inspection are presentation actions. Full military/civilian symbology profiles remain proposed in the two 2026-09-05 requirement drafts.

## Formulas

Baltic canvas projection (existing code):

```txt
x = clamp01((longitude - 24.0) / 1.5)
y = clamp01((latitude - 59.5) / 1.0)
latitude  = 59.5 + normalizedY * 1.0
longitude = 24.0 + normalizedX * 1.5
```

Only the latitude/longitude-to-canvas path clamps. The inverse and normalized-pose path do not add a clamp.

Placeholder placement (existing code): hash the string seed:ID with DeterministicHash.OrdinalHash. For friendly units use layoutSeed; for contacts use layoutSeed + 17. Take the low 16 bits for hx and the next 16 bits for hy.

```txt
x = (hx / 65535) * 0.75 + 0.1
y = (hy / 65535) * 0.75 + 0.1
```

This places fallback markers in the interior of the canvas; it is a layout convention, not estimated geography.

Presentation interpolation: for 0 ≤ t \< 1, blend each eligible coordinate as a + (b - a) \* t; negative t becomes zero, and t ≥ 1 returns current rows. Geographic values blend only when both endpoints provide them. Course first-vertex equality uses absolute X and Y differences below 1e-5.

## Edge Cases

- Missing or incomplete coordinate pairs fall through the precedence rule rather than fabricating a partial authoritative pose.
- Out-of-box geographic coordinates clamp to the Baltic canvas edge while retaining the original geographic values. Out-of-range normalized values are retained by MapPictureProjection; upstream validation is a separate responsibility.
- Missing atlas frames must resolve through the existing glyph fallback seam. H5 will define asset delay, corruption, version mismatch, timeout/cancellation, visible diagnostics, and measured budgets for its chosen local pilot before delivery.
- Ghost rows are unselected and carry ghost IDs; they must not masquerade as new authoritative contacts.
- Destroyed units retain destroyed-symbol presentation and do not emit plotted courses or interpolate motion.
- Inspection history may lack pose evidence. Display unavailable evidence explicitly instead of substituting a later/current pose.
- Empty OOB/contact inputs produce an empty picture. Null required bridge inputs are rejected. Finite-coordinate validation is not introduced by this design refresh.

## Dependencies

Current source contracts:

- `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Bridge/MapPictureBridge.cs`
- `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/MapPictureProjection.cs`
- `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/MapPanelBinder.cs`
- `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/MapSymbolPresentationLerp.cs`
- `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Presentation/C2PresentationController.cs`
- `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/MapPlaceholderPanelHost.cs`
- `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/GlobeMapProductHost.cs` — present in the pre-existing dirty working tree; no integrated-main equivalence claimed.

Normative architecture: `docs/architecture/adr-010-headless-first-command-driven-ui.md`, `docs/architecture/adr-007-c2-map-presentation.md`, `docs/architecture/adr-001-sim-assembly-boundary.md`.

Requirements: `Game-Requirements/requirements/20-Command-And-Control-UI.md`; `Game-Requirements/drafts/2026-09-05-military-tactical-symbology.md`; `Game-Requirements/drafts/2026-09-05-civilian-gameplay-symbology.md`; proposed LIB-05 in `Game-Requirements/drafts/27-Scenario-Library-Campaigns.md`.

Delivery: [DRG-275 design reconciliation](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-275), [DRG-208 owner acceptance](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208), [DRG-332 H5 inventory](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-332), [DRG-331 H5 ADR](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-331), and [DRG-347 local presentation pilot](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-347).

Related design: Core Simulation Design and Weapons & Engagement Resolution.

## Tuning Knobs

layoutSeed controls placeholder layout only. ScenarioCommsDisplaySettings supplies ghost offsets and lag labels. The host frame-enable flag, manifest preference, and manifest path select the current atlas availability path. Presentation interpolation t belongs to the frame clock.

Baltic box constants describe the current demo projection; making arbitrary theater bounds data-driven is a future design decision. H5 compatibility versions, timeout/cancellation policy, content class, diagnostic wording, and performance budgets remain explicit pilot decisions. Neither a 5k-symbol/60 FPS product target nor full globe fidelity is asserted by this page.

## Acceptance Criteria

Existing contracts to preserve, validated here by source inspection rather than a new test run:

- Same seed and IDs give stable fallback placement and ordering; a complete pose replaces fallback and sets the authoritative flag. Evidence: `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Projection/MapPictureProjectionTests.cs` and `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Bridge/MapPictureBridgeTests.cs`.
- Unknown pose, selection, comms ghost/frozen styling, and atlas fallback remain observable. Evidence: `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Projection/MapPanelBinderTests.cs`.
- Friendly/contact selection and previous graph highlights remain coordinated. Evidence: `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Presentation/C2PresentationControllerTests.cs`.
- Combat effects resolve contact identity without changing the underlying map picture. Evidence: `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Presentation/CombatMapIntegrationTests.cs`.
- Interpolation remains presentation-only and courses exclude destroyed units. Evidence: `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Projection/MapSymbolPresentationLerpTests.cs` and MapPictureProjectionTests.

Pending owner/product acceptance: DRG-208 records the revision-specific Play Mode walk and individual criteria; headless proxy passes do not substitute for it. DRG-275 owns review of this draft and any corrections to the current/proposed boundary.

Proposed H5 acceptance: after inventory and ADR gates, inject missing, delayed, corrupt, and version-mismatched presentation assets; show the agreed fallback/diagnostic; compare authoritative state and order-log fingerprints at identical simulation ticks. Record revision, build/catalog/scenario identity, commands, expected/actual results, and evidence links. Pilot budgets are agreed before execution; no measured pass is claimed here.

## Linked Linear

Project: [cmano-clone](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/project/cmano-clone-7f6a00e4c1c9) · Current design review: DRG-275 / Combat UX M0 / S122–S127. Original stub milestone: M5 — Map/UI Rendering (historical).

pages.title: ⚙️ Core Simulation Design
pages.content:
Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/17-Replay-AAR-And-Order-Log.md`; `Game-Requirements/drafts/26-Verification-CI-Gauntlet.md`
Req IDs: RPL-29, VER-07
Lifecycle: Draft — owner acceptance pending
Linear: [DRG-343](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-343) · [DRG-349](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-349) · [DRG-201](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-201) · [DRG-244](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-244)

---

Status: Draft — source reconciliation authored; owner review pending.

Owner: drg amtd

Related Linear Milestone: M3 / Core — S122–S127 evidence rebaseline.

Last updated: 2026-09-30.

Design review task: [DRG-343](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-343).

Evidence identity: The 2026-09-30 refresh cited a local checkout at `C:\Users\dgorn\cmano-clone\cmano-clone`, HEAD `4190fb1b49cd15775b6b995b7c245d73828cd7a2`, with uncommitted changes. As of 2026-11-20 that SHA is not on origin (absent from a fetched clone and from GitHub), and uncommitted working-tree changes cannot be pinned. Published main SHAs: last main tip at the time of the refresh, [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd) (2026-09-27, 2:40 PM CDT, #681), which this page already named as a separate target; current main [99a4d6e4](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/99a4d6e4be82dcf1bbce372caa47abef150f2b9b) (2026-11-17, 7:16 PM CT). Blob links that previously used `4190fb1b` now point at the same paths on [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd). Refreshed against main 1902dc12 because 4190fb1b was never pushed (ruling: Decision, 2026-11-20). Planning completion does not grant product acceptance.

---

## Overview

The headless simulation supplies authoritative execution; the player prepares the scenario, begins execution, delegates orders, and inspects outcomes. This page describes the implemented session/tick contract and distinguishes it from proposed session restoration. UI reads projections and submits intent through approved command seams; it does not own the simulation clock or world state.

The main orchestration source is [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/SimulationSession.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/SimulationSession.cs); delegation is [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/DelegationOrchestrator.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/DelegationOrchestrator.cs). GitNexus path-qualified context calls against this exact checkout corroborated both classes, plus ReplayCheckpointStore and the delegation SeededRng. Same-name sibling indexes are not interchangeable; graph results corroborate source navigation, not runtime proof.

## Player Fantasy

Command a theater at the pace needed to understand events: plan before execution, pause to inspect attention and constraints, accelerate quiet periods, then see why delegated or human orders executed or were withheld. Outcomes remain reproducible for a fixed build and input sequence. Pause freezes the interactive simulation clock; it must not be presented as a guarantee that all orchestration queues and logs stop changing.

## Detailed Rules

1. Planning versus execution. SimulationSession.Tick and TickHeadless return false in Planning before running the session. BeginExecution changes the orchestrator phase; its initial Planning-to-Executing transition appends a mode-change record. The session does not infer readiness from elapsed calendar time.
2. Outer delegation call. RunExecutingTick calls Orchestrator.Tick once with the supplied ObservedState. The orchestrator drains approved orders, evaluates active agents, and drains agent/human issued queues into ExecutedOrders. It derives its order tick from the observed SimTime; this is distinct from the pipeline clock.
3. Interactive pause. The pause check occurs after the orchestrator call. A paused executing session may therefore drain queues or emit decision/denial records while its simulation clock does not advance. Tick returns true for the executing call even when paused; that return value alone does not prove a new simulation tick.
4. Engagement and cadence. An unpaused call selects Engage orders, applies communications and salvo/deconfliction gates, enqueues requests, and calls Sim.TickOnce in RealTime mode. It logs the initial results and applies damage handling, then performs acceleration-factor-minus-one extra pipeline steps. Delegation, result logging/damage handling, and the final logistics FSM call are not repeated for every extra step by this method. Do not describe acceleration as a whole-session tick repeated uniformly.
5. Headless execution. TickHeadless selects HeadlessBatch, bypassing the pipeline pause gate while retaining the pause flag. In Planning it still returns false. Watch attention can require acknowledgement or explicit override through TryResumeSim; legacy ResumeSim bypasses that watch gate.
6. Verification checkpoints. [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpointStore.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpointStore.cs) appends strictly increasing checkpoint ticks and finds the latest at/before a requested tick. [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpoint.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpoint.cs) contains SimTick, WorldHash, LogFingerprint, and LastSequenceId. These are verification metadata, not a serialized restorable session.

## Formulas

- Clock time is `SimClock.SimTime = SimTick * FixedDeltaSeconds`; default delta is `1/60` second. Acceleration changes the number of fixed steps, not the delta. See [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Time/SimClock.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Time/SimClock.cs).
- For an executing, unpaused session call with factor F, the pipeline advances `1 + max(0, F - 1)` steps. F is clamped to 1–256. The session owns this outer acceleration loop; direct pipeline Accelerated mode separately uses F steps. See [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SimTickPipeline.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SimTickPipeline.cs).
- Delegation [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Decision/SeededRng.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Decision/SeededRng.cs) initializes state from global seed XOR salted agent identity, substitutes 1 for zero, applies xorshift updates (13, 7, 17), then returns `(state & 0xFFFFFF) / 0x1000000`. Reproducibility requires the same seed, salt, and draw order.
- The separate [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SeededRng.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SeededRng.cs) uses seed/domain/entity/tick/draw-index hashing. Its masked uint division can include the endpoint 1.0; the two RNG contracts must not be conflated.

## Edge Cases

- Calling Tick during Planning is rejected even when headless execution was requested.
- Paused execution is not queue immutability; distinguish observed order time, orchestration effects, and pipeline tick progression in diagnostics.
- Repeating a checkpoint tick or recording an earlier tick is ignored; an empty/before-first lookup returns no checkpoint.
- A hash checkpoint cannot reconstruct pending events, RNG state, engagements, resources, or authority-bearing mission state.
- Proposed RPL-29–31 require same-build/scenario/catalog/policy uninterrupted-versus-restored equality and non-mutating corrupt/incompatible-load failure. These contracts, [DRG-348](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-348) and [DRG-349](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-349), are gated backlog work; save/resume and multiplayer are not established by replay goldens.

## Dependencies

The [cmano-clone project](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/project/cmano-clone-7f6a00e4c1c9) links requirements 03/08/17, ADR-001 simulation boundary, ADR-003 order log, ADR-004 tick pipeline, and presentation ADR-010 sections 2–3 plus ADR-007. `DelegationBridge` remains zero-touch. Scenario policy, catalog, seed and ordered input identities are required context for deterministic comparisons. S122–S127 delivery follows evidence gates; [DRG-208](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208) remains owner Play Mode acceptance.

## Tuning Knobs

Fixed delta and clock factor are existing implementation settings; factor bounds 1–256 are code constraints, not newly accepted product performance targets. Scenario-policy values govern gameplay tuning. Checkpoint frequency is chosen by the harness/caller, not persisted as a save/resume contract. Any cadence or performance change needs profiling, criterion-specific evidence and current upstream impact analysis before symbol edits; no parameter changes are authorized by this page.

## Acceptance Criteria

These are review/verification criteria, not fresh execution results or owner signoff.

- CS-01: verify Planning calls do not advance the pipeline; BeginExecution exposes the documented phase/log transition. Candidate source tests: `SimulationSessionPhaseTests`.
- CS-02: verify paused interactive clock remains unchanged while separately inspecting approved/human queue and log behavior; do not accept only the Tick boolean. Candidate source tests: `SimulationSessionClockControlsTests`; queue/log coverage must be checked explicitly.
- CS-03: compare factors 1 and greater than 1 against the documented outer/inner cadence; confirm fixed delta does not stretch. Existing clock tests are candidate mappings, not proof of uniform subsystem acceleration.
- CS-04: verify headless pause override and watch acknowledgement/override behavior. Candidate source tests: `SimulationSessionWatchAttentionTests`.
- CS-05: repeat identical build/input/seed runs and compare state/order fingerprints; retain Baltic v2 hash `17144800277401907079`. Use `AGENTS.md` standing gates and the six canonical replay cases; recorded counts must identify revision and local delta.
- CS-06: review checkpoint metadata honesty and keep RPL-29–31 proposed until schema/feasibility/ADR and differential restore tests exist.
- CS-07: collect criterion-level SHA/build/local delta/scenario/catalog/policy/test-layer/result evidence and an explicit owner decision under proposed VER-07.3–6. This draft and source inspection satisfy neither Editor coverage nor owner acceptance.
