pages.title: 🔍 Mission Editor — UX/UI Review (2026-07-26)
pages.content:
Type: Review artifact (not a design page — the wiki's 8-section design template does not apply)

Status: Draft — for owner triage

Reviewer: `/ux-review` (adapted: interface review, not spec review)

Date: 2026-07-26

Subject: Mission Editor / Scenario Map Authoring — GitNexus-derived web mock (ME-W1) reviewed against the shipped Unity panel at repo HEAD

Related: [Scenario Editor Spec](https://app.notion.com/p/3a7f7cb4e4df819a8645c89f0c1d5d20)

## Tracked in Linear

Filed 2026-07-26. Two findings turned out to be defects in already-delivered work rather than Phase 2 scope, so they carry no milestone — following the DRG-50 / DRG-54 precedent for defects found after a milestone closes. The remaining 21 findings stay here rather than being duplicated into Linear, per the workspace contract that Linear points at design rather than restating it.

| Issue | Covers | Milestone |
| --- | --- | --- |
| \DRG-56](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-56%22%3EDRG-56%3C/a%3E) — validation gate unreachable from the UI | UX-01 | none (defect) |
| \DRG-55](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-55%22%3EDRG-55%3C/a%3E) — findings sort contradicts ADR-008 | UX-02 | none (defect) |
| \DRG-57](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-57%22%3EDRG-57%3C/a%3E) — H4 open/no-go decision | UX-03…23 | H4 |

DRG-55 and DRG-56 are actionable now — both are presenter-layer and headless-testable, and neither needs the H4 scope decision. Everything else waits on DRG-57.

## Scope and method

Reviewed the ME-W1 mock against the shipped implementation, so each finding is marked as affecting the mock, the shipped panel, or both. All code claims carry `file:line` from a HEAD read.

One framing note that shapes the whole review: the mock is ahead of the shipped panel in one respect and identical to it in the worst respect. The mock renders severity badges, human messages, and entity ids on findings; the shipped panel renders bare code strings. But neither surfaces the export gate — and that gate is the product's entire stated differentiator.

## Verdict

NEEDS REVISION — 8 blocking, 11 should-fix, 4 backlog.

The blocking set is not cosmetic. Three of the eight (UX-01, UX-02, UX-05) are cases where correct, tested behaviour exists in the core and is simply not reachable from any UI. That is the cheapest class of defect to fix and the most expensive to leave.

## What is already right

Worth stating, because the fixes below should not disturb it:

- Headless-first presenter split (`src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/`) means every recommendation here is testable without the Editor. The UX debt is in the view layer, not the architecture.
- Design tokens exist — `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/UI/AegisTokens.uss` with a real semantic palette (`--text-muted`, `--affil-friendly`, `--selected-row-bg`). Most of the visual fixes are token work, not redesign.
- Save is never gated while export/publish/sample are. This is the correct policy and the UI should make it legible, not change it.
- Two-phase gestures with `CancelGesture()` on every chrome rebuild — a genuinely good safety design that prevents stale invisible payloads.
- Deterministic findings with a `ReportHash`. The ordering bug in UX-02 is a presenter defect, not a determinism defect.

## Summary

| ID | Finding | Surface | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UX-01 | Export gate is invisible and unreachable from any UI | Both | Blocking |
| UX-02 | Findings sorted by code, not severity — violates ADR-008 | Both | Blocking |
| UX-03 | Shipped findings list shows codes only — no severity, message, or location | Panel | Blocking |
| UX-04 | Findings are dead ends — no navigation, no fix path | Both | Blocking |
| UX-05 | No Undo/Redo UI despite a disk-backed cross-process undo stack | Panel | Blocking |
| UX-06 | No keyboard model: no focus styles, no shortcuts, no tab order | Both | Blocking |
| UX-07 | Implementation vocabulary is the dominant on-screen text | Mock | Blocking |
| UX-08 | Center canvas is dead space; primary content exiled to a 90px strip | Mock | Blocking |
| UX-09 | Dirty state under-weighted; editVersion always shown raw | Both | Should fix |
| UX-10 | No conflict/reconcile UI for the CONFLICT path | Both | Should fix |
| UX-11 | Contrast unverified; flat 10/11/13px type scale; opacity-only disabled | Both | Should fix |
| UX-12 | Severity conveyed by colour alone in counters and row tint | Mock | Should fix |
| UX-13 | Hover, selected, and focus share one fill | Both | Should fix |
| UX-14 | Filter chips and count chips are visually identical | Mock | Should fix |
| UX-15 | Raw ticks shown as user-facing time | Mock | Should fix |
| UX-16 | "Timeline" is a table — no density view, though ADR-016 warns on density | Mock | Should fix |
| UX-17 | Inspector clipped, untitled; ROE inheritance state ambiguous | Mock | Should fix |
| UX-18 | Contextual actions enabled out of context | Both | Should fix |
| UX-19 | Panel USS bypasses its own token file in three places | Panel | Should fix |
| UX-20 | No seed / determinism surface, no sample-run action | Both | Backlog |
| UX-21 | No dbRef / catalog binding indicator | Both | Backlog |
| UX-22 | No TL branch indicator | Both | Backlog |
| UX-23 | No provenance display (user / ai / import) | Both | Backlog |

---

# Blocking

## UX-01 — The export gate is invisible and unreachable

Surface: both.

The shipped button set is Browse, Open, Load UI Dev Baltic, Save, Rebuild, Refresh Findings, four domain buttons, and the place/RP form actions (`ScenarioMapAuthoringWindow.cs:307-338`). There is no Export, Publish, Validate, or Play action. `ScenarioExportCommand.Prepare` exists at `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Authoring/ScenarioExportCommand.cs:23` with no UI caller anywhere in the Unity layer. `EditModeController.TryEnterPlay` (`EditModeController.cs:51-63`) is the error gate, and it is not referenced by the window at all — the window holds only `_session`, `_surface`, `_findings` (`ScenarioMapAuthoringWindow.cs:33-36`).

The mock repeats the gap: Refresh, Save, Clone Selected. A designer looking at "1 ERROR" learns that something is wrong and nothing about what it costs them.

This is the central finding. The GDD's stated differentiator is that the tool never lets you ship something broken silently. Right now the editor is silent about the one thing it exists to say.

Fix. Add a persistent gate status element in the session bar, adjacent to the findings count: `EXPORT BLOCKED · 1 error` / `READY TO EXPORT`. Render Export, Publish, and Sample as disabled buttons carrying the blocking reason in tooltip and accessible name — not as absent controls. Disabled-with-reason teaches the rule; absent teaches nothing.

Presenter work required: `LiveFindingsPresenter` exposes only `HasErrorSeverity` (`LiveFindingsPresenter.cs:42-43`). It needs per-severity counts and a `CanExport` flag sourced from `ScenarioExportCommand.Prepare(...).Allowed`, so the view never recomputes the gate.

## UX-02 — Findings are sorted by code, not severity

Surface: both.

`LiveFindingsPresenter.cs:52-55` sorts with `.Select(f => f.Code).OrderBy(c => c, StringComparer.Ordinal)`. ADR-008 pins the order as `(Severity DESC, Code ASC, MissionId, UnitId, TargetId, Message)`.

The mock shows the consequence exactly: the visible order is WARN, WARN, ERROR, WARN. The only item that blocks export is third in a list of four, styled at the same weight as the things that block nothing.

Fix. Implement the ADR sort in the presenter, never in the view. Add a test asserting error-first ordering — this belongs with the existing determinism assertions, since the ADR ordering is part of the deterministic contract that produces `ReportHash`.

## UX-03 — Shipped findings show codes only

Surface: shipped panel.

`BuildFindingsLines()` (`ScenarioMapAuthoringWindow.cs:605-619`) emits `LastCodes[i]` and nothing else. `FillScroll` (`:621-643`) applies a uniform `scenario-map-list-item` class to every row (USS `:281-286`). So the panel renders `MISSION_NO_UNITS` as a bare string — no severity, no indication of which mission, no message.

Severity here is not colour-only. It is absent.

Fix. Adopt the mock's row anatomy, which is already correct in shape: `[severity glyph + label] [code] [entity chip] [human message] [action]`. This is the one place where the mock should be treated as the specification and ported into the panel more or less as drawn.

## UX-04 — Findings are dead ends

Surface: both.

Neither surface lets you act on a finding. The mock names what (code + message) and where (`strike-1`, right-aligned, the lowest-contrast element on the row), but there is no way to click through to the offending entity, and no fix affordance. The GDD promises what, where, and how to fix it. We currently deliver what.

Fix.

- Whole row clickable: select the entity, reveal it on the map, focus the offending field in the inspector.
- Surface structured finding data inline instead of prose. `STRIKE_UNREACHABLE` carries `Data["excess_nm"]` — render "38 nm beyond combat radius", not "Target hostile-1 beyond combat\_radius\_nm".
- Offer a deterministic remedy where the rule has one (reposition launch base, assign units, add a third waypoint to a degenerate patrol zone).
- Promote the entity id from a right-aligned afterthought to a leading chip. It is the where, and it is currently the weakest element on the row.

## UX-05 — No Undo/Redo, despite a disk-backed undo stack

Surface: shipped panel.

Zero occurrences of `undo` or `redo` in the window, the UXML, or the USS. The backend is fully built: `ScenarioUndoStackStore.cs:54` writes a `.undo-stack.json` sidecar, `ScenarioEditCommandBus.cs:180-195` captures a snapshot per mutation, and the CLI exposes `scenario_undo`. None of it is reachable from the panel.

This is a data-loss risk, made worse by naming: the only recovery-shaped controls visible are Rebuild and Refresh, both of which read as discard my work.

Fix. Undo/Redo buttons plus ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z, with the undo label naming the last action ("Undo Place Unit"). Rename Rebuild to "Reload from disk" and confirm when the document is dirty.

## UX-06 — No keyboard model

Surface: both.

- No `KeyDownEvent`, no `OnGUI`, no `Event.current` handling anywhere in the window.
- Six `[MenuItem]` entries, none carrying a shortcut suffix.
- No `:focus` rule in either USS file — `ScenarioMapAuthoringPanel.uss` or `AegisTokens.uss`. Only `:hover` (`:152`, `:222`) and a `:disabled` opacity rule (`:227`).
- No tab order, no `tooltip` attribute anywhere in UXML or code.
- `WireButton` sets `focusable = true` programmatically (`:349`) — the single accessibility affordance in the panel — and then calls `StopPropagation()` on ClickEvent (`:369`).

The project standard requires keyboard-only navigation to be fully specified for PC targets. Nothing here is specified.

Fix. A visible focus ring token at 2px with ≥3:1 contrast against both the base surface and `--selected-row-bg`; F6 region cycling (chrome → tabs → timeline → inspector → findings); ↑/↓ + Enter through findings; ⌘S / ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z / ⌘F; a `?` shortcut sheet.

## UX-07 — Implementation vocabulary dominates the interface

> ⚠️ Partially retracted, 2026-07-26. These mocks are committed documentation artifacts generated from a GitNexus query (the Platform Editor equivalent is `docs/superpowers/reviews/platform-editor-uiux-preview.html`). The TRACE row and pipeline footer are provenance chrome for a generated document, not proposed product UI, so criticising them as interface copy mistakes a design artifact for a screen.

>

> What survives: the trace chrome must not be carried into the product, and the "Copy as CLI command" suggestion below stands on its own merits. The finding's severity should be read as advisory, not blocking.

Surface: mock.

Counted on one screen: a TRACE row of nine C# symbols; `BUS COMMIT: MissionUpdatePatrolCommand → ScenarioDocumentEditor.RequireEditVersion` sitting inside an editing form; `LiveFindingsPresenter.RefreshImmediate` in the findings header; a CLI-parity footer; and finding messages carrying `(MissionBoardPresenterTests pattern)` and `(test parity)`.

For a tool whose stated fantasy is theater designer, the most prominent text on screen is the call graph. The domain — patrols, strikes, ferries, ROE — is the smallest text on screen.

Fix. Collapse all of it into a "Developer / trace" drawer, closed by default.

Then replace the passive CLI-parity footer with an active "Copy as CLI command" on each mutation. Same information, now a feature: it gives designers a scriptable path, it makes the mutation legible, and it reinforces ADR-017's premise that the core is the system of record and every UI is a thin front-end over it. The footer currently asserts that premise; the button would demonstrate it.

## UX-08 — Dead center canvas

Surface: mock.

Roughly 45% of the viewport — everything between the session header and the timeline table — is empty, while the TIMELINE tab's primary content is confined to a \~90px strip with its own nested scrollbar inside an already-scrolling page. Three scroll regions, no visible boundaries between them.

Fix. The active tab owns the center region; the timeline expands to fill it. One scroll context per region, with explicit boundaries. The findings dock becomes collapsible with a persistent count in its header so it can yield space without disappearing.

---

# Should fix

## UX-09 — Dirty state is under-weighted

`• unsaved` is mid-gray, inside a breadcrumb where the title, path, dirty flag, edit version, and findings count all carry equal visual weight. The panel has the same flat treatment across `scenario-session-path`, `-edit-version`, and `-dirty` labels.

Fix. Title becomes "Baltic Patrol" at a real title size, path demoted to a secondary line or tooltip. Dirty state gets an accent dot on the title, and SAVE takes primary button styling when dirty, muted when clean. Hide `editVersion` in the normal flow — see UX-10 for where it belongs.

## UX-10 — No conflict UI

A stale `--edit-version` raises `ScenarioEditConflictException` with `currentEditVersion` and `fileHash`, exit 3, before any write. There is no dialog for this in either surface. This is the single moment when `editVersion` becomes meaningful to a human, and it is unhandled.

Fix. A reconcile dialog: "This scenario changed on disk — you have v2, disk has v3", with Reload / Keep mine / Show diff. `scenario_diff_summary` already exists to power the third option.

## UX-11 — Contrast, type scale, disabled state

The panel uses only three sizes: 10px, 11px, and 13px. Nothing establishes a title. `--text-muted: #8C9BAA` on `--surface-deep: #080E16` needs measuring, as do the mock's description paragraph, footer, and table header row — several look sub-AA. Disabled state is `opacity: 0.45` (USS `:227-229`), which drops contrast below threshold and communicates no reason.

Fix. Measure every foreground/background pair against WCAG AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 UI and status). Introduce a three-step type scale with a genuine page title. Replace opacity-only disabled with an explicit token pair plus a tooltip reason — which UX-01 needs anyway.

## UX-12 — Colour-only severity in counters and row tint

The mock's badges carry text (ERROR / WARN), which is correct. But the count chips and the row-level tint are colour-only, and amber against red is a poor pairing under deuteranopia — the two most important states are the two hardest to separate.

Fix. A distinct glyph per severity (✕ / ⚠ / ℹ) alongside the existing text label, and a colourblind simulation pass over the findings dock.

## UX-13 — Hover, selected, and focus share one fill

`.scenario-map-platform-row:hover` and `.scenario-map-platform-row--selected` both resolve to `var(--selected-row-bg)` (USS `:152-161`), and no focus style exists at all. Three distinct states, one appearance.

Fix. Hover subtle; selected = fill plus a left marker bar; focus = ring, per UX-06. Selection must remain visible when the region loses focus.

## UX-14 — Two chip vocabularies, one appearance

`ALL | ERRORS | WARNINGS | 1 ERROR | 3 WARNINGS` renders as five near-identical pills — three filters and two counters that read as five filters.

Fix. One row of filters carrying their own counts: `All 4 · Errors 1 · Warnings 3`, with an unmistakable selected state.

## UX-15 — Raw ticks as user-facing time

`T+0`, `T+120`, `T+3600`. Scenario designers think in mission time.

Fix. `T+00:00:00` as the primary display, raw tick as a secondary column or on hover. The sim stays tick-authoritative; only the display changes.

## UX-16 — "Timeline" is a table

Nothing in the timeline view conveys density, clustering, or gaps — yet ADR-016 defines a `peak_tick_density` warning that fires above 20 events in a tick. The designer has no way to see the condition approaching.

Fix. A horizontal density strip above the table: tick axis, event-count bars, and a threshold line drawn at the configured `densityWarnThreshold`. This makes an abstract warning into a visible slope, before it fires.

## UX-17 — Inspector clipped, untitled, ambiguous

The right panel is cut mid-field at its top edge, its scrollbar begins above the visible area, and it has no header — there is no way to tell which object is being edited. `RoeOverride` with placeholder `inherit sideRoe` puts camelCase identifiers in front of designers.

The ROE point deserves emphasis beyond labelling: inherited-versus-overridden rules of engagement is a command-safety distinction in a military simulation. Encoding it as "the placeholder text is showing" is too subtle for the consequence.

Fix. Panel header with entity type, id, and side. Scroll container starts below the header. Human labels with helper text ("Inherits from side ROE if empty"). An explicit two-state control that reads unambiguously as Inherited from side or Overridden.

## UX-18 — Contextual actions enabled out of context

CLONE SELECTED is enabled on the TIMELINE tab with no visible selection. On the panel side, `ShouldEnableCatalogAndFormChrome` returns `true` unconditionally (`ScenarioMapAuthoringHostPolicy.cs:31`), so the whole placement form is live with no session open — the user can fill it in completely before learning it does nothing.

Fix. Disable-with-reason throughout, consistent with UX-01. Selection-scoped actions live in the surface that owns the selection.

## UX-19 — Panel USS bypasses its own tokens

Three hardcoded literals despite `@import url("../AegisTokens.uss")` at `:5` — `rgba(74, 158, 255, 0.22)` (`:122`), `rgba(16, 24, 36, 0.4)` (`:149`), `rgba(74, 158, 255, 0.28)` (`:232`). Two of the three are near-duplicates of `--selected-row-bg`, which is exactly the drift tokens exist to prevent.

Fix. Promote to tokens. Add a lint gate rejecting raw colour literals in panel USS — cheap to add now, before more panels land.

---

# Backlog — surfaces the spec implies and the UI lacks

UX-20 — Determinism is invisible. `metadata.seed` (default 42) is never shown, and there is no sample-run action, though `scenario_simulate_sample` emits `SEED=… HASH=…` over 32 ticks. For a project where reproducibility is a gating property, the editor should display the seed and offer "Sample run (32 ticks)" with its hash.

UX-21 — No catalog binding indicator. `DB_MISMATCH` and `BROKEN_REF` are among the most common failure modes, and the bound `dbRef` / `dbSnapshotId` is shown nowhere. Note that `ScenarioValidateCommand.ResolveCatalog` silently falls back to `InMemoryCatalogReader.BalticPatrolFixture()` — a designer can be validating against a fixture without knowing it.

UX-22 — No TL branch indicator. `metadata.tlBranch` (TL-0…TL-5) and `maxTechnologyLevel` gate publish via `TL_BRANCH_*` errors, with no display.

UX-23 — No provenance display. Every output carries `ManifestBuilder.ProvenanceTag` with `Source ∈ {user, ai, import}`, surviving into the published manifest. ADR-015 (Proposed, decision due 2026-09-01) would derive an agent-authored label from it. That ADR will need this surface to exist; designing it now is cheaper than retrofitting.

---

# Recommended sequencing

Wave 1 — make the gate real. UX-01, UX-02, UX-03, UX-04. These are one coherent piece of work: extend `LiveFindingsPresenter` with severity counts and a `CanExport` flag, fix the ADR-008 sort, port the mock's finding-row anatomy into the panel, and wire row-click navigation. Mostly presenter work, fully testable headless, and it converts the product's stated differentiator from a claim into a visible behaviour.

Wave 2 — safety and input. UX-05, UX-06, UX-09, UX-10, UX-18. Undo/redo, the keyboard model and focus ring, dirty-state weighting, and the conflict dialog. This is the wave that stops users losing work.

Wave 3 — legibility and craft. UX-07, UX-08, UX-11 through UX-17, UX-19. Layout, contrast, tokens, the timeline density strip, the inspector header.

Backlog. UX-20 through UX-23, sequenced against ADR-015's 2026-09-01 decision date.

---

> OPEN QUESTION: Is ME-W1 (the mock) intended to become the Unity panel, a separate web front-end, or a design study only? The answer changes UX-03 substantially — if the mock ships as its own front-end, the panel needs its own port of the finding-row work rather than inheriting it.

> OPEN QUESTION: ADR-008 gates export on findings, and `EditModeController.TryEnterPlay` gates play. Are these intended to be the same gate with two entry points, or two policies? They are currently implemented separately and neither is reachable from the panel, so the question has not had to be answered yet.

pages.title: 🎛️ Main Game Window — Proposed C2 UI Requirements (CMD-16…CMD-28)
pages.content:
Source: `Game-Requirements/requirements/20-Command-And-Control-UI.md`
Req IDs: CMD-16..CMD-30
Lifecycle: Draft — canonical home pending owner land decision (landed delta in REQ-20)
Linear: [DRG-192](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-192) · [DRG-272](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-272) · [DRG-849](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-849) · DRG-850 · DRG-870 · DRG-895 · DRG-896

---

Type: Requirements proposal — amendments to REQ-20, not a replacement

Status: Draft — for owner triage

Date: 2026-07-26

Canonical home: `Game-Requirements/requirements/20-Command-And-Control-UI.md` — if accepted, these land there, not here

Method: Reference-product analysis (CMO v1.01 build 1121.8 main window) diffed against existing Aegis specs

Related Linear Milestone: H1 — C2 Runtime Depth

## Read this first — what this is not

The main game window is already specified, and specified well. Before proposing anything I read:

- `Game-Requirements/requirements/20-Command-And-Control-UI.md` — 202 lines, CMD-01…CMD-15, layout zones, NFRs, acceptance criteria, phased delivery, and an honest per-row status column
- `design/ux/c2-command-post.md` — 175-line UX spec with wireframe, zone sizes, state table, interaction map, data sources
- `design/gdd/command-and-control-ui.md`, `docs/architecture/adr-007-c2-map-presentation.md`

REQ-20 is explicitly derived from the CMO manual (Ch 3–4, §6.2–7, §6.9, §1.3, §10.1) — the same product this analysis looks at. So a fresh "UX/UI requirements" page would duplicate it and create a competing source of truth, which the wiki's own rule forbids.

What follows is only the delta: things visible in the reference product that neither REQ-20 nor the UX spec currently requires. Eight proposals, numbered to continue REQ-20's scheme.

## Already covered — do not re-file these

So the next reader doesn't repeat the analysis: REQ-20 already requires persistent layout zones (CMD-01), UI Toolkit stack (CMD-02), headless command-driven binding (CMD-03), top bar with time/compression/pause (CMD-04), message log with sequence deep-link (CMD-05), map symbol picture (CMD-06), map↔OOB↔panel selection sync (CMD-07), doctrine inheritance panel (CMD-08), delegation badges (CMD-09), context menus (CMD-10), intent preview / FireAbort explain (CMD-11), colorblind-safe affiliation and keyboard focus (CMD-12), and defers the product globe, multitasker, and 5k@60 to Phase N (CMD-13–15).

---

# Proposed requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Why it is missing today |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CMD-17 | Unknown-due-to-comms as a first-class display state | P0 | Sim models it; UI has no representation |
| CMD-19 | Per-axis manual / auto delegation control | P0 | Delegation specified at unit granularity only |
| CMD-20 | Map scale bar + camera altitude readout | P0 | Not mentioned in any spec |
| CMD-21 | Selected-unit sensor / weapon envelope rings | P0 | At risk of deferring with Phase N EW overlays |
| CMD-18 | Domain-appropriate discrete alt / depth / throttle presets | P1 | Alt/speed specified as data, not as commands |
| CMD-16 | Persistent unit-order toolbar | P1 | Only context menus are specified |
| CMD-22 | Zulu / local / remaining scenario time | P1 | "Time" specified without disambiguation |
| CMD-23 | Collapsible non-primary zones | P2 | Zones specified as fixed-height and always present |

---

## CMD-17 — Unknown-due-to-comms is a first-class display state [P0]

Requirement. Where a unit's telemetry is unavailable because the unit is out of comms, the UI shall render an explicit unknown state that names the cause, visually distinct from zero, blank, and last-known-value.

Reference evidence. The unit panel shows `Course: XXX`, `Speed: XXX`, `Altitude: XXX`, and `Status: UNKNOWN (Out of comms)`. The submarine is selected and on the map — the player simply cannot talk to it.

Why this is the most important item here. Aegis already models comms degradation (`docs/engineering/comms-degradation-runtime.md`, requirements doc 19), and REQ-20 mentions a COMMS legend — but nothing specifies how a panel renders data it cannot obtain. A blank field reads as "no data / UI bug." `XXX (Out of comms)` reads as "the link is down" — which is a tactical fact the player must act on. Getting this wrong silently converts a modelled game system into an apparent defect.

Must also settle: whether last-known values are shown with an age stamp ("Course 270 · 4m stale") or suppressed entirely. These are different games — the first supports dead reckoning, the second forces reacquisition.

## CMD-19 — Per-axis manual / auto delegation [P0]

Requirement. Each independently commandable axis (depth/altitude, throttle, EMCON, sensors) shall expose its own manual-versus-automatic control, and its current mode shall be readable without opening a menu.

Reference evidence. The unit panel carries a separate `Manual | Set Auto` pair for Alt and for Throttle — two axes, two independent autonomy switches.

Why it matters for Aegis specifically. REQ-20's CMD-09 models delegation at unit granularity — a badge reading human, agent, or mixed. But "mixed" is exactly the interesting case and the badge cannot express it: a unit may be under agent speed control while the human holds depth, or running autonomous EMCON under manual maneuvering. Agent delegation is this project's stated differentiator, and the control surface for it is currently coarser than the reference product's.

This likely also implies a projection change — per-axis autonomy state has to reach the panel.

## CMD-20 — Map scale and camera altitude [P0]

Requirement. The map shall persistently display a distance scale in nautical miles and the current camera altitude.

Reference evidence. A nautical-mile scale bar sits bottom-right; `Camera Alt: 867550m` sits in the status line.

Why. Range is the primary spatial judgement in this genre — every engagement decision is "can I reach it, can it reach me." A theater map without a scale cannot support that read. Neither REQ-20 nor the UX spec mentions a scale indicator; this looks like a simple omission rather than a decision, which is why it is worth filing explicitly.

## CMD-21 — Selected-unit envelope rings [P0]

Requirement. On selection, the map shall render the unit's sensor and weapon envelopes as visually distinguishable range rings.

Reference evidence. The selected submarine carries several concentric rings in distinct colours — detection and engagement envelopes read at a glance.

Why file it separately. REQ-20 defers "full EW overlay product layers" to Phase N. Own-unit envelope rings are not an EW overlay — they are the baseline read that makes a selection meaningful. The risk is that the baseline gets deferred along with the advanced feature because both are described as "overlays." This requirement exists to prevent that bundling.

## CMD-18 — Domain-appropriate discrete presets [P1]

Requirement. Altitude/depth and throttle shall be commandable as named doctrinal states appropriate to the platform's domain, not solely as numeric entry.

Reference evidence. The submarine panel offers depth as `Surface · Periscope depth · Shallow · Just over the layer · Just under the layer · As deep as possible`, and throttle as `Stop · Creep · Cruise · Full · Flank`.

Why. "Just under the layer" is not a depth — it is a thermocline-relative acoustic decision whose numeric value changes with water conditions. The named command carries tactical intent that a number cannot, and it is the correct unit of delegation to an agent. Likewise `Creep` is a quieting decision, not a speed. REQ-20 lists "alt/speed" as panel data; this proposes it as a command vocabulary.

Open: preset sets differ per domain (subsurface / air / surface / ground) and need a catalog source rather than hardcoding.

## CMD-16 — Persistent unit-order toolbar [P1]

Requirement. The main window shall present a persistent toolbar exposing primary unit-order actions for the current selection, in addition to context menus.

Reference evidence. Twelve always-visible order groups: Auto/Manual Engage Target, Plot Course, Throttle & Altitude, Formation Editor, Magazines, Aircraft Operations, Boat Operations, Mounts & Weapons, Sensors, Systems & Damage, Unit/Group Doctrine, Mission Editor.

Why. REQ-20's CMD-10 specifies context menus, and neither its zone table nor the UX spec's wireframe includes a toolbar. Context-menu-only means every one of a dozen order verbs is discoverable exclusively by right-clicking the correct object — a heavy discovery burden for new players and a lot of hidden surface for a command post. The reference product provides both paths deliberately.

Caveat, from this session's reviews: a flat wall of twelve buttons is itself a legibility problem. Adopt the redundancy, not the layout — group by domain and reflect selection context.

## CMD-22 — Zulu, local, and remaining time [P1]

Requirement. The top bar shall display scenario date, Zulu time, local time, and remaining scenario duration.

Reference evidence. `Time: Monday, October 9, 2000 · Zulu: 11:00:00 · Local: 14:00:00 · 1 d to go`.

Why. REQ-20's CMD-04 specifies "time" without disambiguation, and the UX spec wireframes a single `TIME 00:42:10`. Zulu-versus-local is doctrinal in coalition operations and drives day/night reasoning; remaining-duration frames session pacing. Cheap to add, awkward to retrofit once the top bar is dense.

Also observed: the reference offers time compression as time-per-step (15 sec / 1 min / 5 min / 15 min) alongside a multiplier. Aegis specifies multipliers only (`1x 4x 8x`, hotkeys 1–4). Those are different mental models — worth a deliberate choice rather than an inherited one.

## CMD-23 — Collapsible non-primary zones [P2]

Requirement. Message log and left drawer shall be collapsible to a title affordance, with state persisted across sessions.

Reference evidence. The message log is collapsed to a title bar with an expand control, returning its area to the map.

Why. The UX spec fixes the bottom log at 120px and REQ-20 treats zones as always-present. Over multi-hour sessions the map is the scarce resource, and the log matters intensely but intermittently.

---

## CMD-24 — Air Operations window [P1, phased]

Requirement. The C2 client shall provide an Air Operations window, opened from the unit-order toolbar (CMD-16), presenting the air assets hosted across the current selection, their readiness, loadout feasibility, and mission-assignment actions.

Reference evidence. A modal titled "Air Ops — Multiple host units" with tabs Aircraft Status / Air Facilities; a table of `Aircraft · Status · Mission · Loadout · Time to ready · Quick`; a stores panel showing magazine availability; and an action bar of `Launch Individually · Launch as group(s) · Ready/Arm · Abort Launch · Doctrine · Assign to mission · Unload Cargo`.

Why it is missing. REQ-20 has zero mentions of aircraft, launch, sortie, hangar or deck. The CMO toolbar surfaces Aircraft Operations and Boat Operations as first-class order groups; REQ-20's parity table has no row for either.

### ⚠️ This requirement is gated by REQ-16, and must be phased accordingly

This is the crux. `Game-Requirements/requirements/16-Logistics-And-Magazines.md` is unusually honest about what exists:

> "Not shipped: full air-ops FSM, UNREP, live magazines C2 panel, product MCP logistics tools."

>

> "Air-ops FSM (taxi/takeoff/land/maint) — Phase N — Boolean readiness only on `main`."

| Model | REQ-16 status | Can the UI show it? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Magazine ledger consume (`MagazineLedger`) | Shipped | Yes |
| Fuel burn / bands, per-domain fuel types (aviation JP) | Shipped / P0 | Yes |
| Boolean `ReadyForLaunch` → `AIR_NOT_READY` (`UnitReadinessMap`) | Shipped | Yes — binary only |
| Ferry missions moving aircraft between bases | Shipped (CLI + validation) | Yes |
| Air-ops FSM — taxi / takeoff / land / maintenance | Phase N | No |
| Deck cycle, sortie generation rate | Phase N | No |
| Composite `readinessScore` | Phase N | No — boolean only |
| UNREP / underway rearm | Phase N | No |

A "Time to ready" column cannot be populated, because no state machine produces a time. Rendering it empty, or with a fabricated value, repeats the exact failure documented in the [Scenario Editor W2 review](https://app.notion.com/p/3aaf7cb4e4df81d58626cdda26db28eb) (W2-02), where a mock advertised a 300 ms validation debounce that `LiveFindingsPresenter` stores and never honours. An absent column is honest; an empty one is a bug report; a fabricated one is a lie.

### Phase A — buildable today against the shipped spine

- CMD-24.1 — Cross-host aggregation. List air assets across all units in the current selection, grouped by type and host with counts (`12x F/A-18A Hornet (CVN 70 Carl Vinson)`). The reference aggregates a carrier, a cruiser, a frigate and a supply ship into one list — the player commands the group's air assets, not each deck separately. This is the window's single most important structural idea and it costs nothing extra to adopt.
- CMD-24.2 — Binary readiness with an explicit cause. Show `ReadyForLaunch`, and where false, name the reason using the same `AIR_NOT_READY` vocabulary the engage gate already emits — so the window and the engage refusal agree word-for-word.
- CMD-24.3 — Magazine-constrained loadout feasibility. For a selected loadout, show how many airframes can be armed from current stock. The reference does this well: `# Available Magazines` alongside `# Available Mags + A/C` answers "how many sorties can I actually arm?" rather than "how much do I have?" This is directly implementable on the shipped `MagazineLedger`.
- CMD-24.4 — Aviation fuel shown distinctly from platform fuel (REQ-16 P0: per-domain fuel types). The reference states it as its own line: `0.0 fuel units remaining (Aviation Fuel)`.
- CMD-24.5 — Assign to mission, bridging air assets to the mission system (doc 11).
- CMD-24.6 — Aggregate ready count in group status (`Aircraft: 35/71`). One line, high value, no new model needed.

### Phase N — gated on the REQ-16 air-ops FSM

Do not build these ahead of the model: time-to-ready timers; `Launch Individually` vs `Launch as group(s)`; `Abort Launch` (requires an in-progress launch state); the Air Facilities tab (deck / hangar / runway capacity and deck cycle); and per-airframe drill-down beyond type aggregation.

When the FSM lands, these should arrive together — a launch button without an abort is worse than neither.

### Do not inherit this defect

In the reference, the entire action bar is disabled with only `Loadout Details: None Selected` as explanation. Which action needs what is left to inference. Per the disabled-with-reason pattern established in the editor reviews, each disabled action should carry its own reason — "select a loadout" differs from "no ready airframes" differs from "magazine stock insufficient."

### Projection dependency

REQ-16 lists `logistics_get_readiness` and `logistics_project_sorties` as MCP Gap — not shipped. The same data has to reach this panel, so CMD-24 likely implies a new read-only projection under ADR-010 rather than view work alone. Worth confirming before estimating.

## CMD-25 — Boat Operations window [P2 — blocked on domain model]

Requirement. The C2 client shall provide a Boat Operations window, opened from the unit-order toolbar (CMD-16), presenting embarked small craft across the current selection, their readiness, and their tasking.

### ⚠️ Epistemic note — what this is and is not based on

I have not seen this window. No screenshot of CMO's Boat Operations dialog was reviewed. What is actually grounded:

- A Boat Operations toolbar button sits beside Aircraft Operations in the reference product's order bar (visible in two screenshots)
- Group status pairs `Boats: 2/2` with `Aircraft: 35/71` — the same ready-over-total treatment
- REQ-16 maps boat ops to CMO manual §3.3.8 and scopes it P1

The existence and rough role of the window are grounded. Its contents are not. Any detailed layout below the requirement statement would be invention, so there isn't one — deliberately.

### The actual finding — the domain is unspecified, not just unbuilt

CMD-24 was gated on a Phase-N state machine, but at least stood on a shipped spine (`MagazineLedger`, boolean `ReadyForLaunch`, fuel bands, ferry hooks). Boat operations has no such floor.

REQ-16 contains a section literally titled "Boat and Naval Operations". Its entire content is three bullets:

>  P1 UNREP for fuel and limited rearm → Phase N\*

>  P0 Docked / underway replenishment affects readiness flags → Partial / Phase N\*

>  P0 Submarine battery/charge model (simplified) → Phase N\*

That is replenishment and submarine power. None of it is about launching, recovering, or tasking boats. The section heading promises a domain the section does not specify.

Corroborating checks:

| Source | Boat operations coverage |
| --- | --- |
| REQ-16 §Boat and Naval Operations | UNREP / replenishment / sub battery only — no launch, recovery, or tasking |
| REQ-18 Combat Domains | Zero hits for boat, small craft, amphibious, littoral |
| REQ-20 C2 UI | No mention |
| `src/` sim model | No boat / craft / amphibious / boarding type exists |
| Sea state / weather model | Not modelled — "sea state" appears only in REQ-15 sensor/EW context |

Recommendation: specify the domain before the UI. A window spec written now would be interface over vapour at two levels — no model and no domain requirements. The productive next step is amending REQ-16 §Boat and Naval Operations to actually cover boat operations, then deriving this window from it.

### Why cloning CMD-24 would be wrong

The symmetry of the toolbar buttons is misleading. Boats differ from aircraft in ways that change the interface, and a copied spec would encode the wrong model:

- Recovery is the hard operation, not launch. Aircraft recovery is gated by deck cycle; boat recovery is gated by sea state and mothership manoeuvring, and a boat that cannot be recovered is a stranded crew, not a diverted airframe. The window's centre of gravity is different.
- Sea state gates the operation — and Aegis has no weather or sea-state model at all. This is a hard dependency air ops does not have.
- Cargo and personnel, not weapon loadouts. CMD-24.3's magazine-feasibility idea has no boat analogue; the equivalent question is who and what is embarked.
- Counts are small. `Boats: 2/2` versus `Aircraft: 35/71` — type-aggregated rows (`12x F/A-18A Hornet`) are the right unit for air and the wrong one for boats, where each hull is individually tracked and named.
- Boarding / VBSS is a mission type, not a launch action — it needs mission-system integration (doc 11) rather than an ops-window button.

### Scoping note worth raising

The reference scenario is anti-piracy — the map carries a "Suspected Pirate Staging Area" label and hostile small craft. In that scenario class, boarding operations are the primary tactical activity, not a supporting one. If Aegis intends to support littoral or counter-piracy scenarios, P1/P2 understates boat operations and the priority deserves revisiting on scenario grounds rather than parity grounds.

### Phase A — what is genuinely buildable today

Almost nothing, honestly:

- CMD-25.1 — Embarked-craft ready count in group status (`Boats: 2/2`), mirroring CMD-24.6. This is a readout, needs no FSM, and is the only piece not blocked.

Everything else waits on a domain model that does not exist yet.

## CMD-26 — Ground Operations window [P2 — scoped to brigade+; battalion depth is out of charter]

Requirement. The C2 client shall provide a Ground Operations window presenting friendly and known-hostile ground formations at brigade echelon and above, their aggregate strength and readiness, their air-defence contribution, and their tasking — within the charter scope defined by doc 01.

### ⚠️ Scope finding — read before designing anything

The requested echelon list runs division → brigade → regiment → battalion. The project charter already draws a line inside that list, and it is not a "not yet" — it is an explicit exclusion.

`Game-Requirements/requirements/01-Project-Overview.md`:

> In scope (line 82): "Air, naval, and aggregate-level ground (brigade+) for air/naval interaction"

>

> Out of scope (line 90): "Land warfare at battalion scale or below"

Echoed normatively in REQ-18 §Land Combat (Limited): "Per doc 01 scope: strategic facilities and IADS, not battalion tactics."

| Echelon | Charter status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Division | In scope | Aggregate formation |
| Brigade | In scope | The boundary, inclusive — "brigade+" |
| Regiment | Needs a decision | Brigade-equivalent in US/NATO and Soviet-pattern usage, so probably in scope — but the charter says "brigade+", not "brigade-equivalent+". Worth resolving explicitly rather than by assumption. |
| Battalion | Out of charter | doc 01 line 90 excludes battalion scale and below by name |

### The structural consequence — the TO&E tree is shallow, by design

This is the finding that actually shapes the interface, and it is easy to miss.

A TO&E window is usually a deep tree: division contains brigades, which contain battalions, which contain companies. But if the charter caps modelling at brigade+, then a brigade is a leaf, not a container. The hierarchy the request implies only has depth if battalions exist as modelled entities — and they explicitly do not.

So the in-scope window is two or three levels deep at most:

```javascript
Division
└─ Brigade / Regiment        ← leaf: aggregate strength, readiness, ADA contribution
   └─ (battalions: out of charter)
```

Designing a deep expandable TO&E tree would build interface for a hierarchy the sim will never populate — the same class of error as CMD-24's `Time to ready` column and the W2-02 debounce chip. Aggregate rows with no expander are the honest shape under current charter.

### What exists today

| Capability | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `CombatDomain.Land` enum + `LandAspectDomainValidator` | Shipped spine / Partial aspect gate |
| Ground platform presets in the scenario editor | Shipped — but they are IADS and facilities: Patriot PAC-3, M901 launcher, S-400, RBS-15 coastal battery, air base, port |
| Tactical Group model (`GroupTarget`, `DetachRejoinService`, detach/rejoin records) | Shipped |
| Echelon / TO&E / organisational hierarchy type | Does not exist — no `Echelon`, `Formation`, `Brigade`, `Battalion` type in `src/` |
| Full land IADS / battalion-scale combat | Phase N (REQ-18) |

Note what the shipped ground presets are: every one is an air-defence system, a coastal battery, or a facility. That is precisely the charter's "strategic facilities and IADS" — the ground domain today is things that shoot at aircraft and things aircraft shoot at, not manoeuvre forces.

### TO&E is not the tactical Group model — do not conflate them

Aegis has a Group concept with detach and rejoin. That is a transient tactical association — units operating together now, formed and dissolved at will, mirroring CMO's naval groups.

TO&E is permanent organisational subordination — a battalion belongs to its brigade whether or not they are co-located, and that relationship survives detachment. The two answer different questions ("who is manoeuvring together" vs "who does this belong to") and a ground window needs the second, which does not exist.

Reusing `GroupTarget` for echelon structure would silently make organisational hierarchy dissolvable, which is wrong.

### Phase A — buildable within the current charter

- CMD-26.1 — Aggregate ground formation list at brigade+ with side, type, and location. Flat or two-level; no battalion expander.
- CMD-26.2 — Air-defence contribution per formation — which IADS assets it fields, their state, and their coverage. This is the charter's stated purpose for modelling ground at all ("for air/naval interaction"), so it is the window's centre of gravity rather than a side panel.
- CMD-26.3 — Facility status — airbase, port, runway damage, and sortie-capacity linkage into REQ-16 (doc 16 already wires runway/sortie capacity where present).
- CMD-26.4 — Aggregate strength / readiness as a single band per formation, not a rolled-up sum of subordinate units — there are no subordinate units to roll up.

### Charter-change path — if battalion depth is genuinely wanted

This cannot be filed as a UI requirement. It would require, in order:

1. Amend doc 01 line 90 — the exclusion is charter-level, and everything downstream inherits it
2. Amend REQ-18 §Land Combat (Limited), which cites doc 01 as its authority
3. Introduce an echelon / TO&E model in `src/` distinct from the tactical Group model
4. Decide the regiment question above
5. Only then derive this window's deep-tree form

That is a significant sim expansion — land manoeuvre warfare is a different game from the air/naval simulation the charter describes. Worth a deliberate product decision, not a requirements edit.

## CMD-27 — Scenario library and load operations [P0]

Requirement. The client shall provide a scenario library surface for browsing, previewing, and loading scenarios and saved games, which states before load whether a scenario will actually run.

### Why P0 — this is the first screen of the game and it is specified nowhere

| Source | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| doc 02 §Core Gameplay Loop | "Phase 1: Scenario Selection & Force Composition" — the loop begins here |
| `design/ux/c2-command-post.md:45` | `Main Menu → **Scenario Select** → Mission Planning → C2 Command Post → AAR` — named in the navigation flow |
| REQ-20 | Zero mentions of load, main menu, front-end, or scenario select |
| `design/ux/` | No main-menu or scenario-select spec (c2-command-post, c2-map-placeholder, interaction-patterns, onboarding-baltic, scenario-editor) |
| `src/`  • CLI | No scenario list/browse verb or projection — `scenario_*` has create / validate / export / publish / simulate / undo / diff / trace, but no list |

Every player's first interaction with the product is a screen that is named twice and designed nowhere.

### The part that is not CMO parity — pre-load feasibility

CMO's Load Scenario dialog lists files. Aegis scenarios are not just files — they are validated, catalog-bound, deterministic artifacts that can fail to load for reasons knowable in advance:

- Catalog binding — `dbRef` / `dbSnapshotId` may not resolve against the installed catalog (`DB_MISMATCH`), and `ref:`-prefixed ids may dangle (`BROKEN_REF`). These are among the most common failure modes in the system.
- Validation state — ADR-008 findings with severity; a scenario can carry blocking errors.
- Schema / version — `scenario-document.schema.json` compatibility and `editVersion`.

CMD-27.1 — Pre-load feasibility. The library shall state, per entry, whether the scenario resolves against the installed catalog and passes validation, before the user commits to loading it.

This is the load-time analogue of the export gate (UX-01 / DRG-56 in the editor reviews). Same principle, different surface: a constraint the system already enforces should be visible before the user hits it, not as a failure afterwards. Listing an unloadable scenario with no indication is the browser equivalent of an unreachable gate.

### Phase A sub-requirements

- CMD-27.2 — Provenance and trust. Distinguish authored / AI-scaffolded / imported (`ManifestBuilder.ProvenanceTag`, `Source ∈ {user, ai, import}`) and bundled / user-saved / third-party. ADR-015 (Proposed, decision due 2026-09-01) would derive an agent-authored label from provenance — this library is where that label becomes visible to a player, and is the natural forcing function for that decision.
- CMD-27.3 — Determinism metadata. Show `metadata.seed`, TL branch (`metadata.tlBranch`), bound policy, and whether a published manifest with `ReportHash` exists. In a project where replay parity is a release gate, "will this reproduce" is a property worth seeing before opening.
- CMD-27.4 — Separate artifact lifecycles. Autosaves, manual saves, and authored scenarios are different classes with different retention and trust; they shall not share one flat list. The reference mixes `Autosave_20sec.scen` through `Autosave_100sec.scen` directly among authored scenarios like `Georgia2008.scen`.
- CMD-27.5 — Search and filter, not only sort. The reference offers a single `Order scenarios by` dropdown. Filter by side, region, duration, validation state, and TL branch.
- CMD-27.6 — Preview pane with a real zero-state. Two further views of this dialog show what actually populates it, in one scrolling region: licence prefix + title, Difficulty and Complexity meters, `Location — Year`, a long briefing, and a rendered map preview. On open, with nothing selected, roughly 40% of the dialog is blank — the zero-state needs instruction, not void.
- CMD-27.7 — Unavailable entries state their reason on the row. ⚠️ Corrected after further views. The padlocked entries are explained — selecting one shows `[NOT LICENSED] Don of a new Era` in red at the top of the preview. So the reason exists; it is just only reachable by selecting each locked item one at a time. The requirement is therefore narrower and cheaper than first written: carry the reason on the list row, so a player sees what they own by scanning rather than by clicking. (Still the third instance of disabled-without-reason in this series — after the editor's greyed actions and the Air Ops action bar — and worth a house rule.)
- CMD-27.8 — Difficulty and Complexity as separate, rated axes. The reference rates both independently, as meters, colour-coded by level (green at low, orange higher). This is a better model than one star rating and worth adopting deliberately: difficulty is how hard the scenario is to win; complexity is how much there is to manage. They are orthogonal — a submarine duel can be hard and simple, a multi-domain operation forgiving and overwhelming.
  
  For Aegis this matters more than for the reference product: agent delegation is the mitigation for complexity, not for difficulty. The library is where that value proposition first becomes legible, so the two axes should be visible before load, not discovered during play.
  

  
  Accessibility: the reference encodes level by bar colour alone. Per CMD-12 (colourblind-safe affiliation), pair the meter with a value or label.
  
- CMD-27.9 — Setting metadata. `Location` and `Year` — the reference shows Ukraine — 2016 and Nova Scotia / Eastern Seaboard — 1975. These are the fields players actually browse by, and they are the natural filter axes for CMD-27.5.
- CMD-27.10 — Briefing is the primary selection content, and it is long. The reference runs several paragraphs of geopolitical background in a scrolling region. Aegis already treats briefings as first-class — `scenario_export_brief` is a shipped CLI verb — so the preview should render the same brief that verb produces, not a separately authored summary. One brief, two surfaces: the CLI/MCP parity principle applied to the library.
- CMD-27.11 — Map preview showing force disposition. The reference renders a real tactical thumbnail — terrain, NATO unit symbols, and place labels (`CFB GREENWOOD`, `HALIFAX`, `HMCS TERRA NOVA`, `HMCS ASSINIBOINE`) — pannable within the preview. You can read the shape of the fight before committing to load.
  
  Aegis can build this cheaply: `MapPictureProjection` and `MapPlaceholderPanelHost` are shipped (REQ-20 CMD-06, ADR-007 Phase A). A scenario preview map is the same projection over an unopened document rather than live sim state — reuse, not new rendering work.
  
- CMD-27.12 — Campaigns are an artifact class, not a folder. The `Northern Inferno` node expands to 15 numbered, dated scenarios running `1. Opening Moves 07 Aug 1975` through `15. Fail Safe 20 Oct 1975` — an ordered chain with narrative progression, not a bag of unrelated files. `Chains Of War` is another. The library must model campaign membership, sequence, and completion state; treating a campaign as a directory loses all three.

### Do not inherit

- File extensions in the UI. `.scen` is an implementation detail; Aegis uses `*.scenario.json`. Show scenario titles, with paths secondary — the same demotion CMD-09 needs in the editor chrome.
- Mixed hierarchy. The reference places expandable folders and flat files at the same level, so `Tutorials ▸` and `Rumble.scen` are siblings with different affordances.
- Ordering encoded in filenames. Campaign sequence is carried by a `1.` … `15.` prefix and the date embedded in each name (`Needle in a Hay Stack 19 Oct 1975.scen`). Sequence and in-fiction date are metadata, not naming convention — encoding them in filenames makes reordering a rename, breaks sorting the moment someone omits a leading zero, and forces the extension-hiding rule above to fight the ordering scheme.

### Dependency — this is not view-only work

There is no scenario list/browse verb or projection. Under ADR-010 (headless-first, command-driven), a browse surface needs a read-only projection, and under the CLI/MCP parity principle it should have a headless equivalent — likely `scenario_list` alongside the existing `scenario_*` verbs. Confirm before estimating.

## CMD-28 — Menu system, map layers, and view tools [P1]

Requirement. The client shall provide a menu system exposing view control, map layer selection, spatial tools, and window management — and it shall be the discovery surface for keyboard shortcuts.

Reference evidence. The View menu carries, in one flat list: `Toggle Full-screen / Windowed  Alt+Enter`, `Zoom In  Z`, `Zoom Out  X`, `Pan Map ▸`, `Select Next Unit  |`, `Select Previous Unit  Backspace`, `Range / Bearing Tool  Ctrl+D`, `Message Log in Separate Window`, `Map Lat/Lon Grid`, then ten basemap layers (`Sentinel-2`, ✓`BMNG`, `Relief`, ✓`Borders + Coastlines`, `Stamen — Terrain`, `Stamen — Roads + Cities`, `Land Cover`, `Custom Layers`, `Placenames`, `Day + Night Lighting`), and `3D View`.

### The gap

REQ-20 specifies no menu bar at all. Keyboard shortcuts appear once in the parity table (§10.1, P1 — Open), custom overlays once (§10.2, P2 — Phase N). There is no mention of fullscreen, zoom controls, a measurement tool, a coordinate grid, a 3D toggle, or basemap layers.

### CMD-28.1 — The menu is how shortcuts become discoverable

Every item in the reference displays its binding inline. REQ-20 already wants keyboard shortcuts (§10.1) and the editor reviews found zero `:focus` rules in the shipped USS — but a shortcut nobody can find is not a feature. The menu is the discovery mechanism, and specifying shortcuts without specifying where they are advertised leaves them unusable.

Pairs with the `?` shortcut sheet proposed in the [ME-W1 review](https://app.notion.com/p/3a9f7cb4e4df8151ae42d2b0a065683e) (UX-06).

### CMD-28.2 — Basemap layer stack — an architectural gap, not a menu item

Ten independently toggleable layers with persisted checked state. Aegis has no layer model. ADR-007 phases map presentation (Phase A placeholder → Phase B Cesium → Phase C APP-6 LOD) but never mentions a layer stack; `src/` has no `MapLayer` / `Basemap` / overlay-stack type.

This needs a decision before it needs a menu:

- Which layers exist, and are they fixed or extensible (`Custom Layers` implies extensible)?
- Who owns visibility state? Under ADR-010 everything else is a projection from the headless core — but layer visibility is pure presentation with no sim meaning. It should almost certainly be UI-local, and that exception is worth stating explicitly rather than discovering later.
- Do layers persist per user, per scenario, or not at all?

### CMD-28.3 — View-state actions are exempt from CLI/MCP parity; command actions are not

This menu makes a boundary explicit that the project will otherwise settle ad hoc.

- View state — zoom, pan, layers, grid, fullscreen, 3D toggle — changes only what this operator sees. It has no headless meaning and needs no CLI verb, no order-log row, and no determinism guarantee.
- Commands — anything that mutates the scenario or issues orders — must keep CLI/MCP parity and produce logged intents (ADR-010).

Stating the line prevents both failure modes: plumbing view toggles through the command bus, and quietly letting a mutating menu item bypass the order log.

### CMD-28.4 — Spatial tools

- Range / bearing measurement with a binding. REQ-20 lists "measure" only as a map context-menu item (§4.2, Partial). In a genre where range is the primary spatial judgement — the same reasoning behind CMD-20 — measurement deserves to be a tool, not a buried context entry.
- Lat/Lon grid as a toggleable overlay; a coordinate reference alongside CMD-20's distance scale.

### CMD-28.5 — Keyboard unit cycling

`Select Next Unit` / `Select Previous Unit`. Complements CMD-07 (map ↔ OOB ↔ panel selection sync) by making selection reachable without pointing, which matters for dense pictures and for accessibility.

### CMD-28.6 — Single-panel detachment is much cheaper than the multitasker

`Message Log in Separate Window` detaches one panel to one window. REQ-20's CMD-14 defers "multitasker bookmarks / multi-monitor detachable chrome" to Phase N — but that is the full product feature. Detaching a single panel is a fraction of the cost and delivers most of the multi-monitor value for a log you want visible continuously. Worth splitting from CMD-14 rather than inheriting its deferral.

### CMD-28.7 — Menu organisation

The reference's View menu mixes roughly six concerns — window management, camera, selection, tools, panel spawning, overlays, basemap layers, render mode — in one flat list of nineteen items. Adopt the coverage, not the organisation: separate view control from layer selection from tools.

### Do not inherit — the fourth instance

`Quick Jump` is greyed in the menu bar with no stated reason. That is now the fourth disabled-without-reason case catalogued in this series — after the editor's greyed actions, the Air Ops action bar, and the scenario library's padlocks. This should stop being four findings and become one house rule: every disabled control states why, at the control.

## CMD-29 — Contact detail panel [P0]

Requirement. Selecting a contact shall present a panel distinct from the own-unit panel, showing classification and its confidence, detection provenance, engagement permission, and battle-damage assessment.

### The framing that matters

The unit panel shows what is. The contact panel shows what we believe.

Everything about a contact is inference from sensor returns and may be wrong — the identification, the classification, the position, whether it is still there at all. Collapsing both into one "selected object" panel silently asserts that hostile data is as trustworthy as own-force data, which in this genre is the central lie to avoid.

This is the same epistemics as CMD-17 seen from the other side: CMD-17 is "I own this unit but cannot reach it"; CMD-29 is "I can see this thing but do not own it." Both are about the gap between the world and the picture.

### The gap

REQ-20's Right-panel row specifies "Selected unit/group: status, sensors, weapons, fuel, doctrine" — own-unit data only. Contacts appear in the left drawer (contact list tab) and in map styling ("Contact styling distinct from friendly"), but selecting one has no specified panel.

### Unusually, the data mostly exists

Most gaps in this series are UI over an absent model. This one is the reverse:

| Capability | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `ContactSummaryProjection`, `ContactPictureProjection`, `ContactPictureEntry` | Shipped (`src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/`) |
| `BdaContactDamageStates` | Shipped |
| `ContactChangeRecord` — contact lifecycle in the order log | Shipped (doc 17) |
| WRA in the engage path | Shipped (`EngagementAbortReason`, `MvpEngagementResolver`, `AbortReasonCatalog`) |
| Contact detail panel spec | Absent |

The gap is specification, not model. That makes this cheaper than its P0 suggests.

### Sub-requirements

- CMD-29.1 — Identification with its confidence. The reference is quietly precise here: the header reads `SAM Bn (SA-3b)` while the resolved line reads `SAM Bn (SA-3c Gon [S-125M1 Nevn-M])`. Those disagree — a coarse initial classification alongside a more specific resolution. Classification specificity increases as sensor data accumulates, and the panel must show how well the contact is identified, not merely assert a name. An overconfident label on a poorly-resolved contact is how players shoot the wrong thing.
- CMD-29.2 — Detection provenance. "Detected by: Automatic detection on [Unknown]" — which sensor, on which platform, and when. Likely the single highest-value element on the panel: it answers why do I think this exists, connects doc 15 (sensor/detection) to CMD-11's "why can't I fire?" explain surface, and makes stale or single-source tracks visible rather than implicit.
- CMD-29.3 — WRA classification. The reference shows `WRA: Land Structure - Soft - Building (Revetted)` — the target classification that drives release authority under doc 13. This is the field that determines whether an engagement is permitted, so it belongs on the panel where the engagement decision is made, not only inside an abort reason after refusal.
- CMD-29.4 — BDA as belief, not truth. `Damage` / `BDA` / `Damage Ctrl` — battle damage assessment is an estimate from observation. Rendering it identically to own-unit damage state would assert knowledge the player does not have. `BdaContactDamageStates` already models this.
- CMD-29.5 — Contact report action. A `Contact Report…` affordance producing the fuller intelligence picture for the selected track.
- CMD-29.6 — Staleness. A contact not currently held is a last-known position with an age, not a current one. Pairs with the CMD-17 question about whether last-known values carry an age stamp or are suppressed — the two should be answered together and consistently, since they are the same design question on own units and on hostiles.

## CMD-30 — Tactical overlay control [P1]

Requirement. The client shall provide control over tactical overlay symbology — range envelopes, engagement vectors, connectivity, courses, and datablocks — separately from basemap layer selection.

Reference evidence. A Map Settings menu carrying eight colour-chipped range toggles (`Air / Surface / Underwater Sensors`, `Air / Surface / Land / Underwater Weapons`, `Aircraft Range`, each stating `(Current: ON)`), plus `Show Non-friendly Range-Symbols`, `Merge Range-symbols`, `Sonobuoy Visibility`, `Reference Point Visibility`, `Illumination Vectors`, `Targetting Vectors`, `Datablocks`, `Datalinks`, `Contact Emissions`, `Plotted Courses`, `Mission area/course`, `Track Selected Unit (T)`, `LOS Tool`, `Minimaps`, and `Terrain Type Legend` — the last rendering a 17-class land-cover legend on the map.

### The architectural point — two stacks, two owners

This is not the same surface as CMD-28.2, and the difference matters under ADR-010:

| Stack | Content | Ownership |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basemap layers (CMD-28.2) | Imagery, relief, borders, land cover — what the world looks like | UI-local; no sim meaning |
| Tactical overlays (CMD-30) | Range envelopes, vectors, datalinks, courses — what the sim state looks like | Projections from the headless core |

Two menus in the reference, two different owners. Conflating them would either plumb basemap toggles through the command bus, or make sim-derived overlays UI-local state that replay cannot reproduce.

### Sub-requirements

- CMD-30.1 — Range symbology is a taxonomy, not a toggle. Eight independent controls across \{Air, Surface, Underwater\} × \{Sensors, Weapons\} plus Land Weapons and Aircraft Range. CMD-21 is a subset of this, not a synonym — CMD-21 is the Phase A baseline for the selected unit; CMD-30.1 is the picture-wide taxonomy.
- CMD-30.2 — Non-friendly range symbols are beliefs. Estimated hostile envelopes are a major tactical affordance, but they are inference (CMD-29 epistemics) and must not render identically to own-force envelopes, which are known.
- CMD-30.3 — Merged range symbols are Phase A decluttering, not Phase N LOD. REQ-20 discusses decluttering only under APP-6 LOD and the 5k@60 north-star (CMD-13/15, Phase N). Merging overlapping envelopes into a hull is cheap, needs no LOD product, and becomes necessary long before 5,000 symbols. Same baseline-versus-deferred split as CMD-21 — do not let it ride along with the LOD work.
- CMD-30.4 — State in text, not colour alone. The reference writes `(Current: ON)` beside each colour chip. Adopt it: satisfies CMD-12 by construction and makes the menu readable without decoding swatches.
- CMD-30.5 — Engagement geometry overlays. Illumination and targeting vectors — who is illuminating or targeting whom (doc 14). Pairs with CMD-11 intent preview.
- CMD-30.6 — Connectivity and emissions. Datalinks are modelled (9 datalink types in `src/`); EMCON is modelled (`EmconState`, `CatalogEmcon`, `CatalogRadarEmconResolver`) though emissions as a distinct concept are not. Links docs 15 and 19 to the map.
- CMD-30.7 — Route and mission-area overlays.
- CMD-30.8 — Datablocks. Configurable symbol labels — the density knob that decides whether a dense picture is readable. Not modelled.
- CMD-30.9 — Camera and analysis tools. Track-selected-unit, LOS tool, minimaps. None modelled.
- CMD-30.10 — Legends for data-driven colouring. The reference pairs its land-cover layer with a 17-class legend. Any layer whose colour encodes a taxonomy needs one — without it the colouring is decoration the player cannot decode.
- CMD-30.11 — Group / Unit view toggle, complementing CMD-07 (§4.4).

> ⚠️ Colour budget — worth an explicit audit. Eight range-symbol colours, plus affiliation colours (CMD-12, which must stay colourblind-safe), plus seventeen land-cover classes, plus severity and diff colours. The colour channel is heavily oversubscribed, and adding overlays without a palette audit will collide with the accessibility commitment REQ-20 has already made.

- Selection stated three times — top-left label, map ring, and right-panel header. Deliberate redundancy for a dense screen; worth keeping in mind when trimming.

---

> OPEN QUESTION: Should these land as new CMD rows in REQ-20, or as a Phase-2 addendum? REQ-20 is `Status: Draft — Template B (Wave 2 re-honesty)` with a carefully maintained honesty column; adding eight P0/P1 rows shifts its completion picture and should be a deliberate edit, not a drive-by.

> OPEN QUESTION: CMD-17 and CMD-19 both imply projection changes, not just view work — per-axis autonomy state and comms-staleness have to reach the panel from the headless core. Are those projections already shaped for it, or is this an ADR-010 contract change?

> OPEN QUESTION: How much CMO parity is actually wanted? REQ-20 tracks parity area-by-area against the manual, but Aegis's differentiator is agent delegation — CMD-19 is the one proposal here that has no CMO equivalent worth copying, because CMO has no agents to delegate to.

pages.title: 🎯 Sprint 109 Plan — Agent Attention UI (DRG-67)
pages.content:
## Status

DONE 2026-08-04 — landed via #401; closeout #402.

Stage: Release · not Launch

Dispatch: serial on shared Projection/UI surface (Linear parallel-dispatch playbook: no co-edit of intersecting surfaces).

Suite: 2369/0f core Release on tip `d7e49acd` (GHA 30955397191).

Linear: DRG-67 + DRG-77…82 Done.

Primary Linear story: [DRG-67 — Agent attention UI](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-67/agent-attention-is-a-designated-core-mechanic-that-no-ui-surface)

Milestone: H1 — C2 Runtime Depth


Make the delegation attention mechanic visible and actionable to the operator, using the same decision-time values the simulation applied.


## Sprint goal

Close the operator-facing gap in the attention mechanic: show each agent's load, budget, and degradation tier; explain attention-driven decisions; warn on tier crossings; and preview the consequence of an assignment before it is committed.

## Scope and constraints

- In scope: AGD-11 through AGD-14 and AGD-20; agent roster, directive/assignment flow, alerts, and explain surface.
- Source of truth: decision-time `AttentionEvaluation`; the UI must not independently re-derive attention state.
- Out of scope: changes to attention simulation rules, live OOB editing, Launch/store work, and broad C2 redesign.
- Hard invariants: deterministic replay; no `DelegationBridge` hotpath edits; Unity remains a read-only snapshot projection except through the approved command/queue boundary.
- Predecessor: S108 complete on 2026-08-04 — #382 through #388 and #392 landed; suite recorded at 2346/0 failures.

## Planned window

5 working days — 2026-08-05 to 2026-08-11, subject to normal serial review and merge gates.

## Workstreams

| Workstream | Objective | Linear child issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S109-01 | Define and test the attention projection contract from decision-time state. | [DRG-77](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-77/s109-01-define-decision-time-attention-projection-contract) |
| S109-02 | Expose per-agent load, budget, and named degradation tier in the roster/directive surface. | [DRG-78](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-78/s109-02-surface-attention-state-in-agent-roster-and-directive-ui) |
| S109-03 | Add attributable, non-spamming alerts on attention-tier crossings. | [DRG-80](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-80/s109-03-alert-on-attributable-attention-tier-crossings) |
| S109-04 | Show post-assignment attention forecast before the operator commits an assignment. | [DRG-81](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-81/s109-04-preview-post-assignment-attention-before-command-commit) |
| S109-05 | Add decision-time attention to the agent explain surface. | [DRG-79](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-79/s109-05-add-decision-time-attention-to-the-agent-explain-surface) |
| S109-06 | Run cross-cutting replay, smoke, accessibility, and closeout gates. | [DRG-82](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-82/s109-06-verify-attention-ui-gates-and-publish-sprint-closeout) |

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] An operator can see load / budget and the three named tiers: `SlowerReactions`, `NarrowedFocus`, and `SimplerDecisions`.
- [x] The displayed state is sourced from the exact `AttentionEvaluation` that applied to the decision; no duplicate UI algorithm exists.
- [x] A tier-crossing alert identifies the affected agent and avoids repeated alerts while the tier is unchanged.
- [x] Before assigning units, the command surface previews the projected attention effect and surfaces the affected tier.
- [x] The explain surface records the decision-time attention state as a reason for degraded behavior.
- [x] Existing command and pending-approval behavior remains intact.
- [x] Build is clean; full solution suite remains at or above the 1638 floor with zero failures (2369/0f core Release on land tip).
- [x] No new `DelegationBridge` hotpath edit and no replay/hash regression.

## Dependency order

1. Projection contract and tests (S109-01)
2. Roster/directive state plus explain surface (S109-02 and S109-05)
3. Tier-crossing alerts (S109-03)
4. Assignment forecast through the established command boundary (S109-04)
5. Full gate, accessibility pass, and closeout (S109-06)

## Risks and controls

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| UI diverges from runtime decision state | Carry the decision-time value through a projection contract; do not compute it again in Unity. |
| Alert noise causes operator blindness | Emit only on tier transitions and retain attribution to the agent. |
| Preview bypasses command safety | Use the existing approved command/queue boundary; preview is advisory until commit. |
| Projection/UI changes overlap | Serialize merged PRs and rerun affected tests after each land. |

## Definition of done

- [x] DRG-67 and all S109 child issues meet their acceptance criteria.
- [x] The attention mechanic is visible before and after assignment, explainable after a decision, and alertable on state transitions.
- [x] Required verification evidence is recorded in Linear.
- [x] H1 progress is updated honestly; Release stage remains unchanged.

- [DRG-67](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-67/agent-attention-is-a-designated-core-mechanic-that-no-ui-surface)

Allowed fields: id, name, domain, side, collisionRadiusNm, speedKn, damage.\{hp,maxHp,resilience,withdraw\}, mounts, sensors, comms[], links[]

### 3. relative-scaling

- Role weights: light 0.25 · standard 0.5 · heavy 0.75

### 4. provenance

- docId: `assistant`

### 5. gate-policy

- New ids only (`plt-*` unique)
- Mutate-existing → out of scope; tell user to use Excel + approval path

### 6. workbook-emit

- Emit DiffRow kinds: added (archetype sheets), info (basis line)
- Destination: Import staging, not live tables

### 7. what-if

- Flag on draft + staging chrome
- Catalog preview allowed; not canonical until ApproveBatch

| Case | Expect |
| --- | --- |
| Light Surface Blue OPV | Peers include skiff/corvette/patrol; HP between min and mid |
| Explicit peer pick | Uses only selected peers |
| Id collision | Suffix `-2`, `-3`… |
| Domain HP outlier | Warning banner |

Type: Design / product artifact

Status: Active — companion to PE-UX productization

Date: 2026-08-04

Related: [Platform Editor — UX/UI Review](https://app.notion.com/p/3aaf7cb4e4df81d2adf9cc55c4dd9dbb) · ADR-011 · doc 21 Platform Editor

---

## Decision

Ship a Platform Design Assistant (proposal agent), not a second Platform Editor.

| Surface | Role |
| --- | --- |
| Catalog | Read-only browse |
| Design Assistant (Propose) | Draft future/hypothetical archetypes relative to peers |
| Import | Propose → Acknowledge → Approve via CatalogWriteGate |

Excel remains the write workbench (ADR-011). Assistant never commits catalog rows.

---

## Why

New platforms must sit on the existing distribution (collision radius, HP, mounts, sensors, latency). Curators need relative placement, not unconstrained generation.

---

## Skill pack (required load order)

1. catalog-grounding — peers from live snapshot only
2. archetype-schema — doc 21 Phase A–B fields only; collision radius ≠ combat radius
3. relative-scaling — weighted interpolation by role (light / standard / heavy)
4. provenance — `proposed · assistant · {peer basis}`
5. gate-policy — extend-only new ids; no silent mutations
6. workbook-emit — DiffRow[] into Import staging
7. what-if (optional) — drafts stay staged until Approve

---

## UX shell

- Mode title: `DESIGN ASSISTANT` (Label, not a fake third Catalog tab)
- Tabs: Catalog | Import | Propose
- Actions: Generate proposal → Send to Import staging | Preview in Catalog (draft only)

---

## Invariants

- No write-path edits outside CatalogWriteGate.ApproveBatch
- New platform id must not collide
- Outliers vs domain stats flagged before Approve
- Implementation vocabulary stays in Developer/trace drawer

---

## Acceptance

1. Assistant produces peer-cited numeric fields for a new Surface OPV-class draft
2. Staging rows appear on Import with source label from assistant
3. Approve remains disabled until ack; blocked rows still gate
4. What-if draft is visible in Catalog preview but labeled not-committed
5. ADR-011 / extend-only policy copy remains on shell chrome

---

## Sequencing

| Horizon | Deliverable |
| --- | --- |
| Now (demo) | Deterministic relative-scaling engine + Propose tab in PE shell mock |
| Next | Wire to real ICatalogReader + workbook emit CLI |
| Later | LLM narrative on top of skill pack (still gate-bound) |
