# Phase A — Must ship for MVP

## SWARM-01 — Swarm is a first-class platform type [P0]

Requirement. The catalog and sim shall support a platform type (or type flag) representing a drone/UAS swarm that can be instantiated as a side-owned unit alongside ships, aircraft, and facilities.

Why. Without a platform type, swarms are either fake groups of N aircraft (micro hell, wrong logistics) or pure VFX.

Acceptance. A scenario can spawn at least one swarm unit; it appears in OOB and accepts selection.

## SWARM-02 — Aggregate integrity [P0]

Requirement. A swarm unit shall expose `droneCount` / `maxDrones` (or equivalent pool HP that maps 1:1 to count). Destruction of the platform occurs when integrity reaches zero.

Acceptance. Damage events reduce count; UI/projections show remaining integrity; at 0 the unit is destroyed/removed per normal unit death rules.

## SWARM-03 — Intent orders: Move, Attack, Hold [P0]

Requirement. The unit shall accept at least Move (plot/course or mission point), Attack (engage target/auto), and Hold (loiter/station) without requiring selection of individual drones.

Acceptance. Headless commands exist; C2 can issue them; swarm centroid follows / engages accordingly.

## SWARM-04 — Effects scale with living drones [P0]

Requirement. Offensive output and sensor effectiveness shall scale with living drone count (monotonic; exact curve is a tuning knob).

Acceptance. Full swarm detects/engages more effectively than a half-depleted swarm under identical geometry; golden or unit tests lock the curve.

## SWARM-05 — Single selection node [P0]

Requirement. Selection, map symbol, and OOB entry treat the swarm as one unit. Per-drone selection is out of scope for Phase A.

Acceptance. Clicking the swarm selects one unit id; multi-select behaves like any other unit.

## SWARM-06 — Headless logged intents [P0]

Requirement. Per ADR-010 patterns, swarm orders shall be headless commands that produce order-log rows (or equivalent deterministic intents), not UI-only gestures.

Acceptance. CLI/MCP or existing command path can move/attack a swarm; replay consumes the same intents.

## SWARM-07 — Deterministic aggregate engagement SoT [P0]

Requirement. Detection, fire, and damage resolution shall use aggregate swarm state, not non-deterministic per-drone physics, as the source of truth.

Acceptance. Same scenario + seed → same integrity timeline; cosmetic member layout may be seeded but must not drive outcomes.

## SWARM-08 — Hard counter interaction [P0]

Requirement. At least one weapon/system class (e.g. area AA / flak / CIWS profile) shall be demonstrably effective at shredding swarm integrity faster than point-fire against a conventional airframe of similar cost band.

Acceptance. Documented test scenario where swarm dies to area AA while surviving longer against single-target fire of equal nominal DPS.

## SWARM-09 — Map integrity + density readout [P0]

Requirement. Map and/or unit panel shall show remaining integrity (count or bar) and a density/affiliation-safe symbol distinct from a single light aircraft where feasible.

Acceptance. Player can read swarm health without opening a deep inspector; color alone is not the only channel (CMD-12 alignment).

## SWARM-24 — Replay integrity [P0]

Requirement. Replay/fixtures shall reconstruct swarm orders and integrity-affecting events. Member cosmetics need not be bit-identical if seeded consistently.

Acceptance. Golden replay or world-hash path includes swarm integrity deltas.

## SWARM-25 — Performance caps [P0]

Requirement. Logical drone count and rendered member count shall be independently capped; Phase A combat must remain aggregate so large logical counts do not imply O(n) engagement work per pulse.

Acceptance. Profiled scenario with design-max swarms meets project frame/pulse budgets (state numbers when landed in REQ NFR).

---

# Phase B — Modes, host, C2, authoring

## SWARM-10 — Operational modes [P1]

Requirement. Swarm shall support modes: Hold, Assault, Screen, Scatter, Rejoin. Mode changes are orders (logged).

Acceptance. Mode is visible in projection; behavior differs in at least movement posture and engagement aggressiveness.

## SWARM-11 — Host / mothership [P1]

Requirement. A swarm may designate a host unit (ship/vehicle/aircraft/base). Screen mode prefers orbiting the host. Host loss triggers doctrine last-order.

Acceptance. Scenario can bind hostId; Screen keeps swarm near host; host death produces a defined autonomous reaction.

## SWARM-12 — LinkState [P1]

Requirement. Swarm shall track linkState ∈ \{connected, degraded, lost\} driven by range, jam, and host/comms rules consistent with project comms degradation themes.

Acceptance. Lost link blocks or delays new player orders per doctrine; panel shows cause (CMD-17 pattern: unknown-with-reason, not blank).

## SWARM-13 — Regeneration [P1]

Requirement. Near a valid host/base with stores, swarm may regenerate drones over time up to maxDrones, subject to logistics rules.

Acceptance. Without stores, regen does not occur; with stores, count climbs on a documented rate.

## SWARM-14 — C2 panel fields [P1]

Requirement. Selected swarm unit panel shows: mode, integrity (count/max), energy/endurance if modelled, host, linkState, and primary sensor/weapon summary.

Acceptance. Fields update live; missing telemetry uses explicit unknown reasons when link lost.

## SWARM-15 — Doctrine / WRA [P1]

Requirement. Doctrine shall control auto-engage posture and whether expend (if present) is authorized. WRA classification for swarm munitions/target classes shall be expressible.

Acceptance. Hold-fire prevents assault shots; authorized expend is the only path to SWARM-19 when that ships.

## SWARM-21 — Catalog + Platform Editor [P1]

Requirement. Authors can define swarm catalog entries: maxDrones, sensors, weapons/munition class, speed/endurance bands, default mode, host constraints.

Acceptance. Platform Editor / PDA path can create a valid swarm db entry consumed by sim.

## SWARM-22 — Scenario editor [P1]

Requirement. Scenario editor can place swarms, set initial count ≤ max, assign side/host/mission.

Acceptance. Round-trip save/load preserves swarm fields; validation catches count > max and missing catalog refs.

## SWARM-23 — Agent delegation [P1]

Requirement. Delegated agents may issue the same intent orders as humans to swarm units; per-axis or unit-level delegation badges apply as for other units.

Acceptance. Agent can task swarm assault/screen without UI; order log attributes actor correctly.

## SWARM-26 — Contact classification [P1]

Requirement. Hostile swarms as contacts expose classification that can distinguish swarm/UAS cloud from single airframe when sensors allow, with confidence (CMD-29 alignment).

Acceptance. Contact panel/projection can show swarm-class label when identified; misclassification possible at low quality.

---

# Phase C — Depth

## SWARM-16 — Formations [P2]

Cloud, wall/screen, spear, orbit as soft constraints on member layout and engagement geometry.

## SWARM-17 — Multi-axis auto-split [P2]

Assault may split logical mass across approach axes against a single high-value target when doctrine allows.

## SWARM-18 — EMP / jam soft-kill [P2]

EMP scatters/freezes mode switches temporarily; jam degrades linkState and order latency.

## SWARM-19 — Expend pulse [P2]

Authorized order spends N drones for a burst strike; irreversible; logged.

## SWARM-20 — Mission integration [P2]

Patrol / support / strike mission types can assign swarms with swarm-appropriate default modes.

---

# Phase N / Won't for MVP

## SWARM-27 — Split / merge [P3]

Split one swarm platform into two; merge compatible swarms. High UX and identity cost — defer.

## SWARM-28 — Per-member physics SoT [P3 / Won't MVP]

Individual drone bodies as engagement authority. Conflicts with SWARM-07; only if product fantasy demands it and replay strategy is redesigned.

## SWARM-29 — Multi-static ISR mesh [P3]

True distributed sensing geometry beyond scaled aggregate quality.

## SWARM-30 — Full MUM-T packages [P3]

Manned flight leads with organic swarms as a package type — after host + air ops maturity.

---

---

# Suggested starter tuning (non-normative)

| Knob | Starter |
| --- | --- |
| maxDrones | 40 logical |
| renderMembers | 24 cap |
| dpsPerDrone | tune vs soft targets |
| regen | 1 drone / 1.5s near host if stores |
| scatter cooldown | 8s |
| armorClass | light-air |

---

# Acceptance criteria — Phase A done when

1. Swarm platform spawns, selects, moves, attacks as one unit
2. Losing drones weakens sensors/weapons measurably
3. At least one hard counter shreds integrity faster than point fire
4. Orders are headless + logged; replay/hash stable
5. Map/panel show integrity without per-drone UI
6. Performance caps documented and met in a stress scenario

## Downloadable artifact



Portable Markdown summary of this research page for offline / PR attachment.

---

Type: Reference research (not an Aegis requirement, not a design page — the 8-section template does not apply)

Status: Research complete — for owner triage

Date: 2026-08-09

Subject: Drone / UAV swarms as platform types for Project Aegis (cmano-clone)

Feeds: [Drone Swarm Platforms — Proposed Requirements (SWARM-01…SWARM-30)](https://app.notion.com/p/3b7f7cb4e4df8104b63be13bc99f2358)

Related design stubs: Entity & Unit Data Model · Weapons & Engagement · Sensor & Detection · Scenario Editor Spec

Related Linear: [https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/project/cmano-clone-7f6a00e4c1c9](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/project/cmano-clone-7f6a00e4c1c9)

## Provenance — read before citing this

This page records research synthesized 2026-08-09 from open doctrinal writing, multi-agent control literature, game-AI practice (boids / flow fields), and one commercial RTS design case study. It is not a commitment, not parity with any CMO feature set, and not a design page under the 8-section template.

Where it feeds requirements, those requirements are SWARM-01… on the sibling proposal page. Git remains SoT for landed requirements under Game-Requirements/requirements/.

> OPEN QUESTION: Does Aegis already model single UAVs / UCAVs as ordinary air platforms in the catalog? If yes, swarms should be a composition / control layer over existing air units, not a parallel domain. If no, swarm work may force the broader UAS spine first.

---

# 1. What "swarm as platform" means

In Aegis terms, a platform is a catalogued, selectable, orderable unit class (ship, aircraft, sub, facility). A drone swarm should be one of those — one roster entity — not N micro-managed micro-UAVs.

| Concept | Meaning for Aegis |
| --- | --- |
| Platform type | Catalog entry, e.g. UAS-Swarm / loitering-munition swarm / ISR cloud |
| Swarm instance | One side-owned unit with integrity (drone count), mode, host/link, energy |
| Member drones | Simulated or LOD-aggregated agents under the swarm controller |
| Operator model | Human (or delegated agent) issues intent; autonomy executes formation, rejoin, local avoidance |

Rule of thumb: player and AI commander select/order the swarm controller; individual drones are not first-class OOB leaves unless a future split-to-individuals feature is explicitly added.

---

# 2. Real-world / doctrinal research

## 2.1 Swarm maneuver ideas (USMC & related)

Open USMC writing on swarm maneuver groups emphasizes:

- Saturation: attack with enough mass to overwhelm defender response capacity without pure target overkill
- Multi-axis convergence: coordinated attack from multiple directions to break single-axis defense focus
- Economy of force: enough combat power, not infinite attrition spam
- Human-on-the-loop C2: remote C2 nodes retask small groups; humans set mission/priority, not every vehicle stick input

## 2.2 PLA "bee swarm warfare" concepts (secondary sources)

Open secondary analyses of PLA conceptual writing describe:

- Decentralized, coordinated, autonomous saturation against predetermined targets
- Numerical superiority to overwhelm sensors and interceptors
- Distinction between swarm employment and manned–unmanned teaming (MUM-T)

Treat as conceptual flavor, not verified TO&E. Useful for scenario design language — not for inventing classified capabilities.

## 2.3 Control architectures (UAV swarm literature)

| Architecture | Who decides | Game relevance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Centralized | One GCS / mothership plans all trajectories | Easy determinism; single point of failure / jam target |
| Hierarchical | Player → swarm controller → local agents | Best default for Aegis |
| Consensus / auction | Peers vote or bid on tasks | Interesting for agent delegation later |
| Emergent | Local rules only (pure boids) | Great for motion; weak for mission intent |

Recommendation for Aegis: hierarchical C2 with optional loss-of-link degraded modes (local last-order / RTB / loiter), consistent with existing comms degradation and delegation themes.

## 2.4 Decision making levels

- Local: collision avoidance, keep formation, short-range threat reaction
- Collective: shared goal, multi-axis split, rejoin after attrition
- Commander: assign area/target/host, set mode/EMCON, authorize expend

This maps cleanly onto Aegis: orders + doctrine at commander level, steering at local level, missions for area tasking.

---

# 3. Game-design research (transferable lessons)

## 3.1 Drone Swarm (2020, real-time tactics)

Coverage of the commercial game Drone Swarm is useful as a control UX case study:

- One mothership + one versatile swarm (no base-building)
- Path-draw orders instead of APM micro
- Formations: protective vortex (rest), wall, serpentine, ball, shrapnel
- Attrition of drones reduces capability; regeneration via upgrades
- Tactile mass control via intent, not selection of individuals

Transfer to Aegis: do not clone arcade physics; do clone the principle that swarm orders are intent-level and integrity is the HP bar.

## 3.2 Large-unit pathfinding (Supreme Commander 2, Planetary Annihilation)

- Flow fields amortize pathfinding when many agents share a goal
- Units flow around obstacles rather than each running independent A\*
- Formation offsets + shared field = swarm motion without O(n) full paths

Transfer: if Aegis ever simulates member drones above a small count, use shared goal navigation + local separation, not per-drone A\* every pulse.

## 3.3 Boids (Craig Reynolds)

Classic three local rules:

1. Separation — avoid crowding neighbors
2. Alignment — match local average heading
3. Cohesion — steer toward local average position

Extended with obstacle avoidance and goal seek. Complexity O(n²) naive; spatial hash / neighborhood ≈ O(n).

Transfer: excellent for visual LOD and believable local motion; strategic where still comes from mission/order pathing.

## 3.4 Aegis AI stack alignment

Existing project AI guidance already recommends A\*/flow fields for where, Reynolds steering for how, FSM/behavior trees for what, fixed AI tick, path cache, stagger distant agents. Swarms are a stress test of that stack, not a different stack — unless counts force GPU/particle LOD.

---

# 4. How CMO-class products usually treat UAS (parity lens)

From existing Aegis research (menu ops, air ops):

- Aircraft are first-class platforms with loadouts, magazines, air ops windows
- Groups form/detach; members can ghost under group symbols
- Missions (patrol, strike, ferry, support…) task units/groups
- Sensors/weapons have domain-specific range rings
- WRA / doctrine gates fire

Typically thin even in CMO-class products:

- True swarm integrity as a single platform with internal count
- Mode reconfiguration (ISR cloud ↔ attack mesh ↔ screen) without respawning different unit types
- Link / jam as a first-class swarm C2 vulnerability
- Saturation vs point-defense trade as designed gameplay, not just many air units

Aegis can treat swarms as a differentiator, not pure parity.

---

# 5. Design pillars (recommendations)

1. One entity, many bodies — selection, OOB, doctrine, messages target the swarm unit
2. Intent, not micro — Move / Attack / Orbit host / Scatter / Rejoin / Hold
3. Attrition is the economy — droneCount maps to DPS, ISR quality, screen thickness
4. Roles by reconfiguration — same pool, different modes (scout, harass, screen, strike, expend)
5. Hard counters — AA/flak, EMP, jamming, high-rate CIWS classes
6. Readable mass — map symbol shows density/integrity; not 200 HP bars
7. Determinism first — controller state is authoritative; member poses either derived or seeded
8. Headless-first — swarm orders are logged intents; projections feed C2 UI

---

# 6. Architecture recommendation

```txt
Player / Delegated Agent
        │  orders / doctrine / WRA
        ▼
  SwarmController (Platform unit)
  - integrity, energy, mode, hostId, linkState
  - shared goal / mission assignment
        │
        ├─ Strategic navigator (shared path / area mission)
        │
        └─ Member agents (logical count ± render LOD)
             local separation + optional boids
```

### Suggested aggregate state

```txt
SwarmPlatform
  id, side, catalogId
  position (centroid), velocity
  droneCount, maxDrones
  energy / endurance
  mode: hold | assault | screen | scatter | rejoin | expend
  formation: cloud | wall | spear | orbit
  hostId? (carrier / truck / ship / aircraft)
  linkState: connected | degraded | lost
  vision / sensor quality scale
  dpsPerDrone, munitionClass
  armorClass: light-air (or loitering-munition)
```

### Motion stack

| Layer | Approach | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Strategic | Mission path / shared flow toward goal | One cost for whole swarm |
| Local | Separation + formation slots | Alive motion, cheap |
| Link loss | Last order / RTB / loiter doctrine | Comms parity with doc 19 themes |
| LOD | Cap rendered members; scale logical effects | Perf + map readability |

### Determinism note (Aegis-critical)

Prefer authoritative controller state in the sim pulse:

- Engagement, detection, damage, and orders use aggregate stats
- Member layout for map cosmetics can be seeded from (swarmId, pulse, count) so replay does not depend on float chaos
- If individual members must take hits, resolve damage against pool first, then recompute layout

Avoid per-drone non-deterministic physics as the engagement SoT.

---

# 7. Combat & balance skeleton (design-facing)

| Concern | Recommendation |
| --- | --- |
| Damage in | Hits reduce droneCount (or pool HP → count) |
| Damage out | droneCount \* dpsPerDrone or salvo model by mode |
| vs armor | Strong vs soft / unarmored / exposed sensors; weak vs hardened armor without SEAD |
| Soft kill | Jam → order delay / mode lock; EMP → temporary freeze + scatter |
| Hard kill | Area AA shreds count quickly |
| Rebuild | Near host/base: regenerate drones over time if logistics allows |
| Expend mode | Spend N drones for burst — explicit player/agent authorize |

Hard counters: high-rate AA, area flak, EW/jam, directed-energy CIWS classes.

Soft trades: cheap vs soft targets; harasses heavy armor without finishing; loses to true air superiority fighters unless numbers extreme.

---

# 8. Host / mothership relationship

Highly recommended for Aegis fantasy and logistics fit:

- Swarm orbits host in Screen mode (ship, vehicle, aircraft, fixed base)
- Leaving host extends range but costs energy and risks link loss
- Host death → doctrine last-order (persist / RTB alternate / disperse)
- Regen gated by host magazines / special stores (REQ-16 adjacency)

This mirrors Air Ops embarkation conceptually, but the swarm remains one platform while airborne as a cloud.

---

# 9. Integration touchpoints (existing Aegis surfaces)

| Surface | Implication |
| --- | --- |
| Entity / catalog | New platform category or flag isSwarm; maxDrones; modes |
| OOB / selection | Single node; optional expand for member count only |
| Doctrine / WRA | Modes + expend authorization; EMCON for emissions of the cloud |
| Sensors (doc 15) | Aggregate ISR quality scales with count |
| Weapons (doc 14) | Saturation salvos; soft vs hard targets; CIWS interaction |
| Comms (doc 19) | LinkState first-class; jam is a tactical fact |
| Logistics (doc 16) | Reload/rebuild near host; aviation-like stores |
| Air Ops (CMD-24) | Host launch/recover of swarm platforms may share window patterns |
| Map / C2 (REQ-20) | Density symbol, integrity badge, mode readout, envelope rings |
| Agents / delegation | Agents issue intent to swarms more naturally than micro |
| Replay | Log swarm orders + integrity deltas; not every member pose |
| Platform Editor / PDA | Author swarm catalog entries with count, sensors, munitions |

---

# 10. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Feels like weak aircraft with extra VFX | Modes + attrition + EW counters + unique orders |
| Perf cliff | Aggregate combat model; render cap; spatial hash |
| Unreadable map | Density glyph + integrity; merge range symbols |
| Micro hell | Never expose per-drone selection in MVP |
| Overpowered saturation | AA counters + energy/link + rebuild cost + WRA |
| Underpowered flavor unit | Exclusive jobs: cheap ISR fill-in, missile soak, soft-target clear |
| Non-deterministic replay | Aggregate SoT + seeded cosmetics |
| Spec over vapour | Gate UI on model; Phase A aggregate only |

---

# 11. Phasing recommendation

### Phase 0 — Design lock

Confirm: player + enemy swarms? Map symbol language? Max logical count? Relation to existing UAV catalog entries.

### Phase A — MVP platform

Spawn/select/move/attack as one unit; integrity bar; scaled sensors/weapons; one hard counter; headless orders logged.

### Phase B — Modes & host

Screen / Scatter / Rejoin; orbit host; regen; link loss; C2 mode UI.

### Phase C — Depth

Formations, multi-axis auto-split, EMP/jam polish, expend pulse, mission types, editor authoring.

### Phase N

True large-N member sim, split/merge platforms, advanced multi-static ISR, full MUM-T packages.

---

# 12. Sources & further reading

- Craig Reynolds — Boids / steering behaviors ([red3d.com/cwr/boids](http://red3d.com/cwr/boids))
- PC Gamer — Drone Swarm control design coverage (2020)
- Game AI pathfinding practice — flow fields (Supreme Commander 2 / crowd continuum literature)
- USMC Journal — swarm maneuver group concepts (open articles)
- UAV swarm navigation surveys — centralized vs decentralized C2 (open access reviews)
- Secondary analyses of PLA bee swarm warfare concepts (Air University / CASI open PDFs)
- Existing Aegis wiki: CMO menu reference; CMD-16…30 C2 proposals; REQ-16 logistics honesty pattern

---

# 13. Implications for existing Aegis docs

| Finding | Affects |
| --- | --- |
| Swarm is a platform composition model, not just another aircraft preset | Entity model · Platform Editor · catalog schema |
| Integrity/count is the HP analogue | Weapons damage resolution · BDA language |
| LinkState is C2-critical | Comms degradation · panel unknown states (CMD-17 pattern) |
| Host orbit/regen | Logistics · Air/Docking ops patterns |
| Intent orders over micro | C2 toolbar / missions · agent delegation |
| Deterministic aggregate SoT | Replay · golden fixtures |

> OPEN QUESTION: Should swarm platforms appear in the same Air Ops window as conventional aircraft, or as a dedicated Swarm Ops surface?

>

> OPEN QUESTION: Is a swarm a CombatDomain.Air unit with a special aspect, or a new domain/aspect for loitering munitions / UAS clouds?

>

> OPEN QUESTION: Minimum catalog fidelity for Phase A — abstract Generic ISR Swarm only, or national exemplars (non-classified public specs only)?

pages.content:

| Layer | Link |
| --- | --- |
| Git branch | `docs/unity-csharp-architect-skill-roadmap` |

| Linear issues | DRG-118 (M0) · DRG-119 (M1) · DRG-120 (M2) · DRG-121 (M3) · DRG-122 (M4) · DRG-123 (M5) |

---

## Status

Stage: Complete — UCA-M0…M5 complete (merged: PRs #471, #473, #474, #475, #476; dogfood #477). Skill `metadata.status: v1` / version `1.0.0`.

Created: 2026-08-11 · Closed: 2026-08-11

Contract: Git = files · Linear = delivery · Notion = design (this page)

AAR: `production/agentic/skills/unity-csharp-architect/AAR-uca-m5-dogfood-2026-08-11.md`

Dogfood PR: [https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/477](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/477) — `MapPictureBridge` + `checklists/pr-finish.md` PASS

## Problem

Project Aegis agents write Unity C# frequently (UI maturity, Platform Editor, C2 map, scenario editor), but architecture knowledge is scattered across ADRs, sprint plans, and tribal memory. Common agent failures:

- MonoBehaviours reaching into live sim/ECS state (violates ADR-010 / 007 / 001 presentation wall)
- Commands mixed with presentation (violates ADR-010)
- Fat assemblies / wrong asmdef edges
- Editor tools coupling to runtime presenters
- Frame-rate work done on the sim clock instead of interpolation
- No finish checklist — PRs look green, architecture drifts

## Goal

Ship a reusable agent skill `unity-csharp-architect` that is to Unity/C# what `building-games` is to browser games: a load-on-demand playbook with hard rules, references, and self-tests.

Primary consumer: agentic Unity work on [cmano-clone](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone)

Secondary: any future Aegis Unity surface (tools, map, PE, C2 chrome)

## Skill shape (proposed)

```txt
production/agentic/skills/unity-csharp-architect/
  SKILL.md                    # frontmatter + core doctrine
  ROADMAP.md                  # milestone plan
  references/
    presentation-boundary.md  # ADR-010/007/001 operationalized
    headless-command-ui.md    # ADR-010 operationalized
    asmdefs-and-layers.md     # assembly graph, allowed deps
    scriptableobjects-data.md # data-driven config, no scene-only truth
    mono-anti-patterns.md     # god MBs, FindObjectOfType, Update thrash
    editor-vs-runtime.md      # EditorWindow / UnityAdapter split
    performance-unity.md      # GC, pooling, main-thread budget
    testing-unity.md          # EditMode/PlayMode + headless-first preference
    aegis-unity-map.md        # where things live in this repo
  checklists/
    pr-finish.md              # agent must pass before Done
    review-gates.md           # human review prompts
```

Frontmatter pattern (match Grok skill convention):

```yaml
---
name: unity-csharp-architect
description: >
  Senior Unity C# architecture for Project Aegis: presentation boundary,
  headless/command-driven UI, assembly definitions, SO data, editor vs runtime,
  performance, and finish self-tests. Triggers on Unity, MonoBehaviour, asmdef,
  C# architecture, UnityAdapter, EditorWindow, presentation, snapshot.
metadata:
  short-description: "Aegis Unity/C# architecture: ADR-010/001/007, asmdefs, finish checks"
---
```

## Doctrine pillars (brainstorm → skill core)

### 1. Two clocks, two worlds

- Sim world: headless .NET, deterministic, command-driven, testable without Unity
- Presentation world: Unity, frame-rate, read-only snapshots + interpolation
- Agents must never invent a third path that mutates sim from MonoBehaviour

### 2. Presentation wall as law (ADR-010 §2–3 / ADR-007 / ADR-001)

- Presentation reads projections/snapshots only
- No live ECS chunk refs, no cached session internals from MBs
- Interpolation is presentation-only; sim steps on sim clock
- Note: Git ADR-018 is sensor side-picture / datalink — not this wall

### 3. ADR-010 as law

- Player intent → commands → engine
- UI presenters are engine-free where possible (UnityAdapter / Authoring pattern)
- Headless-first: if it can be proven without Editor, prove it without Editor

### 4. Assembly graph discipline

- Allowed edges only (diagram in `asmdefs-and-layers.md`)
- Forbid: UI → Simulation internals; Editor → Runtime presentation shortcuts; circular asmdefs
- Prefer ProjectAegis.\* namespaces already established

### 5. Data ownership

- ScriptableObjects / catalog rows for designer data
- Runtime mutable state lives in sim or explicit session services — not on every MB

### 6. Finish criteria (agent must run)

- [ ] No MB reads live sim chunks
- [ ] New UI path has a command or documented exception ADR
- [ ] Asmdef edges documented if new
- [ ] EditMode or headless test for pure logic
- [ ] No new `FindObjectOfType` / scene-only singletons without waiver
- [ ] Perf: no per-frame alloc hot path without note

## Sprint / milestone roadmap

| Milestone | Outcome | Primary artifacts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UCA-M0 | Spec + skeleton + cross-tool artifacts | This page, Linear project, git roadmap |
| UCA-M1 | Core `SKILL.md`  • presentation-boundary doctrine | `SKILL.md`, `references/presentation-boundary.md` |
| UCA-M2 | Reference pack | asmdefs, SO, mono-anti-patterns, perf, testing |
| UCA-M3 | Aegis playbooks | UnityAdapter map, Editor vs runtime, C2 UI notes |
| UCA-M4 | Self-tests + checklists | `checklists/*`, optional CI lint hook |
| UCA-M5 | Dogfood + closeout | Use skill on one Unity PR; AAR; mark skill v1 |

Cadence note: Aegis uses outcome milestones, not cycles (`linear-usage-contract.md` §7). UCA milestones are outcome-keyed; dates on Linear are soft.

## Parallel-agent dispatch plan (when UCA-M1+ starts)

Per `linear-parallel-dispatch-playbook.md`:

| Lane | Work | Surface rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — Doctrine | `SKILL.md` core + ADR-018/010 operationalization | `skills/unity-csharp-architect/SKILL.md`, `references/presentation-boundary.md`, `headless-command-ui.md` |
| B — Structure | asmdefs, mono anti-patterns, SO data | `references/asmdefs*`, `mono*`, `scriptable*` |
| C — Aegis map | Repo path map + Editor/runtime split | `references/aegis-unity-map.md`, `editor-vs-runtime.md` |
| D — Gates | Finish checklists + review prompts | `checklists/*` |

Lanes A–D are file-disjoint. No agent touches CRITICAL hubs or sim core for this program unless a separate product issue requires it.

## Related existing assets

- ADR-010 / ADR-007 / ADR-001 presentation boundary (Git ADR-018 = datalink, not presentation)
- ADR-010 Headless-First / Command-Driven UI
- ADR-007 C2 Map Presentation
- Unity UI Maturity Plan
- Platform Design Assistant skill pack (different skill family — catalog/PDA, not architecture)
- `production/agentic/linear-parallel-dispatch-playbook.md`
- `production/agentic/linear-usage-contract.md`

## Acceptance for program Done (UCA-M5) — met 2026-08-11

1. Skill directory merged to `main` (M0–M4) + dogfood PR #477
2. Agents open skill on Unity/C# architecture tasks (`SKILL.md` triggers + finish checklist)
3. Real Unity PR dogfooded with checklist evidence: PR #477 (`MapPictureBridge` + pr-finish PASS)
4. This page Complete; Linear project Unity C# Architect Skill → Completed; epic DRG-124 Done
5. Presentation ADR citation = ADR-010 / 007 / 001 (not Git ADR-018 datalink) — corrected in M1 doctrine

## Open questions (resolved / superseded 2026-08-12)

1. Skill home: `production/agentic/skills/unity-csharp-architect/` — accepted (v1 landed).
2. CI: soft `rg` remains advisory only (UCA-A3). Hard lint requires a separate product decision issue — not enabled by adoption train.
3. DOTS: still out of v1 — prefer headless ECS in sim core; Unity presentation non-authoritative.

## Decision defaults

1. Path: `production/agentic/skills/unity-csharp-architect/`
2. CI: checklist-first (`pr-finish.md`); soft-ci-rg advisory; no product-floor hard lint without product issue
3. DOTS: reference only — no full DOTS Unity playbook in v1

## Follow-on train — UCA-A (2026-08-12)

Adoption (not a re-land): routing embeds skill + pr-finish; ADR citation hygiene; soft-CI posture; product consumption dogfood.

- Kickoff: `production/agentic/uca-a-adoption-train-2026-08-12.md`

- ADR law (corrected): presentation boundary = ADR-010 §2–3, ADR-007, ADR-001. Git ADR-018 = sensor side-picture / datalink — not presentation.
- Early brainstorm text on this page that said “ADR-018 = presentation” is historical / superseded by UCA-M1 doctrine and this note.

## UCA-A closeout (2026-08-12) — CLOSED

Status: UCA-A0…A5 complete. Linear project UCA Adoption (UCA-A) → Completed. Epic [DRG-135](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-135) Done. Stage remains Release. Skill remains v1 / `1.0.0` (no doctrine change).

pages.title: 🎯 Combat Interaction UX — Proposed Requirements and Vertical Slice
pages.content:
Source: `Game-Requirements/drafts/26-Verification-CI-Gauntlet.md`; `Game-Requirements/requirements/20-Command-And-Control-UI.md`
Req IDs: VER-07
Lifecycle: Draft — owner acceptance pending
Linear: [DRG-201](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-201) · [DRG-244](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-244) · [DRG-208](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208) · [DRG-233](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-233)

---

## Four-system delivery contract

- Notion: requirements, slice framing, acceptance gates, and design decisions.
- Linear: milestones, epics, stories, ownership, dependencies, and delivery status.
- GitHub: code, pull-request review, CI evidence, merge history, and release provenance.
- Graphite: atomic branch stacks and pull-request ordering; each layer remains independently reviewable.

### Required traceability

Every Linear implementation story links to this requirements page. Every GitHub pull request names its Linear story, links the relevant Notion requirement, states acceptance criteria and test evidence, and records its Graphite stack position when applicable. On merge, the Linear story records the merged pull request and moves only when its acceptance criteria are verified.

---

## Delivery roadmap

Linear is the execution system of record; this page is the requirements and design source. Each delivery epic and story links back here rather than duplicating its full specification.

- Slice A — Sense and target: Find, Fix, Track, Target; contact-state projection, information quality, authority and ROE, sensor-to-shooter traceability, and a targetability scenario.
- Slice B — Engage and assess: Target, Engage, Assess; event contract, missile/gun/laser rendering, explanation, contact combat card, replay, and accessibility.
- Slice C — Command, learn, adapt: confidence-aware recommendations, after-action review, sensor/EW understanding, damage state, and formation coordination.
- Cross-cutting readiness: performance and declutter budgets, usability scenarios, and kill-chain traceability.
- Slice G - Unity UX/UI rebaseline and acceptance: Slice G - Unity UX/UI Rebaseline and Acceptance extends acceptance across C2 and Mission/Platform Editor surfaces, reusing existing A-C and cross-cutting stories. [DRG-233](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-233) owns delivery; this addition does not close any existing acceptance gate.

---


Delivery status (Linear 2026-09-04): Headless Combat UX stories DRG-206–230 are Done on `main` @ `6f80d226` (#610 docs W1-HUB). Wave 5 leftovers (#600–#603) remain on main. This page stays the requirements SoT. Update 2026-09-30: UI stories proceed under the authorized S122.0–S127 evidence rebaseline. DRG-180/181/182 are Done in live Linear; DRG-183/169/258/197 are In Progress. Owner Play Mode [DRG-208](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208) remains Todo and human-only at Linear-reported integration1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd. It is an acceptance gate for the program. The current roadmap and mandatory QA plan separate delivery status, retained technical evidence and owner acceptance. Proposed VER-07.3–6 strengthens revision provenance under DRG-201/244. Do not treat this page as a second board.


## Slice framing

### Slice A — Sense and target

Find → Fix → Track → Target. A player can trace a contact from detection to targetability, including provenance, confidence, freshness, comms state, classification, authority, and rules-of-engagement constraints.

### Slice B — Engage and assess

Target → Engage → Assess. The existing vertical slice proves a missile, gun, and laser engagement from command through outcome, explanation, accessible symbology, replay, and assessment.

### Slice C — Command, learn, and adapt

Observe → Orient → Decide → Act. The player reviews outcomes, receives clearly non-authoritative recommendations, commands formations within delegated authority, and updates intent using battle-damage assessment.

## Cross-cutting requirement lenses

- Command and control: make authority to observe, recommend, approve, engage, abort, and delegate explicit.
- Sensor-to-shooter: preserve traceability from detection through firing solution to engagement and assessment.
- Rules of engagement and escalation: explain permitted, withheld, and approval-required actions.
- Information quality: distinguish confidence, provenance, freshness, comms loss, and genuine unknowns.
- Mission command and BDA: express intent and constraints, then support retasking, withdrawal, or re-attack from assessed results.

---

Status: Accepted for headless delivery; UI/render in progress under S122–S127, owner acceptance via [DRG-208](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208).
Purpose: Requirements and slice framing. Linear holds story status.
Scope: Cross-domain C2 presentation only. The simulation remains the source of combat facts; the UI renders projections and submits commands through the approved boundary.

---

## Recommended requirement set

### CMB-UI-01 — Combat event grammar [P0]

Every player-visible engagement shall have a consistent lifecycle: intent accepted, authorization or refusal, weapon launch or firing, in-flight or sustained effect where applicable, terminal outcome, and replay correlation. The event payload shall identify shooter, target, weapon family, outcome, and explanation reference.

### CMB-UI-02 — Weapon-family symbology [P0]

The tactical map shall distinguish missile, gun, and laser engagements without depending on color alone. Each family shall have distinct iconography, line behavior, motion treatment, and accessible text or tooltip labels. The same semantics shall appear in the event log and replay.

### CMB-UI-03 — Engagement explanation [P0]

For a selected engagement or blocked order, the player shall be able to see firing solution state, hard constraints, doctrine or policy constraints, sensor/contact confidence, selected weapon, and the actionable reason for refusal.

### CMB-UI-04 — Contact combat card [P0]

A selected contact shall have a presentation distinct from an own-unit panel. It shall show identity confidence, detection provenance and freshness, posture, targetability, associated engagement status, and battle-damage assessment when known.

### CMB-UI-05 — Scale-aware declutter and accessibility [P0]

At operational scale, salvos and gun bursts shall aggregate while selected or replay-inspected engagements remain explorable. Weapon family, affiliation, clearance, and outcome shall use redundant channels: shape, line style, label, and color.

---

## Vertical slice

One deterministic scenario shall show one shooter and one target for each family: missile, gun, and laser. It shall prove command acceptance, permitted and refused engagement states, event ordering, map symbology, impact or miss, event-log correlation, replay determinism, and usable presentation at tactical and operational zoom.

---

## Story sequence

1. Combat event projection contract — headless projection with replay correlation; blocks all UI stories.
2. Missile, gun, and laser renderer — consumes only the event projection; validates the visual vocabulary.
3. Engagement explain surface — connects selected event to constraints and doctrine reasoning.
4. Contact combat card — provides provenance, confidence, targeting state, and BDA.
5. Declutter and accessibility pass — validates three zoom bands and non-color-only recognition.
6. Replay acceptance harness — asserts event-to-render outcomes across the vertical slice.

---

## Acceptance gates

- A user can identify shooter, target, weapon family, and outcome without opening a detail panel.
- A blocked shot states the reason and the next corrective action when one exists.
- Replay emits the same combat event sequence and yields the same presentation state.
- Weapon family and outcome remain distinguishable in a non-color-only mode.
- No presentation code derives combat truth independently from the simulation projection.

---

## Dependencies and boundaries

- Reuse existing sensor and weapon envelope overlays; do not rebuild them.
- Keep the simulation and C2 command contracts headless-first.
- Do not start implementation until this draft is accepted and placed in a newly authorized delivery scope.

---

pages.title: 🚢 SYM-CIV-01 — Custom Civilian-Friendly Gameplay Symbology
pages.content:
Source: `Game-Requirements/drafts/2026-09-05-civilian-gameplay-symbology.md`
Req IDs: SYM-CIV-01
Lifecycle: Draft — canonical home pending owner land decision (owner acceptance pending)
Linear: [DRG-232](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-232)

---

## Traceability

Design requirement: SYM-CIV-01. Delivery: [DRG-232](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-232). Linear owns delivery status; this page owns the draft design and acceptance criteria.

Local draft mirror: `Game-Requirements/drafts/2026-09-05-civilian-gameplay-symbology.md` (uncommitted working copy, not a landed Git source). Linked from REQ-20 and the local Game Requirements index. Paired profile: [SYM-MIL-01](https://app.notion.com/p/3d2f7cb4e4df81bc8028f32673f31e32).

## Requirement — SYM-CIV-01

Project Aegis shall provide an original Civilian-Friendly gameplay symbology profile that lets players without military-symbol training recognize supported unit/contact categories and their displayed state. This is an alternate visual vocabulary over the same tactical picture, not an easier simulation or a change to military/civilian affiliation.

## Scope assumption requiring review

The user's phrase custom civilian symbology is provisionally interpreted as a simplified display profile for all supported units, not only icons for civilian vessels. A clarification question has been sent. If the intended scope is civilian vessel/traffic categories only, revise this requirement before implementation. The requirement is Draft and the Linear item remains Backlog.

## Acceptance criteria

- CIV-AC-01: Map options expose Civilian-Friendly alongside Military Tactical, with a preview and plain-language legend. The chosen profile persists across application restarts; both profiles remain selectable. First-run default is a separate product decision, not changed by this requirement.
- CIV-AC-02: Original, consistent silhouettes/pictograms cover surface vessels, submarines, aircraft/UAS, ground units, and unknown contacts already supported by the scenario. Civilian vessel categories may include merchant, tanker, fishing, passenger, and pleasure craft only when the observer knows that category; otherwise use a generic vessel/unknown contact.
- CIV-AC-03: Affiliation uses redundant shape/badge and text cues as well as color. Civilian category, neutral affiliation, and unknown identity remain distinct; no profile may label an unknown track civilian or non-threatening without projected evidence.
- CIV-AC-04: Each civilian-friendly symbol maps to the same semantic entity/domain/affiliation/status as its military-profile equivalent. Unknown/stale/lost/degraded information remains explicit; heading is shown only when known. No recognizable silhouette may reveal an unclassified enemy platform.
- CIV-AC-05: Switching profiles during paused or running gameplay preserves camera, selected entity, OOB/detail synchronization, command availability, orders, and replay outcomes. Selection, pending commands, refusals, and assessment feedback remain legible in either profile.
- CIV-AC-06: A documented visual atlas, asset manifest, and style guide specify sizes, contrast, stroke weights, zoom/declutter behavior, and generic fallbacks. User-importable symbol packs are not required by this item.
- CIV-AC-07: At the supported minimum viewport and 100%/150% UI scale, UAT participants unfamiliar with NTDS correctly identify at least 9 of 10 predeclared category/affiliation/state examples using the legend, with zero hostile-versus-friendly/neutral inversions. Record sample size, fixtures, answers, and screenshots; missing evidence is not a pass.
- CIV-AC-08: Headless profile-parity/fallback tests and Unity mouse/keyboard UAT show all declared categories render without missing icons, selection drift, hidden-information leaks, or altered command behavior.

## Reference and originality

- [CMO official UI addendum — military and stylized symbol choices](https://command.matrixgames.com/?page_id=2697) provides precedent for player-selectable profiles.
- The artwork and style guide are original Project Aegis gameplay assets. No assertion of MIL-STD-2525/APP-6 compliance is made for the civilian-friendly glyphs.

## Boundaries and delivery

Status: Draft requirement, recorded 2026-09-05 at the user's request. Implementation is not started or scheduled. This addition does not mark existing map symbology complete or reopen a release milestone.

Related requirements: REQ-20 / CMD-06 (map picture), CMD-07 (selection sync), CMD-12 (accessibility), CMD-13 (APP-6/LOD), CMD-28 (map options), CMD-29 (contact knowledge), and CMD-30 (tactical overlays).

Architecture: presentation reads existing observer-side projections and preserves ADR-010 §§2–3, ADR-007, and ADR-001. Changing a symbol profile must not change simulation state, orders, ROE, ownership, visibility, contact knowledge, or replay hashes. Missing or uncertain information must remain missing or uncertain.

Verification: headless mapping/semantic tests first, then Unity Game view UAT and retained screenshots. Verify selection and contact provenance in both profiles, including unknown, stale/lost, and degraded-comms tracks.

pages.title: 🎖️ SYM-MIL-01 — Military Tactical Symbology (NTDS / APP-6 / MIL-STD-2525)
pages.content:
Source: `Game-Requirements/drafts/2026-09-05-military-tactical-symbology.md`
Req IDs: SYM-MIL-01
Lifecycle: Draft — canonical home pending owner land decision (owner acceptance pending)
Linear: [DRG-231](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-231) · [DRG-232](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-232)

---

## Traceability

Design requirement: SYM-MIL-01. Delivery: [DRG-231](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-231). Linear owns delivery status; this page owns the draft design and acceptance criteria.

Local draft mirror: `Game-Requirements/drafts/2026-09-05-military-tactical-symbology.md` (uncommitted working copy, not a landed Git source). Linked from REQ-20 and the local Game Requirements index. Paired profile: [SYM-CIV-01](https://app.notion.com/p/3d2f7cb4e4df81a68f32f174cabcd48d).

## Requirement — SYM-MIL-01

Project Aegis shall provide a selectable Military Tactical symbology profile for U.S. Navy surface ships and the other supported unit/contact domains. The profile shall use documented NTDS naval display conventions and an explicitly versioned mapping to NATO APP-6 and U.S. MIL-STD-2525, informed by the CMANO/CMO tactical-display reference experience.

## Standards and reference interpretation

CMO's official UI addendum names its military symbol option NTDS + NATO APP-6, alongside a Stylized option. MIL-STD-2525 is the U.S. joint military symbology standard; APP-6 is the NATO standard family. These names must not be treated as interchangeable or as evidence that CMO implements every provision of MIL-STD-2525.

The supplied NTIS link identifies the 2007 Common Navy Warfighting Display Symbology Implementation Guide (ADA484484), not the standard itself. Its abstract describes maritime implementation of MIL-STD-2525 and additional Navy modifiers from NTDS/SSDS. Use this as supporting naval guidance; document deviations from the selected standard.

DLA lists MIL-STD-2525 Revision E Change 1, dated 2025-03-02. Proposed implementation baseline: that revision for the U.S. mapping; the exact APP-6 edition and NTDS subset must be pinned in the mapping specification before artwork implementation. This is a documented subset requirement, not a claim of formal standards certification.

## Acceptance criteria

- MIL-AC-01: Map options expose a clearly named Military Tactical profile and an in-game legend identifying its selected standards editions and any custom deviations.
- MIL-AC-02: A versioned symbol mapping manifest records semantic key, domain, affiliation, known platform category, frame/icon/modifiers, source edition or guide section, and fallback for every supported symbol. Missing entries use a documented generic unknown symbol.
- MIL-AC-03: The naval test atlas covers at least carrier, destroyer, cruiser, frigate, amphibious, support/auxiliary, and unknown surface vessel categories when known to the observer. Any category unsupported by the chosen standard has an explicit generic fallback; symbols must not invent class-level identification.
- MIL-AC-04: Friendly, hostile, neutral, and unknown tracks are distinguishable by shape/frame and text/legend, not color alone. A U.S. Navy platform's nationality does not automatically make it friendly; displayed affiliation follows the observer's projected knowledge.
- MIL-AC-05: Domain, affiliation, heading when known, selection, and observed contact quality/status remain readable at supported zoom/UI scales. Selection and command/outcome overlays must not overwrite or contradict symbol identity. Unobserved damage and platform type stay undisclosed.
- MIL-AC-06: Map, OOB, and detail views identify the same selected entity, including contact-to-unit selection transitions. Switching to/from the civilian profile preserves selection, camera position, simulation time, and active orders.
- MIL-AC-07: Headless mapping/unknown-fallback tests plus a Unity visual atlas review prove conformance to the declared subset and document any deviations. Asset provenance is retained; CMANO/CMO are behavior references, not a source of copied proprietary artwork.

## Sources

- [CMO official UI addendum — Map Symbols](https://command.matrixgames.com/?page_id=2697)
- [DLA official MIL-STD-2525 record](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsDocDetails.aspx?ident_number=114934)
- [NTIS / Naval Surface Warfare Center naval symbology guide, ADA484484](https://ntrl.ntis.gov/NTRL/dashboard/searchResults/titleDetail/ADA484484.xhtml)
- [User-supplied NTDS discussion — contextual only, not a normative standard](https://forum.finescale.com/t/navy-command-symbols/132729)

## Boundaries and delivery

Status: Draft requirement, recorded 2026-09-05 at the user's request. Implementation is not started or scheduled. This addition does not mark existing map symbology complete or reopen a release milestone.

Related requirements: REQ-20 / CMD-06 (map picture), CMD-07 (selection sync), CMD-12 (accessibility), CMD-13 (APP-6/LOD), CMD-28 (map options), CMD-29 (contact knowledge), and CMD-30 (tactical overlays).

Architecture: presentation reads existing observer-side projections and preserves ADR-010 §§2–3, ADR-007, and ADR-001. Changing a symbol profile must not change simulation state, orders, ROE, ownership, visibility, contact knowledge, or replay hashes. Missing or uncertain information must remain missing or uncertain.

Verification: headless mapping/semantic tests first, then Unity Game view UAT and retained screenshots. Verify selection and contact provenance in both profiles, including unknown, stale/lost, and degraded-comms tracks.

pages.content:

Additional Sources: `2026-08-17-cmd-38-kinematic-map-picture-draft.md`, `2026-08-17-cmd-39-attention-toast-clock-interrupt-draft.md`

---

## Delivery records

[DRG-233: Slice G epic](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-233)

- [DRG-234: G1 requirement and evidence baseline](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-234)
- [DRG-235: G2 integrated C2 workflow acceptance](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-235)
- [DRG-236: G3 Mission and Platform Editor acceptance](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-236)

G2 and G3 depend on G1. These links are the execution records; consult Linear for current status.

## Purpose and scope

Establish a truthful Unity UX/UI baseline across C2, Mission Editor and Platform Editor, then close verified presentation gaps through existing delivery owners. The owner authorized creating this slice on 2026-09-08. This is a planning and acceptance contract, not a completed implementation or visual signoff.

## Sources and ownership

- Combat Interaction UX — Proposed Requirements and Vertical Slice supplies the combat requirements.
- Main Game Window — Proposed C2 UI Requirements (CMD-16…CMD-28) is a proposed delta to repository requirement 20.
- Unity UI Maturity Plan — Project Aegis is historical context; its implementation claims require revalidation.
- Repository plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-08-slice-g-unity-ux-ui.md`. This file is local and uncommitted at creation; no published Git URL is asserted.
- Canonical requirement amendments belong in repository requirements 11, 20 and 21. Linear owns delivery status. This page owns the Slice G scope and acceptance contract.
- Audit categories D/E/F are document defects, traceability, and tooling findings, respectively. They are not verified delivery slice definitions. Existing delivery Slices A-C retain their identities.

## G1: Requirement and evidence baseline

Create a requirement-to-criterion-to-surface-to-projection/command-to-test-to-scenario-to-evidence mapping. Each row records commit plus local delta, Linear owner, evidence class and owner acceptance separately.

Reassess audit B-10, the presentation portions of B-15, D-10 and D-15. Reconcile CMD-31 through CMD-39 against actual records. Proposed CMD-40 through CMD-43 and pending CMD-38/39 decisions must not be presented as approved.

Acceptance: every reviewed row has evidence or an explicit missing-evidence reason; no headless-only row is described as visually accepted. Reuse [DRG-187](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-187) and [DRG-188](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-188).

## G2: Integrated C2 workflow acceptance

Validate map/OOB/detail selection, live/history boundaries, command availability and refusal, approval-required state, alerting, stale/unknown/comms-loss states, keyboard access and density. Reuse existing A-C implementation stories and [DRG-170](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-170), [DRG-177](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-177) and [DRG-205](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-205).

Acceptance: reproducible success and degraded-state scenarios, reachable controls at supported view sizes and scale extremes, and separate callback versus pointer/keyboard evidence. Positive group/BDA and live coverage gaps remain owned by [DRG-185](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-185), [DRG-175](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-175) and [DRG-192](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-192).

## G3: Mission and Platform Editor acceptance

Validate library/load, authoring navigation, map selection, validation, save/export, return-to-play, catalog browse/import preview and proposal feedback. Exercise invalid/empty/dirty states and recovery. Preserve Excel-primary Platform Editor authoring and human production write approval.

Acceptance: each critical workflow has a reproducible success and recovery path; actual screenshots and linked findings appear in an HTML review under `docs/superpowers/reviews/`.

## Baseline and limitations

The repository is at `37e6ba6d` with existing uncommitted Slice C layout, metadata and evidence changes. The September 8 Slice C package reports technical Play Mode smoke PASS, six Unity tests, 3,216 headless tests, 24 proxy tests and six canonical replay goldens. Owner acceptance remains pending. These are prior recorded results, not fresh measurements from this page.

The smoke scene has no configured task group or authored live coverage geometry. Coverage screenshots are a labeled presentation fixture. A complete positive live group/BDA workflow is not proven by that package.

Live Linear DRG-185 still reads Backlog. No existing delivery issue is automatically closed by this plan.

## Dependencies and verification

G1 and traceability reconciliation can proceed while [DRG-197](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-197) restores GitNexus. Fresh path-specific impact is required before symbol edits. G2 and G3 follow G1 and may run in isolated worktrees with one local Editor coordinator.

Reuse [DRG-176](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-176) and [DRG-26](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-26) for measured frame/bind budgets. Headless bind timing is not Unity frame-time evidence.

Run the required build, full suite, proxy and replay checks; preserve the observed baseline, v2 hash `17144800277401907079`, zero-touch DelegationBridge and existing CatalogWriteGate paths. Apply the unity-csharp-architect finish checklist.

Presentation follows ADR-010 sections 2-3, ADR-007 and ADR-001; editor authoring also follows ADR-011/017. Never use Git ADR-018 as the presentation boundary. No Unity serialized YAML hand-edits.

## Exit gate

- Evidence rows are verified or explicitly dispositioned by the owner.
- Requirement amendments, issue ownership and evidence links agree.
- Headless, Editor, performance and owner acceptance results are separately reported.
- No new high-severity usability defect remains without owner-approved disposition.
- Technical gates pass and protected boundaries are preserved.
- Owner explicitly accepts the scoped UX/UI package. Planning authorization and automated test passes do not constitute visual signoff.

## Project rules

### Unity MCP and CLI (added 2026-09-27 by drg amtd)

Any agent working on a story that touches Unity (scenes, prefabs, UXML/USS, UI Toolkit panels, Console, Game View visuals, Editor tooling) must consider the Unity MCP and the Unity CLI, and state in the kickoff and in the PR whether they were used.

- Stack: Ivan Murzak Unity-MCP (`com.ivanmurzak.unity.mcp`, MCP server `ai-game-developer` at `http://localhost:8080`) and `npx unity-mcp-cli@`. Do not add CoplayDev MCP for Unity (ADR-027, PR #679).
- Probe first: `curl` `http://localhost:8080` or `unity-mcp-cli status ./unity/ProjectAegis`. If it's up, follow the Unity-MCP loop in `AGENTS.md` (mutate, save scene/prefab, Play Mode if visual, `console-get-logs` + Game View screenshot) and attach the evidence to the PR. If it's down (cloud VMs have no Editor), stay headless and write "Unity MCP: unavailable, headless only" in the PR.
- Verification authority: headless `dotnet test` and Buildkite stay the gate. MCP/CLI evidence supplements them and never replaces them.
- Surface bound: MCP/CLI writes (scenes, prefabs, assets, UXML) stay inside the stamped Surface.
- Hard nos apply to MCP too: never mutate DelegationBridge via `script-execute` or reflection. No SimulationSession, CatalogWriteGate, or overlay-host edits through the Editor.
- Play Mode stays human: agent MCP screenshots or Play Mode runs never count as the owner Play Mode sign-off (DRG-208).
- Config safety: do not run bare `setup-mcp`, because it clobbers `mcp.json`. Use the committed config plus `tools/pin-unity-mcp-8080`.
- Pure headless sim/delegation stories skip this rule.

## Decision boundary

No owner acceptance at the target revision was found in the inspected records. DRG-208 is Todo. Its current explicit blockers are DRG-243, DRG-183, DRG-239 and DRG-244. This index organizes evidence; it does not execute the owner walk, close those blockers, or grant a waiver.

The September 8 Slice C package supports scoped technical Editor smoke. It explicitly leaves owner acceptance pending and does not prove the positive live group Hold → BDA → Withdraw workflow. Slice B's September 5 package supports headless implementation and offline compilation, with outstanding visual acceptance. Symbology records are draft requirements.

Jev review: Requested but not completed. Located the Windows project `.env` and confirmed the OpenRouter key variable is present without exposing its value. Prepared a nine-question structured review using [TypeSafe Jev 1.13](https://openrouter.ai/typesafe/jev-1.13) and the [OpenRouter Decisions API](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/alphadecisions/submit-a-decisions-questions-and-answers-request). Automatic approval review rejected execution because the payload would disclose a summary of private repository and Notion evidence to OpenRouter. No authenticated inference request was executed and no Jev recommendation is claimed. Awaiting explicit user approval for that evidence-summary disclosure.

## Required evidence-link checklist

Checked boxes mean the source link was located and read, not that the corresponding product behavior is accepted.

## How to interpret the evidence

| Class | What it means here |
| --- | --- |
| Source / requirement | A document, implementation report or requirement was read. Presence does not prove execution. |
| Headless-tested — historical report | The dated delivery package reports .NET tests, smoke proxy or replay results. Those commands were not rerun for this index. |

| Owner-accepted | Requires an explicit human decision naming revision, local delta, scope, observations and limitations. No target-revision acceptance was found. |
| Unverified | No sufficient evidence found in the inspected records; specify the missing proof and delivery issue. |

Reading an evidence file at `da6c5c64d0181238931002de4a3f6cf763137c88` verifies its contents at that revision. It does not move the original run date or execution revision forward. Reported screenshots are linked for audit; their pixels were not independently inspected during this task. No Unity session, test suite, frame capture or scenario was executed for this index.

No missing row is a pass. An owner disposition must name its scope, rationale, risk and follow-up. Recording a gap here does not waive a blocker.

## Owner re-signoff capture sheet

Execution is human-only. Use Unity 6000.3.22f1, DelegationSmoke and the checklist at the current DRG-208 target [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/unity/ProjectAegis/PLAYMODE-SMOKE.md). Preserve historical da6c5c64 package links above as historical evidence. Agents must not start Unity for this walk, perform the signoff, relaunch DRAW/Cesium or start Launch.

Record this header with the observations: UTC timestamp; owner; full HEAD; branch; local delta/cleanliness; plugin state; Unity version; scene and policy; Game View resolution and UI scale; screenshot/log locations. If the required revision changes, explicitly rebaseline before attributing any result to it.

- [ ] Startup: no top-bar NRE; ACK → RESUME and clock controls behave as expected.
- [ ] Overlays: selected unit sensor/weapon rings, circular on non-square view; expected ENVELOPES / DATALINKS counts and datalink state.
- [ ] Map ↔ OOB ↔ detail selection, including contact evidence and own-unit distinction.

- [ ] Slice C command-review / coordination surfaces if visible; record exactly what was exercised and any missing/partial surface.
- [ ] Kill-chain overlay if visible; absence alone is not a fail under DRG-208.
- [ ] Tick/no-hitch and Console/bridge observations; distinguish observation from profiling.
- [ ] Separate added #666/#669/#667 chrome observations mentioned by the latest DRG-208 comment; no acceptance inferred from merge.

- [ ] Human acceptance statement posted to DRG-208, including unverified scope and any explicit dispositions.

## Open review questions for Jev and the owner

These are review prompts, not completed decisions or Jev recommendations.

1. Confirm the evidence boundary: retain historical technical passes as scoped evidence while requiring a new human decision at the target SHA.
2. Recommend a disposition for the Slice B status conflict. Current Todo versus DRG-240's historical In Review claim should not be silently normalized.
3. Confirm DRG-239 remains the enabling work for positive live group/coverage proof, without treating headless success or fixture screenshots as closure.
4. Confirm symbology stays “requirements only / not ready” until the respective scope and mapping decisions and delivery evidence exist.
5. Decide whether any scoped interim acceptance is appropriate under the S123/S127 owner-walk plan. Any exception must be explicit and must not silently remove current blockers.
6. Reconcile the target's PR-label inconsistency using Git evidence if needed; preserve the exact SHA and do not interpret tracker labels as visual proof.

Jev response: Pending explicit approval to send the private evidence summary to OpenRouter following automatic approval review rejection. Prepared questions cover historical evidence, Slice B status conflict, live group/coverage gaps, symbology readiness, missing G1 baseline, interim acceptance, revision labels, DRG-208 closure and index publication. Any returned recommendation will be advisory, not independent artifact verification or human acceptance. Owner decisions: Pending. Index publication: Documentation only; no issue state or blocker relation is changed.

Requirements, backlog and roadmap reconciliation — 2026-09-30

DRG-208 remains Todo and blocked by DRG-243/183/239/244. DRG-183/169/258/197 are In Progress in the fresh board; the older table above records historical status. DRG-180/181/182 are Done as delivery states, not visual acceptance. Live-group/coverage and symbology residuals remain open.

New evidence rows under DRG-201 / proposed VER-07.3–6 must identify requirement/criterion, executed revision and dirty-input identity, scenario/seed/catalog/policy, evidence kind, harness/command, artifact location/hash, result and timestamp. Keep measured test counts separate from the standing floor. Human acceptance separately names person, date, revision and scoped decision; a technical pass cannot supply it. pages.title: ⚖️ Jev AI — in-game decisioning research (2026-09-22)
pages.content:
## Status

User AC 2026-09-22 CT — REQ accepted. Surface: `surface/c2-presentation` (CMANO). Still no impl / no VS children until land `#673→#675→#672` clears. Owner research: Jev router. Does not interrupt land stack or DRG-167.

## Problem / opportunity

Aegis needs fast, calibrated in-game decisioning (route / prioritize / gate / recommend) that is:

- Too fuzzy for hard-coded `if` trees alone (ROE edge cases, attention triage, weapon-family tradeoffs under incomplete contact data).
- Too small / too frequent for a frontier LLM chat round-trip on every player glance or chrome refresh.
- Must stay advisory — never write DecisionLog / sim, never auto-fire, never bypass ADR-010 command façade.

TypeSafe Jev (System One Decision API) returns typed Choice, Score, or Noul answers with probabilities in one round trip. That fits player-assist chrome, attention scoring, ROE gates, and recommendation UI — not replacing the existing in-sim trait-weighted `DecisionPipeline` (stochastic) that runs on agents every tick.

Separation of concerns:

| Layer | Role |
| --- | --- |
| In-sim `DecisionPipeline` | Agent tick behavior (stochastic, trait-weighted) — unchanged |
| Jev in-game (this REQ) | Player-assist / attention / ROE gates / recommendation chrome |
| `/workspace/jev` shadow hooks | Out-of-band sprint dispatch router for agents — not product |

## References

- Linear research ticket: [DRG-318](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-318/research-jev-ai-in-game-decisioning-choice-score-noul-req-draft)
- Jev Decision API: [https://jevtypesafeai.com/docs](https://jevtypesafeai.com/docs)
- Jev product overview: [https://www.jevtypesafeai.com/](https://www.jevtypesafeai.com/)
- Cloudflare `typesafe/jev` model docs: [https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai/models/typesafe/jev/](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai/models/typesafe/jev/)
- Existing agent decision pipeline: Agent decision pipeline — developer guide
- Agentic combat capabilities: Agentic Combat Capabilities — Proposed Requirements
- Related Linear (recommendation UI Done): [DRG-172](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-172) — threat/weapon recommendation, never fire
- Related: [DRG-185](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-185), [DRG-167](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-167)
- Privacy precedent: DRG-244 — Play Mode re-signoff evidence index (current target1902dc12; historical evidence retained) (Jev review blocked without user ACK to send private evidence to OpenRouter)
- ADR-010 command façade: UI never writes DecisionLog/sim; recommendations only; Accept → façade enqueue

### Jev API facts (pinned for this REQ)

- `POST decide` with `state` + `questions` map
- Types: Choice (≤255 criteria map), Score (2–10 ordered levels), Noul (yes/no probability)
- Pin `jev-1.13.x` in production; current openrouter path: `typesafe/jev-1.13` via Decisions alpha
- Cost \~\$0.42 / 1M input tokens — trim state aggressively
- Ready-made agent/risk patterns useful analogy for tool gates / command proposals (player-facing propose only)

## Question inventory

Concrete question IDs for a future `questions` map. Criteria sketches are REQ drafts — CMANO may rename before Surface.

| Question ID | Jev type | Criteria / levels (sketch) | Player-facing use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `weapon_family_recommend` | Choice | `missile` / `gun` / `laser` / `hold` / `withdraw` / `evasive` (≤255; keep ≤8) | Glue to DRG-172 recommendation chrome; never fire |
| `threat_urgency` | Score (4–5) | `calm` → `elevated` → `urgent` → `critical` (+ optional `imminent`) | Contact / track chrome urgency; attention boost |
| `suggest_ok_under_roe` | Noul | P(yes) that showing a suggested engage/order card is ROE-compliant for this contact | Gate before "suggested order" card; low → escalate / hide |
| `contact_class_assist` | Choice | `friendly` / `hostile` / `unknown` / `civilian` / `neutral` | Assist classification UI; player confirms |
| `attention_priority` | Score (5) | `ignore` → `low` → `watch` → `focus` → `immediate` | Which unit/contact needs player eyes |
| `order_proposal_risk` | Choice or Noul | Choice: `allow` / `confirm` / `block` — or Noul escalate-to-confirm | Player-facing propose only; Accept still goes through command façade |
| `skill_unavailable_disclosure` | Noul | P(yes) that UI must show unavailable/offline chrome for this skill path | Force disclosure when model/skill down |
| `engage_range_posture` | Choice | `close` / `standoff` / `hold_range` / `break_contact` | Slice C command-learn-adapt posture hint (advisory) |
| `ew_vs_kinetic_bias` | Score (3–4) | `prefer_ew` → `balanced` → `prefer_kinetic` (+ `hold`) | Combat UX soft bias when both options exist |
| `task_group_focus` | Choice | Task-group / unit IDs in current projection (dynamic criteria ≤255) | C2 attention: which TG merits player camera / panel |
| `wra_exhaustion_warn` | Noul | P(yes) that WRA remaining warrants a soft warn before recommend | Chrome warn; does not mute recommendation |

## State payload sketch

Source of truth: projections / player-visible models only. Trim for cost. Never send full scenario files, DecisionLog dumps, or repo paths to hosted API without explicit user ACK.

```json
{
  "schema": "aegis.jev.state.v0",
  "unitId": "u-…",
  "contactId": "c-…",
  "taskGroupId": "tg-…",
  "roe": {
    "weaponsFree": false,
    "weaponsTight": true,
    "holdFire": false,
    "excludeCivilian": true
  },
  "wraRemaining": { "missile": 2, "gun": 140, "laser": 1 },
  "contact": {
    "classHint": "unknown",
    "rangeNm": 18.4,
    "bearingDeg": 112,
    "closing": true,
    "iff": "unknown"
  },
  "ownship": {
    "posture": "patrol",
    "damageState": "nominal",
    "sensorsUp": true
  },
  "playerInfoModel": {
    "selectedUnitId": "u-…",
    "cameraFocusId": null
  },
  "personalityEditPolicy": "read_only_assist",
  "skillAvailability": {
    "jevDecide": true,
    "lastOkAt": "2026-09-22T13:50:00-05:00"
  }
}
```

Forbidden in hosted payload (without ACK): scenario XML/JSON dumps, DecisionLog / sim internals, absolute repo paths, secrets, full doctrine text corpora, private Notion/git evidence.

## Confidence / escalation policy

Draft thresholds (calibrate after VS1 telemetry; pin model `jev-1.13.x` so thresholds stay meaningful):

| Signal | Threshold (draft) | UI behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Noul P(yes) | `< 0.55` | Escalate / hide auto-suggest; require explicit player path |
| Choice confidence (top) | `< 0.60` | Show top-2–3 alternatives; never single-path chrome |
| Score at max urgency | any | Boost attention chrome; still no auto-engage |
| Any engage-adjacent suggest | low conf or ROE Noul low | Never show engage suggestion as default Accept |
| Model / skill unavailable | n/a | Fail-closed for engage suggestions; disclosure chrome |

Hard rule: never engage (or enqueue fire) on low confidence. Recommendation ≠ authorization ≠ automatic engagement (DRG-172 spirit).

## Offline / unavailable fallback

When Jev/OpenRouter path is down or `skillAvailability.jevDecide = false`:

1. UI chrome: persistent "assist unavailable" disclosure (driven in part by `skill_unavailable_disclosure`).
2. Cached last-safe recommend: optional stale badge; age out quickly; never upgrade a stale recommend into Accept-default.
3. Disable auto-suggest for engage / order cards; keep manual C2 paths.
4. Log locally (box / client telemetry) — do not ship private dumps off-box to diagnose without ACK.
5. Fail-closed for engage suggestions; fail-soft for attention Score (fall back to heuristic sort).

## Privacy boundary

| May leave the box (product path) | Requires user ACK |
| --- | --- |
| Trimmed projection state sketch above | Full scenario / mission files |
| Anonymous aggregate telemetry of question IDs + conf bands | DecisionLog dumps, repo paths, private Notion/git |
| Public docs / synthetic fixtures | Real customer / classified Aegis evidence to OpenRouter |

Prior precedent: Jev Play Mode evidence review was blocked without user ACK — reuse that boundary for in-game product paths.

Out-of-band `/workspace/jev` shadow hooks for sprint dispatch are a separate meta-router; they are not this in-game product surface.

## Non-goals

- Replacing tick `DecisionPipeline` on every agent every tick with Jev
- Frontier LLM chat for every chrome refresh
- Auto-fire / auto-engage / silent world mutation
- UI writing DecisionLog or sim (violates ADR-010)
- Bypassing ROE / authority with "the model said so"
- Floating `latest` model tag for calibrated thresholds
- Shipping private Aegis dumps to OpenRouter without explicit user ACK
- Touching product C#/Unity or PRs `#673` / `#675` / `#672` in this research ticket
- Implementing cloud agents / Play Mode acceptance as part of DRG-318

## Vertical slices (exactly 3)

### VS1 — Player attention Score + disclosure chrome (lowest risk)

- Questions: `attention_priority`, `skill_unavailable_disclosure`
- Chrome only: highlight / sort units needing eyes; show unavailable disclosure
- No order cards, no weapon recommend, no façade enqueue
- Success: player can tell when assist is offline; attention sort feels sane on fixtures

### VS2 — Threat urgency Score + weapon family Choice → DRG-172 UI (still never fire)

- Questions: `threat_urgency`, `weapon_family_recommend` (+ optional `wra_exhaustion_warn`)
- Glue into existing DRG-172 recommendation UI; advisory labels only
- Never fire; never enqueue without explicit future Accept path (VS3)
- Success: recommend chrome updates with conf + alternatives when low conf

### VS3 — ROE Noul gate before "suggested order" card

- Questions: `suggest_ok_under_roe`, `order_proposal_risk`
- Show suggested-order card only when ROE Noul clears; Accept → command façade enqueue only (ADR-010)
- Low Noul / high risk → confirm or block; offline → no card
- Success: no Accept path exists that skips façade; fail-closed offline

## Surface note (CMANO stamp 2026-09-22)

Confirmed label: `surface/c2-presentation` (advisory chrome only).

### Consume / glue (existing)

- `AdviceBridge` / `AdviceModels` / `AdviceSkillService` (CommandReview)
- `EngageExplainProjection` + `EngageExplainPanelHost`
- `CommandReviewView` / `CommandReviewSection` / `CommandReviewTimeline` / `CommandReviewDashboard`
- Optional VS1: `C2TopBarPanelHost`
- Accept enqueue only via `CoordinationCommandBridge` façade (no new write path)

### New (expected)

- NEW headless Presentation Jev binder (AttentionScore / ThreatUrgency / RoeNoul disclosure) + tests — Dlz/Wra binder pattern
- NEW thin disclosure chrome UXML/USS on advisory card (not map overlay hosts)

### Gated / secondary

- `PendingApprovalPanelHost` — VS3 only after #675 lands; do not open until assisted-confirm Surface free

### Hard exclusions

- MapPlaceholderPanelHost, GlobeMapProductHost
- DelegationBridge Tick/hotpath; CatalogWriteGate; SimulationSession; CMD-31/32/34
- Silent ReplayGolden re-bless; replace tick `DecisionPipeline`
- Land-stack Surfaces `#672/#673/#675`; DRG-167 battle-graphics
- Private Aegis dumps to OpenRouter without explicit user ACK

Still REQ-level until land stack + user AC — no impl children yet.

## Open questions (remaining after Surface stamp)

1. Confirm Surface assignment — done: `surface/c2-presentation`.
2. Approve question ID naming + Choice criteria vocab (esp. `weapon_family_recommend` vs doctrine terms).
3. Lock confidence thresholds or require a calibration fixture set first.
4. Confirm Accept on VS3 = `CoordinationCommandBridge` only (CMANO stamped façade path).
5. Is dynamic Choice criteria from live task-group IDs (`task_group_focus`) allowed, or must criteria be static enums?
6. Telemetry retention for conf bands — local only vs aggregated product analytics?
7. Relationship to Slice C: does `engage_range_posture` ship in VS2 or wait?
8. Confirm production pin `jev-1.13.x` / OpenRouter `typesafe/jev-1.13` for future impl.
9. User AC on this draft — accepted 2026-09-22 CT. Open VS1 child only after land `#673→#675→#672`.
